Existing haptic displays commonly encode haptic intensity through the deformation amplitude of individual haptic pixels. Although amplitude-modulated (AM) approaches have enabled compact haptic pixels, independently controlling the deformation amplitude of a large number of pixels can require increasingly complex and bulky driving systems, posing challenges for scaling toward high-density, large-area wearable displays. To address this scaling challenge, we investigate an FM

sections.text:
We present a frequency-modulated (FM) haptic display based on piezoelectric vibrating actuators. Existing haptic displays commonly encode haptic intensity through the deformation amplitude of individual haptic pixels.

Although amplitude-modulated (AM) approaches have enabled compact haptic pixels, independently controlling the deformation amplitude of a large number of pixels can require increasingly complex and bulky driving systems, posing challenges for scaling toward high-density, large-area wearable displays.

To address this scaling challenge, we investigate an FM design principle in which haptic intensity is encoded through vibration frequency.

We further develop a \textit{Shared-Source Frequency Modulation} (SSFM) structure in which multiple haptic pixels are powered by a common power amplifier while their vibration spectrum are controlled individually, reducing the need for independent high-power amplification at each pixel.

A proof-of-concept piezoelectric haptic display was built and evaluated on rendering spatial and temporal haptic patterns through volunteer tests. The results show that participants reliably distinguished spatial and temporal patterns encoded using FM principles within the investigated operating range.

These findings demonstrate the feasibility of FM-based distributed haptic rendering and suggest a potential pathway toward more compact driving architectures for future high-density, large-area wearable haptic displays.

summary.en: Individually controlling deformation amplitude across many haptic pixels can require bulky, complex drive electronics. This study investigates encoding haptic intensity through vibration frequency and develops Shared-Source Frequency Modulation (SSFM), where multiple piezoelectric pixels share a power amplifier while their spectra are controlled individually. A proof-of-concept display renders spatial and temporal patterns in volunteer tests. Participants reliably distinguished frequency-modulated patterns within the investigated operating range. The results support feasibility of distributed FM haptic rendering and suggest a possible path toward compact, scalable displays, but do not demonstrate a finished large-area wearable product.
summary.zh: 高密度可穿戴触觉显示若逐个像素调节振幅，驱动系统可能变得复杂笨重。论文研究以振动频率而非形变振幅编码触觉强度，并提出共享功放、各像素单独控制频谱的SSFM结构。作者制作压电触觉显示原型，通过志愿者测试呈现空间和时间模式。测试参与者能够在研究所考察的工作范围内可靠区分频率调制编码的模式。研究由此支持分布式频率调制触觉呈现的可行性，但并未证明已实现大面积高密度可穿戴产品。

items.title: Frequency-Modulated Piezoelectric Haptic Display

items.intro: arXiv:2609.30873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A series elastic actuator has a single torque port and pays for it twice: the geared motor must swing its own reflected inertia through the spring, so the amplitude it delivers collapses as $\omega^{-2}$ in the command frequency $\omega$ once it saturates, while commands below the transmission's breakaway friction never arrive at all. This letter opens a second torque port on the load side, placing a frameless direct-drive micro motor in parallel

sections.text:
A series elastic actuator has a single torque port and pays for it twice: the geared motor must swing its own reflected inertia through the spring, so the amplitude it delivers collapses as $\omega^{-2}$ in the command frequency $\omega$ once it saturates, while commands below the transmission's breakaway friction never arrive at all.

This letter opens a second torque port on the load side, placing a frameless direct-drive micro motor in parallel with a fixed-stiffness spring -- a parallel-integrated SEA, or Pi-SEA, whose delivered torque is read from spring deflection and micro current without a sensor -- and dividing the commanded torque between the two channels by time scale rather than by filter design.

The micro torque loop is the fast subsystem, which makes the closed loop singularly perturbed and turns the separation the channels need into a bound to check rather than a crossover to tune; a leaky mid-ranging integrator returns the steady load to the spring; and the amplitude ceiling, read backwards, becomes a closed-form sizing rule that matches spring, geared motor and micro motor to the amplitudes and frequencies an application asks for.

Against SEAs, the Pi-SEA widens the tracked band at small amplitudes and lowers the residual the joint imposes on its environment, each by an order of magnitude.

summary.en: A series elastic actuator's single torque path is limited by reflected inertia, spring dynamics, and transmission friction, degrading small-amplitude, high-frequency tracking. Pi-SEA adds a load-side torque path by placing a direct-drive micro motor in parallel with a fixed-stiffness spring, allocating torque by timescale rather than filter design. Output torque is inferred from spring deflection and motor current without an added sensor. The paper derives channel-separation bounds, a leaky mid-ranging integrator, and sizing rules. Compared with SEAs, the authors report an order-of-magnitude wider tracked band at small amplitudes and lower residual interaction with the environment.
summary.zh: 串联弹性执行器的单一力矩通道受反射惯量、弹簧和传动摩擦制约，高频小幅命令跟踪能力会下降。论文提出并联集成弹性执行器Pi-SEA，在负载侧将直接驱动微电机与定刚度弹簧并联，以时间尺度而非滤波器划分两路力矩；弹簧形变和微电机电流用于估计输出力矩，无需额外传感器。设计还给出通道分离条件、泄漏中程积分及部件选型规则。相较SEA，作者报告小幅值跟踪频带扩大、对环境的残余作用均改善一个数量级。

items.title: A Second Torque Port for Series Elastic Actuators: Parallel-Integrated Design and Time-Scale Torque Allocation

Motivated by the way humans selectively look at relevant terrain during locomotion, we introduce TAGA, a Terrain-aware Active Gaze learning framework for Attention-based humanoid control. By fusing vision, proprioception, and motion commands, our framework guides the model to learn anticipatory cues and actively attend to specific areas of the height scan, selectively using these informative regions

sections.text:
Agile humanoid locomotion across diverse challenging terrain demands both wide perceptual coverage and precise local geometry understanding. Motivated by the way humans selectively look at relevant terrain during locomotion, we introduce TAGA, a Terrain-aware Active Gaze learning framework for Attention-based humanoid control.

By fusing vision, proprioception, and motion commands, our framework guides the model to learn anticipatory cues and actively attend to specific areas of the height scan, selectively using these informative regions for the downstream network.

This adaptively increases the information density of observations under tight onboard computational constraints, thus enabling fine-grained perceptive locomotion over larger-scale terrains.

We find that such gaze behaviors can naturally emerge through reinforcement learning alone, without requiring additional supervision or explicit guidance, significantly improving training efficiency.

As a result, the trained policy demonstrates robust and generalizable locomotion in simulation and on hardware, including reliable terrain-aware foothold selection, elevated-platform traversal, competitive sparse-foothold traversal, and the largest reported real-world gap traversal distance of 1.2m among perceptive humanoid locomotion systems, while maintaining stability under severe perceptual disturbances and environmental interference.

summary.en: Agile humanoid locomotion requires broad perception and precise local terrain geometry under onboard compute limits. TAGA fuses vision, proprioception, and motion commands to learn anticipatory cues and actively attend to informative regions of a height scan, supporting terrain-aware foothold selection. The authors report that gaze behavior emerges through reinforcement learning without extra supervision and improves training efficiency. The policy is evaluated in simulation and on hardware, including elevated platforms, sparse footholds, and perceptual disturbances. The abstract reports a 1.2 m real-world gap traversal, described as the largest reported among perceptive humanoid locomotion systems.
summary.zh: 人形机器人在复杂地形上行走，需要兼顾广域感知与局部几何细节，但机载算力有限。TAGA融合视觉、本体感觉和运动指令，训练策略主动关注高度扫描中的信息区域，以提高观察的信息密度并提前选择落足位置。作者报告这种主动注视行为可仅通过强化学习涌现，无需额外监督，并能提高训练效率。策略在仿真和硬件上测试，展示高台、稀疏落脚点及受感知干扰时的行走能力；摘要称其在感知式人形系统中实现了最大报告的1.2米真实跨沟距离。

items.title: TAGA: Terrain-aware Active Gaze Learning for Generalizable Agile Humanoid Locomotion

We study instruction switching, where a new task is issued during or after the execution of a different one. We observe that a target task that is reliably completed from its standard initial states can become inaccessible from states produced by a preceding task. We call such

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can execute many tasks from standard initial states, yet a new instruction may fail after another task has altered the robot's physical state. We study instruction switching, where a new task is issued during or after the execution of a different one.

We observe that a target task that is reliably completed from its standard initial states can become inaccessible from states produced by a preceding task. We call such states task islands. We propose Causeway, a training-free inference-time intervention.

Given the current state and a re-entry pose for the target task, Causeway back-propagates through the frozen decoding computation and applies a state-directed write within the action-stream representation. The VLA decodes the return motion itself, without parameter updates, a new action head, or external action generation.

Across 71 cross-object pairs, three switch timings, and three VLA architectures on LIBERO-Goal, Causeway raises bare-switch success from 3-26% to 47-65% and increases the rate of reaching the handoff neighborhood by 42-72 percentage points across models.

Additional experiments on LIBERO-Object and a real xArm platform show that the recovery extends beyond the main LIBERO-Goal setting, both in simulation and on a robot.

summary.en: A VLA task that works from its standard initial state may become inaccessible after another task changes the robot's state, creating what the authors call a task island. Causeway is a training-free inference-time intervention: given the current state and a target re-entry pose, it back-propagates through frozen decoding and writes state-directed information into the action stream, letting the VLA generate its own return motion. Across 71 cross-object pairs, three switch timings, and three architectures on LIBERO-Goal, bare-switch success increases from 3–26% to 47–65%. The handoff-neighborhood rate rises by 42–72 percentage points. Further tests include LIBERO-Object and a real xArm.
summary.zh: 视觉语言动作策略从标准初始状态能完成任务，但前一任务改变机器人状态后，新指令可能落入无法进入目标任务的“任务孤岛”。Causeway是一种免训练的推理时干预：给定当前状态和目标任务重入姿态，对冻结解码过程反向传播，并在动作流表示中写入状态引导信息，由原策略生成返回动作。LIBERO-Goal上，作者跨71组跨物体任务、三种切换时机和三种架构测试，报告切换成功率从3%至26%升至47%至65%；到达交接邻域的比例提升42至72个百分点。LIBERO-Object及真实xArm实验也显示恢复效果。

items.title: Causeway: Restoring Task Accessibility for Instruction Switching in VLA Policies

Using monocular RGB, GPT-6-Astra decides when to observe, how to move, and when to stop, without navigation-specific fine-tuning, a trained waypoint predictor, or a pre-built scene

sections.text:
We investigate whether GPT-6-Astra, a general-purpose foundation model, can navigate unfamiliar environments using its own perception, reasoning, and decision-making capabilities.

Our evaluation focuses on zero-shot vision-and-language navigation in continuous environments (VLN-CE) through a minimal interface in the Codex harness, aiming to unleash GPT-6-Astra's full potential for navigation.

Using monocular RGB, GPT-6-Astra decides when to observe, how to move, and when to stop, without navigation-specific fine-tuning, a trained waypoint predictor, or a pre-built scene map. Our evaluation yields four key findings and implications. First, GPT-6-Astra achieves strong zero-shot navigation performance using only monocular RGB observations.

On R2R-CE-100, GPT-6-Astra (ultra reasoning) achieves a success rate of 81.3%, exceeding the strongest reported zero-shot and even train-based success rates by 15.3 and 9.2 percentage points, respectively. Second, GPT-6-Astra exhibits promising capabilities in interpreting multi-stage instructions, understanding the environment, and adjusting routes.

Third, execution and goal-verification failures persist even with ultra reasoning. Fourth, these results motivate combining general-purpose model capabilities with navigation-specific expertise.

Based on these findings, future VLN research should investigate which aspects of instruction interpretation, spatial understanding, and navigation decision-making general-purpose models can handle directly, and where navigation-specific learning can extend their capabilities.

This includes exploring how spatial representations, navigation experience, and learned control skills can improve progress tracking, error recovery, and goal verification while preserving the flexibility to adjust routes.

summary.en: The paper evaluates whether GPT-6-Astra can perform zero-shot vision-and-language navigation in unfamiliar continuous environments using its own perception and reasoning. With monocular RGB, it chooses when to observe, move, and stop, without navigation-specific fine-tuning, a trained waypoint predictor, or a prebuilt map. On R2R-CE-100, the authors report 81.3% success with ultra reasoning, exceeding the strongest reported zero-shot and train-based results cited in the abstract. The evaluation also notes multi-stage instruction understanding and route adjustment, but execution and goal-verification failures remain, motivating combination with navigation-specific expertise.
summary.zh: 论文评估通用基础模型GPT-6-Astra能否仅凭自身视觉与推理能力，在陌生连续环境中零样本执行视觉语言导航。模型使用单目RGB，自主决定何时观察、如何移动及何时停止，不使用导航专项微调、训练路点预测器或预建地图。在R2R-CE-100上，作者报告ultra推理设置成功率为81.3%，高于文中最强已报告零样本和训练式结果。评估还观察到多阶段指令理解与路线调整能力，但执行和目标验证失败仍存在；摘要据此提出结合通用模型与导航专门能力，而非宣称问题已解决。

items.title: GPT-6-Astra Lights Up Embodied Navigation: Evaluation in Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments

Moreover, the absence of an explicit world model casts further doubt on their control capabilities. In this concept paper, we propose a novel architecture that addresses sample efficiency in VLAs by training a predictive world model on the embedding space of the VLA's vision encoder. We hypothesize that these embeddings are action-relevant and usable for

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs), while showing strong potential for robot control, require massive amounts of high-quality imitation learning data. Moreover, the absence of an explicit world model casts further doubt on their control capabilities.

In this concept paper, we propose a novel architecture that addresses sample efficiency in VLAs by training a predictive world model on the embedding space of the VLA's vision encoder. We hypothesize that these embeddings are action-relevant and usable for future prediction.

To this end, we propose using the suggested architecture to investigate how well these embeddings predict the future based on actions, as the inability to do so would mark a key limitation of VLA architectures: the lack of a non-lossy implicit world model to simulate real-world dynamics.

The proposed architecture differs from the standard world model dynamics as the loss comes from the embedding space rather than the pixel space, similar to joint embedding predictive architectures. Furthermore, the trained world model can be utilized for short-term planning tasks by sampling VLA actions given goal images.

We intend to examine the richness of vision embeddings in VLAs and reduce their high data requirements through a world model that can also generate plans during inference.

summary.en: This concept paper addresses VLA dependence on large imitation datasets and the lack of an explicit world model. It proposes training a predictive world model in the embedding space of a VLA vision encoder rather than directly in pixel space, hypothesizing that the embeddings capture action-relevant information for future prediction. The proposed model could also support short-horizon planning by sampling actions conditioned on goal images. The abstract describes intended investigations and expected uses, but reports no completed experiments or performance results.
summary.zh: 这篇概念论文关注视觉语言动作模型对高质量模仿数据的依赖及缺少显式世界模型的问题，提出在视觉编码器嵌入空间训练预测式世界模型，而非直接在像素空间拟合未来。作者假设视觉嵌入包含与动作相关、可用于未来预测的信息，并计划检验其预测能力；若无法预测，将暴露现有表征的局限。提案还设想根据目标图像采样动作，用于短期规划。摘要描述的是拟研究的架构和目标，没有报告已完成实验或性能结果。

items.title: Towards VLA-Dreamer: Refining VLA Behavior Using World Models

items.intro: arXiv:2609.31110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as high-level planners for mobile robots, robot manipulators, and autonomous vehicles. Recent studies show that these systems can be influenced through malicious text, speech, visual instructions, retrieved documents, and poisoned sensory context. Most defenses ask whether a proposed action is physically safe. This paper studies a different problem: an action may be physically safe and still violate the mission authorized by the user. An attacker may redirect

sections.text:
Large language models are increasingly used as high-level planners for mobile robots, robot manipulators, and autonomous vehicles. Recent studies show that these systems can be influenced through malicious text, speech, visual instructions, retrieved documents, and poisoned sensory context. Most defenses ask whether a proposed action is physically safe.

This paper studies a different problem: an action may be physically safe and still violate the mission authorized by the user. An attacker may redirect a delivery robot, replace an approved object, extend a robot's operating region, activate an unnecessary sensor, or delay a mission without creating an immediate physical hazard.

We call this attack \emph{safety-compliant mission hijacking}.We propose MissionPAIR, an adaptive attack framework that searches for executable plans that pass a safety gate while violating an authenticated mission.

We also propose AuthGuard-R, a deterministic authorization layer that binds every executable action to a signed mission, robot identity, object and region scope, current state, time, and input provenance. AuthGuard-R operates with an independent safety gate, giving a dual-gate architecture.

We formalize mission policies over robot traces, define security games, and prove authorization soundness, mission non-escalation, replay resistance, robot binding, provenance separation, threshold-approval security, audit-log tamper evidence, and trace-level composition.

We report a preliminary cross-model evaluation with Claude Haiku~4.5 and the open-source Qwen2.5~7B planner. Across 240 live attack trials, the planners followed an injected mission deviation in 109 trials; AuthGuard-R rejected all 109 resulting unauthorized actions.

A separate hand-constructed suite of eleven protocol- and policy-level attacks was also blocked completely.

summary.en: An action may pass a physical safety check yet violate the user's authorized mission, for example by changing an approved object or expanding the operating region. The paper studies this safety-compliant mission hijacking and proposes MissionPAIR, an adaptive attack framework, plus AuthGuard-R, a deterministic authorization layer operating alongside an independent safety gate. Actions are bound to a signed mission, robot identity, scope, state, time, and input provenance; several security properties are formalized and proven. In a preliminary evaluation, two planners followed injected deviations in 109 of 240 live trials, and AuthGuard-R rejected all 109 resulting unauthorized actions. It also blocked eleven hand-constructed attacks.
summary.zh: 机器人动作即使通过物理安全检查，也可能违反用户授权的任务，例如擅自更换目标物或扩大作业区域。论文将此类问题称为符合安全约束的任务劫持，并提出攻击框架MissionPAIR，以及与独立安全门并行的确定性授权层AuthGuard-R，将动作绑定到签名任务、机器人身份、对象和区域范围、状态、时间及输入来源。作者形式化多项安全性质并给出证明。初步跨模型评估中，两个规划器在240次攻击试验里109次遵从注入的任务偏离，AuthGuard-R拒绝了这109项未授权动作；另构造的11种协议与策略攻击也全部被拦截。

items.title: AuthGuard-R: Safety-Compliant Mission Hijacking and Dual-Gate Defense for LLM-Controlled Robots

This hierarchical design has practical value only if the planner can generate plans fast enough to meet real-time control requirements, and the resulting plans actually contribute to the generation of action. We study one such system, a waypoint hierarchy pipeline adapted from $\pi_{0.5}$, and find that neither requirement is satisfied. This baseline

sections.text:
Hierarchical vision-language-action (VLA) systems consist of a high-level vision-language planner and a low-level action expert that generates continuous actions.

This hierarchical design has practical value only if the planner can generate plans fast enough to meet real-time control requirements, and the resulting plans actually contribute to the generation of action. We study one such system, a waypoint hierarchy pipeline adapted from $\pi_{0.5}$, and find that neither requirement is satisfied.

This baseline relies on token-level autoregressive decoding (Token-AR) to generate a waypoint plan, requiring 57 very expensive vision-language model (VLM) forward passes. However, we find that erasing the waypoint endpoints has little effect on task success.

Two findings reveal the misalignment of planner-executor: the planner generates outputs at an excessively fine granularity, and the executor underuses plans as a control condition.

We address the latency issue with waypoint-aligned block-autoregressive decoding (Block-AR), and plan underuse issue with normalized goal modulation (NGM), a layer-wise goal path constrained by phase gating and anti-shortcut training so that the waypoint influences action generation maintaining other signals.

Our method reduces the maximum number of VLM forward passes from 57 to 8 on LIBERO, including one prefix prefill, and achieves an $8.7\times$ reduction in planning latency on a Rokae dual-arm robot.

With normalized goal modulation and anti-shortcut training, Block-AR's success rate on LIBERO-Long increases from 91.0% to 96.2%, while its average success rate across the four suites increases from 95.85% to 98.45%.On three bimanual tasks with this robot, success rates remain comparable across methods.

summary.en: Hierarchical VLA systems need both timely planning and faithful execution of plans. Analysis of a waypoint pipeline adapted from pi0.5 finds token-level autoregressive generation requires 57 costly VLM passes, while erasing waypoint endpoints barely affects task success, indicating overly fine plans and weak executor conditioning. Block-AR generates waypoint-aligned blocks to reduce latency; normalized goal modulation and anti-shortcut training make plans more influential in action generation. On LIBERO, the maximum passes fall to eight, and planning latency on a Rokae dual-arm robot drops 8.7-fold. LIBERO-Long success rises from 91.0% to 96.2%, with comparable results on three bimanual robot tasks.

sections.text:
World Action Models (WAMs) jointly model visual dynamics and action generation for generalist robot manipulation. A central challenge is to integrate priors from large-scale pretrained models---including visual dynamics, scene semantics, geometry, and motion---into a unified framework for robot action generation.

We introduce InternW0-$\Delta$, a unified WAM pretrained on a heterogeneous corpus that outperforms prior methods across simulation benchmarks and real-robot platforms. InternW0-$\Delta$ combines pretrained visual dynamics, scene-level semantics, 4D geometric and motion priors, and action generation within a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) framework.

A pretrained video expert and an action expert interact under semantic guidance from a frozen VLM, while a pretrained 4D foundation model injects geometric and motion priors through training-only distillation.

We further introduce Causal Imprint, which learns future-relevant scene changes from training-only future supervision and provides predictive representations directly to the action expert without future-video rollout at inference.

For large-scale joint training, we construct a heterogeneous corpus of robot demonstrations, UMI data, egocentric human demonstrations, and Ego2Robot data, curated and aligned under a common state-action representation. The resulting corpus contains over 20K hours of processed training data, to our knowledge the largest open-source corpus of its kind.

We pretrain InternW0-$\Delta$ on this corpus and demonstrate strong performance across simulation benchmarks and real-robot platforms. We will open source the training code, model weights, infrastructure, data-processing pipeline, and processed data where licenses permit. Project page: https://internrobotics.github.io/InternW0-Delta/

summary.en: A generalist World Action Model must combine visual dynamics, scene semantics, geometric and motion priors, and action generation. InternW0-Delta uses a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture in which pretrained video and action experts interact under a frozen VLM's semantic guidance; a pretrained 4D model contributes geometry and motion through training-only distillation. Causal Imprint learns future-relevant scene changes from training supervision without requiring future-video rollout at inference. The authors curate over 20,000 hours from robot, UMI, egocentric human, and Ego2Robot data, and report strong simulation and real-robot performance, without numerical results in the abstract.
summary.zh: 通用机器人世界动作模型需要将视觉动力学、场景语义、几何运动先验与动作生成结合。InternW0-Δ以混合Transformer架构协同预训练视频专家和动作专家，由冻结视觉语言模型提供语义引导，并通过仅训练期蒸馏注入四维几何与运动先验；Causal Imprint利用未来监督学习与动作相关的场景变化，推理时无需生成未来视频。作者汇集机器人示范、UMI、人类第一视角及Ego2Robot数据，形成超过2万小时处理数据，并报告模型在模拟基准和实体机器人平台表现强劲，但摘要未给出具体成绩数值。

items.title: InternW0-$\Delta$: A World Action Model Bridging Predictive Dynamics and Actions with 20K+ Hours of Open Data

items.intro: arXiv:2609.30554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have recently demonstrated promising capabilities as in-context policy optimizers for Reinforcement Learning (RL), enabling policy search driven by both numerical reward signals and natural language reasoning. However, deploying such methods in practice requires transmitting raw policy parameters and rewards history to cloud-based LLM APIs, exposing proprietary control strategies to third-party service providers. To address this issue, this paper introduces Privacy-Preserving Prompted Policy Search (PP-ProPS), a framework that enables LLM-guided

sections.text:
Large language models (LLMs) have recently demonstrated promising capabilities as in-context policy optimizers for Reinforcement Learning (RL), enabling policy search driven by both numerical reward signals and natural language reasoning.

However, deploying such methods in practice requires transmitting raw policy parameters and rewards history to cloud-based LLM APIs, exposing proprietary control strategies to third-party service providers.

To address this issue, this paper introduces Privacy-Preserving Prompted Policy Search (PP-ProPS), a framework that enables LLM-guided policy optimization while keeping policy and environmental parameters confidential.

PP-ProPS encodes policy parameters and reward values using secret client-side transformations before they are included in each API request, ensuring that the LLM provider observes only encoded policy parameters and scaled reward information.

Furthermore, unlike Vanilla ProPS, the proposed framework does not require the true optimal episodic return to be known or disclosed to the LLM. Beyond protecting the optimization data, PP-ProPS improves the search process in two ways.

First, it provides the LLM with individual reward components instead of only a single total return, offering more informative feedback about each candidate policy. Second, it uses a bounded history that prevents the prompt from growing indefinitely, improving search with high-dimensional policies and supporting the use of open-weight LLMs.

The proposed PP-ProPS is evaluated on both continuous and discrete control problems spanning Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact (MuJoCo) locomotion, classic control, highway driving, and robotic arm manipulation.

Compared to Vanilla ProPS, the proposed PP-ProPS outperforms ProPS in seven of the ten evaluated tasks, and surpasses conventional RL methods including PPO, SAC, and TRPO, in five of the six tasks.

summary.en: Cloud-based LLM policy optimization can expose proprietary parameters and reward histories. PP-ProPS applies secret client-side transformations to encode policy parameters and rewards before API submission; it also supplies individual reward components, bounds history length, and does not require revealing the true optimal return. Evaluation covers continuous and discrete control, including MuJoCo locomotion, classic control, highway driving, and arm manipulation. The authors report that PP-ProPS outperforms Vanilla ProPS on seven of ten tasks and surpasses conventional methods such as PPO, SAC, and TRPO on five of six tasks. The abstract does not state a formal privacy guarantee.
summary.zh: 让大语言模型通过云端API优化强化学习策略，通常需发送原始参数和奖励历史，可能泄露专有控制信息。PP-ProPS在客户端先用秘密变换编码策略参数和奖励，并向模型提供分项奖励及有界历史，不要求披露真实最优回报。论文在连续与离散控制任务上评估，包括MuJoCo、经典控制、高速公路驾驶和机械臂操作。相较Vanilla ProPS，作者报告PP-ProPS在10项任务中的7项表现更好；与PPO、SAC、TRPO等传统强化学习方法相比，在6项任务中的5项胜出。摘要未说明隐私保护的形式化保证，结果限于所测任务。

items.title: Privacy-Preserving Prompted Policy Search for Robotic Control

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable robots to follow natural language instructions and generalize across diverse tasks, but they remain vulnerable to execution failures that compromise reliability in real-world deployment. Detecting such failures during execution is therefore critical for the robust deployment of embodied systems.

Existing failure detection methods either rely on expensive action resampling or external models, while alternatives propagate trajectory-level labels uniformly across every timestep, obscuring localized failure signals.

In this paper, we propose \textbf{Hide-and-Seek}, a framework that formulates VLA failure detection as a coarsely supervised learning problem.

By combining inter-trajectory and intra-trajectory contrastive objectives, Hide-and-Seek localizes failure-indicative actions and induces temporally structured failure signals from trajectory-level supervision alone, without any step-level annotation.

We evaluate Hide-and-Seek on LIBERO, VLABench, and a real-world robotic platform across three representative VLA policies: OpenVLA, $\pi_0$, and $\pi_{0.5}$.Our method achieves state-of-the-art multi-task failure detection performance with a practical accuracy--timeliness trade-off under conformal prediction, and generalizes well to both seen and unseen tasks.

summary.en: Robot execution failures are difficult to label frame by frame, while assigning a trajectory-level label uniformly can obscure localized signals. Hide-and-Seek treats VLA failure detection as coarsely supervised learning, combining inter- and intra-trajectory contrastive objectives to localize failure-indicative actions without step-level annotations. The authors evaluate it with OpenVLA, pi0, and pi0.5 on LIBERO, VLABench, and a real-world platform. They report state-of-the-art multi-task failure detection and a practical accuracy-timeliness trade-off under conformal prediction, with generalization to seen and unseen tasks. The abstract provides no specific accuracy figures.
summary.zh: 机器人策略执行失败时，逐帧监测信号难以获得，直接把整条轨迹标签复制到每一时刻又会掩盖局部故障。Hide-and-Seek将视觉语言动作策略的失败检测作为粗粒度监督学习，结合跨轨迹和轨迹内对比目标，从轨迹级标签定位提示失败的动作时段，无需逐步标注。作者在LIBERO、VLABench及真实机器人平台上测试OpenVLA、π0和π0.5，报告其多任务失败检测达到当时最佳，并在保形预测下取得实用的准确率—及时性权衡，对已见和未见任务均有泛化表现。摘要未列出具体准确率。

items.title: Hide-and-Seek in Trajectories: Discovering Failure Signals for VLA Runtime Monitoring

sections.text:
Air-ground collaborative robots have shown great potential in the field of fire and rescue. Mapping and navigation, as the key foundation for air-ground collaborative robots to achieve efficient task execution, have attracted a great deal of attention.

This growing interest in collaborative robot mapping and navigation is conducive to enhancing the intelligent execution of fire and rescue tasks, but there has been no comprehensive investigation of this field to highlight their strengths.

In this paper, we present a systematic review of the air-ground collaborative robots for fire and rescue from a new perspective of mapping and navigation. First, an air-ground collaborative robots framework for fire and rescue missions based on unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) mapping and unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) navigation is introduced.

Then, the research progress of mapping and navigation under this framework is systematically summarized, including UAV mapping, UAV/UGV co-localization, and UGV navigation, with their main achievements and limitations.

Based on the needs of fire and rescue missions, the collaborative robots with different numbers of UAVs and UGVs are classified, and their practicality in fire and rescue tasks is elaborated, with a focus on the discussion of their merits and demerits.

In addition, the application examples of air-ground collaborative robots in various firefighting and rescue scenarios are given. Finally, this paper emphasizes the current challenges and potential research opportunities, providing a reference for practitioners and researchers interested in this rapidly evolving field of air-ground collaborative robotics.

summary.en: This systematic review examines air-ground collaborative robots for fire and rescue from the perspectives of mapping and navigation. It outlines a framework in which unmanned aerial vehicles map environments and unmanned ground vehicles navigate, then surveys UAV mapping, UAV-UGV co-localization, and ground-robot navigation, including reported achievements and limitations. The authors classify systems by the numbers of aerial and ground robots and discuss their practicality across firefighting and rescue scenarios. Application examples are summarized, followed by current challenges and research opportunities. As a review, the abstract reports no new quantitative experiments.
summary.zh: 论文针对消防救援中的空地协同机器人开展测绘与导航视角的系统综述，关注无人机建图与无人地面车导航如何配合支撑任务执行。作者先提出以无人机测绘、地面车导航为核心的协同框架，再梳理无人机建图、空地协同定位和地面车导航的研究进展、主要成果及局限，并按无人机与地面车数量分类讨论不同系统在救援场景中的适用性。综述还汇集消防和救援应用示例，最后归纳当前挑战与研究机会；摘要没有报告新的定量实验结果。

items.title: Air-Ground Collaborative Robots for Fire and Rescue Missions: A Survey from the Mapping and Navigation Perspective

sections.text:
Contact-rich assembly tasks such as peg-in-hole insertion remain difficult to learn from limited demonstrations. While retrieval-augmented imitation learning, which augments target demonstrations with relevant prior data, offers a promising direction, its applicability to contact-rich manipulation remains largely unexplored.

Contact-rich insertion unfolds over multiple phases from search to insert, and retrieving phase-specific experience from prior data in principled ways remains an open question.

Our key insight is that a compliant wrist enables the robot to sustain contact throughout execution, producing rich tactile and force signals that naturally reveal the phase structure of insertion and inform what should be retrieved.

Based on this insight, we present PHASE (PHase-Aware Segmentation and REtrieval), a framework for compliance-enabled tactile phase retrieval that integrates multimodal contact-aware representation learning, variable-length phase segmentation from tactile signals, and phase-consistent retrieval for policy learning.

We evaluate PHASE on real-world peg-in-hole insertion across five peg geometries, comparing against retrieval strategies drawn from state-of-the-art methods under a shared policy architecture.

PHASE improves the overall success rate by 13 percentage points over the strongest non-phase-aware baseline, and improves performance under unseen initial positions by 30 percentage points. These results demonstrate that aligning retrieval with interaction-defined contact phases substantially improves robustness in few-shot insertion learning.

summary.en: Contact-rich insertion must handle multiple phases, from search to insertion, while learning from few demonstrations. PHASE uses a compliant wrist to maintain contact and extract phase structure from tactile and force signals, combining multimodal contact representations, variable-length segmentation, and phase-consistent retrieval for policy learning. On real-world peg-in-hole insertion with five peg geometries and a shared policy architecture, the authors report a 13-percentage-point overall success gain over the strongest non-phase-aware retrieval baseline. Performance with unseen initial positions improves by 30 points. The evidence concerns the tested insertion tasks.
summary.zh: 接触丰富的插孔装配需要从少量示范中学习，并处理搜索、对准和插入等交互阶段。PHASE利用柔顺腕部维持接触，从触觉与力信号识别阶段，再结合多模态接触表征、可变长度阶段切分和阶段一致的经验检索训练策略。作者在五种插销几何的真实插孔任务中，以相同策略架构与既有检索方法比较，报告总体成功率比最强非阶段感知基线高13个百分点；在未见初始位置下高30个百分点。结果支持按交互阶段检索有助于少样本插入鲁棒性，适用范围是所测真实任务。

items.title: PHASE: Compliance-Enabled Tactile Phase Retrieval for Few-Shot Insertion Learning

Specifically, MOCHA leverages the hypernetwork architecture to learn a network that produces specialized network parameters optimized for a given objective and parameterized robot design; we term this a multi-objective design hypernetwork (MDH). We demonstrate the capabilities of MDHs to represent

sections.text:
In this work, we present MOCHA, the first, to our knowledge, reinforcement learning based approach to computing a family of Pareto-optimal policies across the design space of a robot using a single network.

Specifically, MOCHA leverages the hypernetwork architecture to learn a network that produces specialized network parameters optimized for a given objective and parameterized robot design; we term this a multi-objective design hypernetwork (MDH).

We demonstrate the capabilities of MDHs to represent a complex family of design-dependent strategies on two distinct robot morphologies, each with six design dimensions and across 2-3 objectives.

Moreover, we propose an approach for efficiently producing a Design Pareto set using evolutionary search of the learned policy network, generating the optimal design-policy combination for each objective prioritization.

Lastly, we provide an efficient method for computing generalist robot designs which achieve the best cumulative performance across the entire set of objectives.

summary.en: MOCHA addresses multi-objective robot co-design by learning a family of Pareto-optimal policies across a robot design space with a single hypernetwork. Its multi-objective design hypernetwork produces specialized policy parameters conditioned on objective priorities and a parameterized design. Evolutionary search over the learned network constructs a design-policy Pareto set, and the paper also describes a method for selecting generalist designs with strong cumulative performance across objectives. Demonstrations cover two robot morphologies, each with six design dimensions and two or three objectives. The abstract gives no numerical performance results or real-robot validation.
summary.zh: 多目标机器人设计通常需为不同目标权衡选择策略与形态，MOCHA尝试用单一超网络表示设计空间中的一族帕累托最优策略。其多目标设计超网络根据目标优先级和参数化机器人设计生成专用策略参数，并通过进化搜索得到设计—策略帕累托集合，同时提供跨目标整体表现较好的通用设计求解方式。作者在两种不同机器人形态上展示方法，每种形态包含六个设计维度及两到三个目标，说明网络可表征设计相关策略。摘要描述能力展示与算法方法，没有给出具体性能数值或实体机器人验证。

items.title: MOCHA: Multi-Objective Co-Design using Hypernetwork Architectures

sections.text:
Traversing narrow gaps is challenging for autonomous quadrotors, especially when control commands come directly from high-dimensional visual observations. Existing end-to-end methods often rely on behavior cloning or full-rollout backpropagation through time (BPTT) via differentiable simulation, which can limit policy performance or incur high training costs.

We propose a two-stage reinforcement learning framework for more efficient ego-centric visuomotor gap-traversal policy training, leveraging quasi-analytical policy gradients (QPG) via differentiable simulation and critic warm-starting.

The framework utilizes QPG to avoid backpropagation through visual rendering, reducing computation and memory costs while improving sample efficiency. In the first stage, an expert actor and critic are trained using privileged observations, including gap geometry.

Unlike prior gap-traversal approaches, our training utilizing QPG does not require resetting the agent along optimized reference trajectories. In the second stage, a visual policy is trained using binary gap masks from two ego-centric cameras and low-dimensional observations, while its privileged critic is warm-started from the first stage.

This substantially improves training efficiency and traversal success compared with cold-starting the critic or using full-rollout BPTT.

Our framework does not require retraining the expert actor when system parameters change, enabling more efficient generalization across drone platforms than state-of-the-art visual gap-traversal methods based on action supervision. The learned visual policy also generalizes to gaps with unseen shapes.

Extensive real-world experiments further demonstrate robust gap traversal using binary masks rendered online. Beyond gap traversal, the proposed framework is generic and can be extended to other visuomotor robot learning tasks.

summary.en: Visual quadrotor gap traversal is difficult to train end to end: behavior cloning can limit performance, while full-trajectory backpropagation through differentiable simulation is costly. The paper proposes two-stage reinforcement learning. A privileged expert is trained first, then a visual policy using binary masks from two onboard views and low-dimensional observations, with the privileged critic warm-started. Quasi-analytical policy gradients avoid backpropagating through rendering and do not require resets along optimized reference trajectories. The authors report better training efficiency and traversal success than cold-starting the critic or full-rollout backpropagation, generalization to unseen gap shapes, and real-world traversal with online-rendered masks.
summary.zh: 四旋翼依赖高维视觉直接穿越狭窄间隙时，行为克隆可能限制策略效果，完整轨迹反传又计算昂贵。论文提出两阶段强化学习：先用包含间隙几何的特权观测训练专家，再以准解析策略梯度和可微仿真训练双目二值间隙掩码视觉策略，并将第一阶段评论家热启动。该方法不需沿优化参考轨迹重置，也避免对视觉渲染执行时间反传。作者报告其比冷启动评论家或完整轨迹反传训练更高效、穿越成功率更好，并可泛化至未见间隙形状；真实实验展示了在线生成掩码条件下的穿越。

items.title: Learning Vision-Based Agile Gap Traversal: Differentiable Simulation with a Warm-Started Critic

items.intro: arXiv:2607.12275v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quadrotors flying in tight formations are severely affected by turbulent aerodynamic interactions, such as downwash, that can cause catastrophic collisions if left unmodeled. To compensate for these effects, we propose a physics-informed residual dynamics learning framework that captures complex aerodynamic interactions while ensuring the joint multi-quadrotor system remains differentially flat. We leverage this preserved flatness to design a computationally efficient feedback linearization controller that is easily tunable with linear control techniques and cancels

sections.text:
Quadrotors flying in tight formations are severely affected by turbulent aerodynamic interactions, such as downwash, that can cause catastrophic collisions if left unmodeled.

To compensate for these effects, we propose a physics-informed residual dynamics learning framework that captures complex aerodynamic interactions while ensuring the joint multi-quadrotor system remains differentially flat.

We leverage this preserved flatness to design a computationally efficient feedback linearization controller that is easily tunable with linear control techniques and cancels aerodynamic disturbances via feedforward compensation. Hardware experiments demonstrate our framework reduces average tracking errors by 31% compared to nominal baselines.

Crucially, our lightweight approach matches the tracking performance of state-of-the-art nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) while requiring an order of magnitude less computation.

We are the first to show that stable, tight formation flight can be achieved with under 30 seconds of training data and a 5ms loop rate, unlocking high-fidelity aerodynamic compensation for compute-constrained flight stacks. The video of our physical experiments can be found at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uF26IkRFQMk

summary.en: Downwash and other aerodynamic interactions can destabilize tight quadrotor formations and cause collisions if left unmodeled. The paper learns physics-informed residual dynamics while preserving differential flatness of the joint system, enabling a computationally efficient feedback-linearization controller with feedforward disturbance compensation. Hardware experiments show a reported 31% reduction in average tracking error versus nominal baselines. The approach matches the tracking performance of state-of-the-art nonlinear MPC while using an order of magnitude less computation. The authors also report stable tight formation flight with under 30 seconds of training data and a 5 ms control loop in their tested setup.
summary.zh: 紧密编队飞行中的下洗等气动相互作用可能造成碰撞，名义动力学难以准确补偿。论文提出保微分平坦性的物理引导残差动力学学习方法，在学习多四旋翼气动效应的同时保持联合系统可微分平坦，据此设计计算高效的反馈线性化控制器及前馈扰动补偿。硬件实验中，作者报告相对名义基线平均跟踪误差降低31%，计算开销比非线性模型预测控制低一个数量级，同时达到相近跟踪表现。论文还报告用不足30秒训练数据、5毫秒控制周期实现稳定紧密编队；这些结果针对其所测飞行设置。

items.title: Flatness-Preserving Residual Learning for Real-Time Tight Quadrotor Formation Flight

This work proposes a dual-UAV payload transportation framework supported by a compact, custom-designed force sensor measuring the interaction force at the UAV cable anchor point. The sensor design and mathematical model are presented, and its performance is characterized through static and dynamic tests evaluating linearity, hysteresis, repeatability, and crossload

sections.text:
Cooperative payload transportation using multiple \textit{Unmanned Aerial Vehicles} (UAVs) poses challenges in stability, coordination, and robustness, especially under external disturbances and unmodeled dynamics.

This work proposes a dual-UAV payload transportation framework supported by a compact, custom-designed force sensor measuring the interaction force at the UAV cable anchor point.

The sensor design and mathematical model are presented, and its performance is characterized through static and dynamic tests evaluating linearity, hysteresis, repeatability, and crossload. The control architecture follows a cascade structure: fast inner loops handle vehicle stabilization, while outer loops are designed to compensate for the measured forces.

The approach is validated through simulations and indoor experiments under position uncertainty. Payload-drop and constrained-space tests assess the proposed sensing and control architecture against literature-based distributed references, showing improved stabilization, coordination, and disturbance rejection.

A video of the experiments is available at: https://youtu.be/rIw9-fvV8Qw.

summary.en: Cooperative payload transport by multiple UAVs must handle stability, coordination, disturbances, and unmodeled dynamics. This work develops a compact force sensor at the cable anchor for a dual-UAV system and uses measured interaction forces in a cascaded controller: fast inner loops stabilize each vehicle, while outer loops compensate for forces. Static and dynamic tests characterize sensor linearity, hysteresis, repeatability, and cross-load. Simulations and indoor experiments examine position uncertainty, payload-drop prevention, and constrained-space transport. The authors report better stabilization, coordination, and disturbance rejection than literature-based distributed references, but provide no numerical results in the abstract.
summary.zh: 多无人机协同吊运载荷需应对稳定性、协调和外部扰动，论文为双无人机系统设计安装于缆绳锚点的紧凑力传感器，并据测得交互力补偿控制。传感器通过静态和动态测试评估线性、迟滞、重复性及交叉载荷；控制采用级联结构，由快速内环稳定飞行器，外环处理测得的力。作者在仿真和室内实验中测试位置不确定、载荷防坠及受限空间任务，并报告相较文献分布式参考方案，稳定性、协同性和抗扰性改善。摘要未给出定量数据，验证环境限于所述室内实验。

items.title: Compact Force Sensor for Dual-UAV Cable-Suspended Payload Transport with Tension-Aware Outer-Loop Control

Learning directly on hardware is further constrained by the cost of real-world interaction. We present an online model-based reinforcement learning framework that learns a probabilistic dynamics ensemble model from scratch for sampling-based model predictive control. A precision-gated contouring objective conditions the progress reward on path accuracy, prioritizing precision over speed. In a data-driven excavator simulator, the framework achieves higher sample efficiency than

sections.text:
Precise, high-speed control remains challenging for robots with complex actuation dynamics. Learning directly on hardware is further constrained by the cost of real-world interaction. We present an online model-based reinforcement learning framework that learns a probabilistic dynamics ensemble model from scratch for sampling-based model predictive control.

A precision-gated contouring objective conditions the progress reward on path accuracy, prioritizing precision over speed. In a data-driven excavator simulator, the framework achieves higher sample efficiency than the evaluated model-based reinforcement learning baselines.

We validate the framework by learning directly on an 11.5-ton Menzi Muck M445 hydraulic excavator, without demonstrations or simulation pretraining. After 20 minutes of interaction, the controller reaches tracking accuracy comparable to prior learned controllers trained on 100-150 minutes of data.

After 40 minutes, it sustains sub-centimeter mean path error at high operating speeds.

summary.en: Precise, fast control of complex actuators is difficult, while learning directly on heavy machinery is costly. The proposed online model-based RL framework learns a probabilistic dynamics ensemble from scratch for sampling-based model-predictive control. A precision-gated contouring objective conditions progress reward on path accuracy. In a data-driven excavator simulator, the authors report higher sample efficiency than evaluated model-based RL baselines. They then learn directly on an 11.5-ton Menzi Muck M445 without demonstrations or simulation pretraining: after 20 minutes, tracking accuracy is comparable to prior controllers trained for 100–150 minutes; after 40 minutes, high-speed mean path error is sub-centimeter.
summary.zh: 液压挖掘机等复杂执行器机器人在真实硬件上学习控制，受交互成本约束，精确高速控制也较困难。论文提出在线模型强化学习框架，从头学习概率动力学集成模型，并用于采样式模型预测控制；精度门控的轮廓跟踪目标在路径误差较大时抑制进度奖励。数据驱动挖掘机仿真器中，作者报告其样本效率高于所比较的模型强化学习基线。随后在11.5吨Menzi Muck M445上直接学习，无示范或仿真预训练，20分钟交互达到既有控制器用100至150分钟训练的相近跟踪精度，40分钟后高速作业平均路径误差低于1厘米。

items.title: Precision at Speed: Sample-Efficient Online Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Hydraulic Excavator Control

At 281 g, it achieves the highest jump yet reported for an electrically actuated, spring-free system. The leg uses a new fabric-wrap transmission that provides a variable mechanical advantage, keeping a small electric motor near its peak power output through the

sections.text:
We demonstrate a jumping robot that reaches high (7.6 m) and fast (190 ms stance time) jumps from a single long leg driven by a direct-drive transmission, without elastic energy storage. At 281 g, it achieves the highest jump yet reported for an electrically actuated, spring-free system.

The leg uses a new fabric-wrap transmission that provides a variable mechanical advantage, keeping a small electric motor near its peak power output through the stroke while bracing the long, lightweight leg against buckling.

A balancing module at the top of the leg uses small propellers to control the leg's orientation on the ground and in the air, where the long leg provides a large moment arm for the control torques. The robot is validated outdoors with vertical jumps, attitude control on the ground and in flight, and tilted jumps.

summary.en: The paper demonstrates a lightweight electrically actuated monopedal robot that jumps without elastic energy storage. A fabric-wrap transmission provides variable mechanical advantage, keeping a small motor near peak power through the stroke while bracing the long leg against buckling. A module at the leg top uses small propellers to control orientation on the ground and in flight. The 281 g robot is reported to jump 7.6 m high with a 190 ms stance time, which the authors describe as the highest jump reported for a spring-free electrically actuated system. Outdoor tests include vertical and tilted jumps and attitude control.
summary.zh: 论文展示一台无需弹性储能、由直驱电机驱动单长腿的电动单足跳跃机器人，目标是在保持轻量的同时获得高跳跃能力。腿部使用织物缠绕传动改变机械优势，使小型电机在行程中接近峰值功率，并支撑长腿避免屈曲；腿顶的平衡模块通过小型螺旋桨控制地面和空中姿态。作者报告机器人质量281克，垂直跳高7.6米、支撑期190毫秒，并称其为当时电驱无弹簧系统中最高纪录。户外验证还包括地面及飞行姿态控制和倾斜跳跃。

items.title: A Long-Legged, Direct-Drive Monopedal Robot Achieves Exceptional Jump Height

In this work, we tackle cloth unfolding using a regrasping-in-the-air strategy, where one manipulator holds the cloth while the other grasps it at an optimally selected point to unfold it. To this end, we

sections.text:
Cloth manipulation is a challenging task due to the deformable and high-dimensional nature of cloth, which leads to complex interaction dynamics and perceptual ambiguity arising from frequent occlusions of critical visual cues such as folds, edges, and grasp points.

In this work, we tackle cloth unfolding using a regrasping-in-the-air strategy, where one manipulator holds the cloth while the other grasps it at an optimally selected point to unfold it.

To this end, we propose CeDiRNet-6DoF, a deep learning framework that jointly predicts effective grasp points and the complete 6-DoF grasp pose from the observed cloth configuration.

By integrating dense 3D grasp regression with segmentation and sine-cosine-encoded Euler angles, the proposed method reliably estimates the grasp configuration that maximizes the unfolded cloth area. We extensively evaluated CeDiRNet-6DoF on a bimanual robotic setup within the ICRA 2024 Cloth Competition framework, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

An ablation study further validates the benefits of key design components, including joint segmentation, background randomization, and image cropping. These results establish CeDiRNet-6DoF as a robust and versatile foundation for reliable robotic cloth manipulation in unstructured environments.

summary.en: Cloth unfolding is difficult because the deformable material is high-dimensional and folds, edges, and grasp points are often occluded. CeDiRNet-6DoF supports an in-air regrasp strategy: one arm holds the cloth while the other grasps a selected point to unfold it. The network jointly predicts an effective grasp point and full 6-DoF pose using dense 3D grasp regression, segmentation, and sine-cosine angle encoding, aiming to maximize unfolded area. Evaluation on a bimanual setup within the ICRA 2024 Cloth Competition framework is reported as state of the art. Ablations examine segmentation, background randomization, and image cropping.
summary.zh: 布料易变形且高维，褶皱、边缘和抓取点常被遮挡，使展开操作中的抓取位姿估计困难。论文提出CeDiRNet-6DoF，采用空中重新抓取策略：一只机械臂持布，另一只在选定位置抓取以展开。网络结合稠密三维抓取回归、分割及正弦余弦角度表示，从布料观测中联合预测抓取点和完整六自由度位姿，目标是最大化展开面积。在ICRA 2024布料竞赛框架下的双臂实验中，作者报告达到当时最优表现；消融分析支持联合分割、背景随机化和裁剪的作用。

items.title: Vision-Based 6-DoF Grasp Pose Estimation for Robot Cloth Unfolding

items.intro: arXiv:2609.27308v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study coding agents for long-horizon, dexterous robotics and ask whether their solutions can provide scalable supervision for learning general robot policies. To test this, we develop EMBODIEDSWE-BENCH, a simulation benchmark for coding agents spanning contact-rich manipulation, deformable objects, and long-horizon tasks requiring up to half an hour of continuous interaction. We find that frontier coding agents can solve complex long-horizon tasks and transfer prior solutions across both tasks and embodiments. We also

sections.text:
We study coding agents for long-horizon, dexterous robotics and ask whether their solutions can provide scalable supervision for learning general robot policies.

To test this, we develop EMBODIEDSWE-BENCH, a simulation benchmark for coding agents spanning contact-rich manipulation, deformable objects, and long-horizon tasks requiring up to half an hour of continuous interaction. We find that frontier coding agents can solve complex long-horizon tasks and transfer prior solutions across both tasks and embodiments.

We also design supporting tools that help agents more effectively solve these tasks. However, the resulting solutions require substantial iterative interaction and are typically specialized to individual task instances. We therefore introduce EMBODIEDSWE-GEN, which expands a single solution from coding agent into large diverse trajectories for training a VLA.

VLA performance improves with more generated demonstrations, and agent-aided diversification improves generalization to held-out task variations. We also show that a VLA finetuned solely on coding-agent-generated simulation demonstrations completes a long-horizon task on real robot.

Together, our framework uses coding agents to solve complex robotics tasks and turn verified solutions into scalable supervision for robot policies.

summary.en: This work asks whether coding agents can solve long-horizon dexterous robotics tasks and provide scalable supervision for general robot policies. EMBODIEDSWE-BENCH is a simulation benchmark covering contact-rich manipulation, deformable objects, and tasks requiring up to half an hour of continuous interaction. The authors find that frontier coding agents solve complex tasks and transfer solutions across tasks and embodiments, though they require substantial iteration and produce instance-specific solutions. EMBODIEDSWE-GEN expands one solution into diverse VLA training trajectories. More generated demonstrations improve policy performance, agent-aided diversification helps held-out variations, and a VLA fine-tuned only on generated simulation data completes a real-robot long-horizon task.
summary.zh: 论文研究编码代理能否解决长时程灵巧机器人任务，并将验证过的程序化解法转化为通用策略训练数据。作者构建EMBODIEDSWE-BENCH仿真基准，覆盖接触操作、可变形物体及最长需连续交互半小时的任务；发现前沿编码代理可完成复杂任务，并将经验迁移到其他任务和形态，但通常需要大量迭代，且解法专用于具体任务实例。为扩展监督，EMBODIEDSWE-GEN将单个解法扩增为多样轨迹。作者报告示范增多可提升VLA表现，代理辅助多样化改善未见变化泛化，且仅用代理生成的仿真示范微调的VLA完成了一项真实机器人长任务。

items.title: EmbodiedSWE: Coding Agents for Long Horizon Dexterous Robotics

items.intro: arXiv:2609.30533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose ST-pRRTC, a GPU-parallel space- time RRT-Connect motion planner for problems with known obstacle trajectories and unspecified arrival time. Searching over many arrival times broadens temporal coverage but divides a finite planning budget among more backward trees. To address the challenge, ST-pRRTC builds a shared forward tree and an adaptive forest of backward goal-time trees. Its interval root formulation samples goal arrival times continuously and guarantees probabilistic completeness and asymptotic arrival- time

sections.text:
We propose ST-pRRTC, a GPU-parallel space- time RRT-Connect motion planner for problems with known obstacle trajectories and unspecified arrival time. Searching over many arrival times broadens temporal coverage but divides a finite planning budget among more backward trees.

To address the challenge, ST-pRRTC builds a shared forward tree and an adaptive forest of backward goal-time trees. Its interval root formulation samples goal arrival times continuously and guarantees probabilistic completeness and asymptotic arrival- time optimality under the stated assumptions in a bounded time domain.

The practical root recycling policy has no such guar- antees. It adapts a fixed number of backward trees, replacing later roots while retaining useful search progress.

Experiments on three dynamic benchmarks show that both variants achieve lower mean first-solution times and earlier mean final arrivals than ST-RRT* and SI-RRT on problems solved by all compared methods. Further experiments demonstrate the benefit of recy- cling over broad arrival-time ranges.

Real-robot demonstrations show root-recycling ST-pRRTC planning motions for a UR5e among moving Crazyflie quadrotors.

summary.en: When obstacle trajectories are known but arrival time is unspecified, searching many possible arrival times spreads a finite planning budget across backward trees. ST-pRRTC is a GPU-parallel space-time RRT-Connect planner with a shared forward tree and an adaptive forest of backward goal-time trees. Its interval-root formulation samples arrival times continuously and provides probabilistic completeness and asymptotic arrival-time optimality under stated assumptions in a bounded time domain. A practical root-recycling variant retains useful progress but has no such guarantees. On three dynamic benchmarks, both variants improve first-solution time and final arrival time versus ST-RRT* and SI-RRT on commonly solved cases; root recycling is also demonstrated with a UR5e among moving Crazyflie drones.
summary.zh: 动态障碍物轨迹已知但到达时间不确定时，规划器若覆盖更多到达时刻，会把有限计算预算分散到更多反向搜索树。ST-pRRTC采用GPU并行时空RRT-Connect，共享一棵正向树并构建自适应的目标时刻反向树集合；连续采样到达时刻的区间根版本，在有界时间域及所述假设下提供概率完备性和渐近到达时间最优性。实际根回收策略会替换较晚根、保留有效搜索进度，但不具备这些保证。三个动态基准上，两种版本在共同求解的问题中比ST-RRT*和SI-RRT首次解更快、最终到达更早；UR5e与移动Crazyflie间的真实演示使用根回收版本。

items.title: ST-pRRTC: Parallel Space-Time RRT-C with Adaptive Goal-Time Forests

items.intro: arXiv:2609.31211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Underwater robotic inspection depends on acquiring views that reveal task-relevant structure. For a structurally complex coral colony, recognising the target is only the starting point: the robot must select and execute a viewing motion suited to the inspection task. We present CoralPlan, a vision-language system that selects an observation skill from a current camera image and task text supplied by an episode manifest. A shared motion interface executes orbit, patch, or survey as

sections.text:
Underwater robotic inspection depends on acquiring views that reveal task-relevant structure. For a structurally complex coral colony, recognising the target is only the starting point: the robot must select and execute a viewing motion suited to the inspection task.

We present CoralPlan, a vision-language system that selects an observation skill from a current camera image and task text supplied by an episode manifest. A shared motion interface executes orbit, patch, or survey as target-relative trajectories; the remaining plan fields provide operator guidance.

Observation completion requires target keeping and primitive-specific coverage, while joint success also requires selection to match the recorded reference. We evaluate this interface in 144 simulated episodes and 36 matched simulation-hardware pairs.

In a clear-water pool with external target-reference poses, hardware observation completion reaches 77.8% and joint success reaches 63.9%.The experiments identify both reference-mismatched completions and incomplete observations after a matching skill selection.

These results connect observation-skill choice to measurable underwater execution outcomes and identify where task-directed acquisition succeeds or fails.

summary.en: Underwater coral inspection requires selecting and executing a viewing motion suited to the task, beyond simply recognizing a target. CoralPlan selects an orbit, patch, or survey observation skill from a camera image and task text, then executes target-relative trajectories through a shared interface. Completion requires keeping the target in view and meeting skill-specific coverage; joint success also requires agreement with a recorded reference selection. Evaluation includes 144 simulated episodes and 36 matched simulation-hardware pairs. In a clear-water pool with external target poses, the authors report 77.8% hardware observation completion and 63.9% joint success, identifying both incomplete observations and reference-mismatched completions.
summary.zh: 水下珊瑚检查不仅要识别目标，还需为任务选择并执行合适的观察动作。CoralPlan根据相机图像和任务文本选择环绕、局部拍摄或巡查技能，再由共享运动接口执行相对目标的轨迹；观察完成要求持续保持目标并达到技能特定覆盖，联合成功还要求所选技能与记录参考一致。评估包括144次仿真和36组仿真—硬件配对。在清水池及外部目标参考位姿条件下，作者报告硬件观察完成率77.8%、联合成功率63.9%，并发现失败既包括技能选对但观察不完整，也包括完成观察却与参考技能不匹配。

items.title: CoralPlan: Observation Skill Selection and Execution for Underwater Robotic Inspection

items.intro: arXiv:2609.31117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Service robots remain difficult to deploy in domestic environments, partly because fully autonomous operation is not yet reliable in unpredictable surroundings, and partly because conventional control methods remain inaccessible to novice users. Extended Reality (XR) enables operators to visualize robot information overlaid onto the real world and to interact with augmented elements. Yet, common XR control methods, such as motion controllers and hand gestures, are still perceived as unintuitive. This paper presents a

sections.text:
Service robots remain difficult to deploy in domestic environments, partly because fully autonomous operation is not yet reliable in unpredictable surroundings, and partly because conventional control methods remain inaccessible to novice users.

Extended Reality (XR) enables operators to visualize robot information overlaid onto the real world and to interact with augmented elements. Yet, common XR control methods, such as motion controllers and hand gestures, are still perceived as unintuitive.

This paper presents a control interface that uses a commercial XR pen to command a semi-autonomous mobile robot in Augmented Reality (AR): the operator points at a position in the room, selects it, and drags an augmented arrow to set the desired orientation of the robot at this destination.

Two additional interfaces, based on the XR motion controllers and hand gestures, were developed within the same framework.

To assess the performance and users' perception of these interfaces, and of the XR pen in particular, a study with 10 participants compared four control methods, i.e., the XR pen, the XR motion controllers, hand gestures, and a computer-based baseline RViz, in navigation tasks performed in a home-like environment.

Results show that the XR pen significantly outperforms the other methods in task selection time with the most consistent selections, and that the XR motion controllers obtain the best perceived workload and usability scores, ahead of the computer-based baseline, supporting XR-based control as an intuitive alternative for novice users.

However, technical limitations in the integration of the recently released XR pen currently hold back its user experience.

summary.en: Unpredictable domestic environments challenge full autonomy, while conventional robot controls can be inaccessible to novices. This study presents an augmented-reality interface using a commercial XR pen: operators point to a destination and drag an overlay arrow to set the robot's final orientation. It is compared with XR motion controllers, hand gestures, and an RViz computer interface. Ten participants perform navigation tasks in a home-like setting. The authors report that the pen yields significantly faster and more consistent task selection, while motion controllers receive the best perceived workload and usability scores. Technical limitations in pen integration still constrain the user experience.
summary.zh: 家居环境不可预测，使服务机器人全自主运行仍不可靠，传统操控方式对新手也不够直观。论文提出用商用XR笔在增强现实中操控半自主移动机器人：用户指向并选择房间位置，再拖动增强箭头设定机器人到达后的朝向；研究同时比较XR手柄、手势和RViz电脑界面。10名参与者在类家庭环境完成导航任务。作者报告XR笔的任务选择时间显著优于其他方式且选择最一致；XR手柄的主观工作负荷和易用性评分最高。XR笔集成的技术限制仍影响体验，因此结果不等于界面已无障碍可用。

items.title: Comparative Evaluation of an XR Pen-based Control Interface for Semi-Autonomous Mobile Robot Navigation in Service Environments

Unlike standard diffusion-based planners that rely on zero-mean, isotropic Gaussian corruption, we introduce task-conditioned structured Gaussians whose means and covariances are derived from Gaussian Process Motion Planning (GPMP), explicitly encoding trajectory smoothness and task semantics in the prior. We first formulate diffusion under a task-conditioned, non-isotropic Gaussian prior with closed-form forward and posterior expressions. Building on

sections.text:
We propose Structured-Diffuser, a diffusion planner that embeds task and motion structure directly into the noise model.

Unlike standard diffusion-based planners that rely on zero-mean, isotropic Gaussian corruption, we introduce task-conditioned structured Gaussians whose means and covariances are derived from Gaussian Process Motion Planning (GPMP), explicitly encoding trajectory smoothness and task semantics in the prior.

We first formulate diffusion under a task-conditioned, non-isotropic Gaussian prior with closed-form forward and posterior expressions. Building on this formulation, our hierarchical design separates prior instantiation from trajectory denoising.

At the upper level, sparse task-centric key states and timings are obtained, which instantiate a structured Gaussian prior (mean and covariance).At the lower level, the full trajectory is denoised under this prior, treating the upper-level outputs as noisy observations.

Experiments across three motion-planning tasks show improved task success and training efficiency, with additional gains in data efficiency, trajectory smoothness, and position--velocity consistency where evaluated.

Ablation studies further show that explicitly structuring the corruption process provides benefits beyond neurally conditioning the denoising network alone. Overall, our approach concentrates the prior's probability mass around task-relevant, temporally structured trajectories. We additionally demonstrate deployment on a physical G1 humanoid.

summary.en: Standard diffusion planners often corrupt trajectories with isotropic Gaussian noise, omitting task semantics and motion structure. Structured-Diffuser derives task-conditioned Gaussian means and covariances from Gaussian Process Motion Planning, encoding smoothness and task information directly in the noise prior. Its hierarchy first selects sparse task-centric states and timings to instantiate the prior, then denoises the full trajectory under it. Across three motion-planning tasks, the authors report better task success and training efficiency, with gains in data efficiency, smoothness, and position-velocity consistency where measured. Ablations indicate benefits beyond conditioning the denoiser; deployment on a physical G1 humanoid is also reported.
summary.zh: 标准扩散规划器通常从零均值各向同性高斯噪声恢复轨迹，未显式体现任务语义和运动平滑性。Structured-Diffuser以高斯过程运动规划生成均值与协方差，构造任务条件的结构化高斯噪声先验，并分层处理先验实例化与轨迹去噪：上层选择稀疏关键状态和时刻，下层在先验下恢复完整轨迹。三个运动规划任务实验中，作者报告任务成功率和训练效率提升，并在相应评估中改善数据效率、平滑度及位置—速度一致性；消融显示结构化噪声本身有额外收益。摘要还称在实体G1人形机器人上进行部署演示。

items.title: Structured-Diffuser: Diffusion with Task-Conditioned Structured Priors for Motion Planning

items.intro: arXiv:2609.30959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human demonstrations are a cheap source of data for dexterous manipulation, but co-training a robot policy on them requires closing the human--robot gap in every modality the policy consumes. We present VisTacAlign, a framework for co-training 3D-visual-tactile dexterous policies on human and robot demonstrations. Glove-tracked human hand motion is retargeted to a 17-DoF tactile robot hand with a one-time fingertip correction. The human hand is then erased from both stereo views and replaced

sections.text:
Human demonstrations are a cheap source of data for dexterous manipulation, but co-training a robot policy on them requires closing the human--robot gap in every modality the policy consumes. We present VisTacAlign, a framework for co-training 3D-visual-tactile dexterous policies on human and robot demonstrations.

Glove-tracked human hand motion is retargeted to a 17-DoF tactile robot hand with a one-time fingertip correction.

The human hand is then erased from both stereo views and replaced by a posed robot-hand mesh painted with pixels from robot recordings, and a real-time stereo foundation model is re-run on the composite, so the human point clouds carry the same stereo errors and visibility as the robot ones.

Finally, a capacitive tactile glove is aligned to the robot's fingertip sensors in its signal space, giving one interpretable per-finger force representation. A diffusion transformer consumes point-cloud, proprioceptive, and per-finger tactile tokens.

On three real-world tasks requiring precise force -- Lego assembly, plucking strawberries of varying size, and activating and lifting a power drill -- adding aligned human demonstrations to existing robot data improves over robot-only policies, and ablations show that both tactile input and visual alignment are necessary.

Project page: https://vis-tac-align.github.io

summary.en: Human demonstrations can provide dexterous-manipulation data, but co-training must bridge human-robot gaps in every input modality. VisTacAlign retargets glove-tracked motion to a 17-DoF tactile robot hand, corrects fingertips, replaces the human hand in stereo images with a rendered robot hand, and reruns stereo estimation so human point clouds share robot-like visibility and errors. Capacitive glove signals are aligned with robot fingertip forces. A diffusion transformer consumes point-cloud, proprioceptive, and tactile inputs. On real Lego assembly, strawberry plucking, and power-drill tasks, aligned human demonstrations improve over robot-only data; ablations indicate both tactile input and visual alignment are needed.
summary.zh: 灵巧操作示范可来自人类，但机器人策略若使用视觉和触觉，就需缩小两种形态在各模态上的差异。VisTacAlign将手套追踪的人手动作重定向到17自由度触觉机器人手，修正指尖位置；再将人手从双目图像中替换为机器人手模型，并重新估计点云，使人类数据具有与机器人相近的遮挡和立体视觉误差；电容触觉手套信号也映射到机器人指尖力表示。扩散Transformer融合点云、本体感觉和逐指触觉。在乐高装配、采草莓和操作电钻三项真实任务中，作者报告加入对齐的人类示范优于仅机器人数据，消融显示触觉和视觉对齐均必要。

items.title: VisTacAlign: Co-Training Dexterous Policies on Tactile Human and Robot Demonstrations

Particularly in tasks that demand quick and proactive feedback, robots must recognize human actions as early as possible from incomplete observations. \textit{Sub-actions} offer the semantic and hierarchical cues needed for this, since human actions are inherently structured and can be decomposed into smaller, meaningful units. However, conventional approaches focus primarily on holistic actions and often overlook the rich semantic structure

sections.text:
Understanding human actions is critical for advancing behavior analysis in human-robot interaction.

Particularly in tasks that demand quick and proactive feedback, robots must recognize human actions as early as possible from incomplete observations. \textit{Sub-actions} offer the semantic and hierarchical cues needed for this, since human actions are inherently structured and can be decomposed into smaller, meaningful units.

However, conventional approaches focus primarily on holistic actions and often overlook the rich semantic structure embedded in sub-actions, making them poorly suited for early recognition.

To address this gap, we introduce SASI (Sub-Action Semantics Integrated cross-modal fusion), a novel framework that integrates existing graph convolution networks to fuse spatiotemporal features with sub-action semantics.

SASI exploits a segmentation model with a traditional skeleton-based graph convolution network, capturing both fine-grained sub-action semantics and overall spatial context, while operating in real-time at 29 Hz.

Experiments on BABEL, a skeleton-based dataset with frame-level annotations, demonstrate that our method improves recognition accuracy over conventional approaches, with additional gains expected as the quality of sub-action segmentation improves.

Notably, SASI also achieves superior performance in understanding partial action sequences, revealing its capability for early recognition, which is essential for proactive and seamless Human-Robot Interaction (HRI).Code is available at https://github.com/SavickTso/SASI .

summary.en: Proactive human-robot interaction requires recognizing actions early from incomplete observations, yet conventional methods often focus on whole actions and overlook sub-action structure. SASI fuses sub-action semantics with spatiotemporal features using an action segmentation model and a skeleton-based graph convolution network, combining fine-grained cues with broader spatial context. It operates at a reported 29 Hz. On BABEL, a skeleton dataset with frame-level annotations, the authors report improved accuracy over conventional approaches and stronger recognition of partial action sequences. They expect better segmentation to help further, but provide no numerical accuracy figures or physical robot evaluation in the abstract.
summary.zh: 在人机交互中，机器人需要从不完整观察尽早识别人的动作，但传统识别多关注整体动作，忽略具有层次语义的子动作。SASI将子动作语义与时空特征跨模态融合，结合动作分段模型和基于骨架的图卷积网络，利用局部子动作线索及整体空间上下文进行识别，报告实时运行速度为29Hz。作者在带逐帧标注的BABEL骨架数据集上测试，称其识别准确率优于传统方法，对部分动作序列也有较好表现；摘要指出分段质量提高可能进一步带来收益，但没有给出具体准确率数值或实体机器人测试。

items.title: SASI: Leveraging Sub-Action Semantics for Robust Early Action Recognition in Human-Robot Interaction
