CognitiveReality turns a robot's RGB-D stream into a live, semantically indexed Gaussian-TSDF map shared by an operator in virtual reality and a tool-using language agent. One mapper binary serves any platform through configuration alone: it ingests poses from robot

sections.text:
A photorealistic 3D view tells a teleoperator where a robot is, but not what the scene contains, how well each object has been observed, or how to turn pointing and speech into robot action.

CognitiveReality turns a robot's RGB-D stream into a live, semantically indexed Gaussian-TSDF map shared by an operator in virtual reality and a tool-using language agent.

One mapper binary serves any platform through configuration alone: it ingests poses from robot SLAM, joint kinematics, motion capture or an inline visual tracker, bridges localization outages with a shadow tracker and keyframe-anchored PnP, and maintains open-vocabulary instance identities with per-object quality at 2 Hz.

Speech and controller rays are grounded against persistent scene objects through validated typed tools and operator-confirmed robot actions. In the controlled agent evaluation, the deployed local Qwen3-VL-8B router reaches 81.24\% tool exact match, while merge-aware replay correctly redirects 101 absorbed object identifiers.

On robot data CognitiveReality exceeds a Gaussian-plus-SDF baseline by 2-8 dB; pose error through 5-40 s SLAM outages stays within 1-8 cm. Deployed live on two quadrupeds, the agent executed 26 of 30 navigation requests and 20 of 20 re-observation requests, raising object quality by 2-5 dB.

summary.en: Photorealistic teleoperation views show robot location but may not convey scene semantics, observation quality, or how speech and pointing map to actions. CognitiveReality turns RGB-D streams into a shared semantically indexed Gaussian-TSDF map for a VR operator and tool-using language agent. It adapts to platforms through configuration and bridges localization outages with shadow tracking and keyframe-anchored pose estimation. Speech and controller rays are grounded to persistent objects through validated tools, with operator confirmation for robot actions. The authors report 81.24% tool exact match, improved reconstruction metrics over a Gaussian-plus-SDF baseline, and live navigation and re-observation requests on two quadrupeds.
summary.zh: 遥操作的逼真三维视图能显示机器人位置，却未必呈现场景语义、物体观测质量或如何将指向和语音转成动作。CognitiveReality将机器人RGB-D流转为共享的语义高斯—TSDF地图，供VR操作员与语言代理共同使用，借助配置适配不同机器人，并以影子跟踪和关键帧定位应对定位中断。语音及控制器射线经工具校验后关联持久物体，机器人动作由操作员确认。作者报告代理工具匹配率81.24%，机器人数据重建指标高于高斯加SDF基线；两台四足机器人上执行了导航及重新观察请求，SLAM中断时位姿误差维持在所述厘米范围。

items.title: CognitiveReality: Robot-Agnostic Semantic Gaussian Mapping with an LLM Agent for Immersive Collaborative VR Teleoperation

items.intro: arXiv:2609.30715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learned robot policies produce actions, but their outputs alone do not establish whether execution is progressing as intended. Robot execution monitoring requires identifying the current execution phase, detecting failures, and recognizing task completion from observations available during execution. Training such monitors requires annotations that are scarce in datasets collected for robot-policy learning. sections.text:
Learned robot policies produce actions, but their outputs alone do not establish whether execution is progressing as intended. Robot execution monitoring requires identifying the current execution phase, detecting failures, and recognizing task completion from observations available during execution.

Training such monitors requires annotations that are scarce in datasets collected for robot-policy learning. We present RoboMonitor, a label-efficient vision--language execution monitor that learns from these datasets before introducing monitoring supervision.

We pre-train on 25 hours of multi-camera trajectories spanning 12 manipulation tasks and two robot embodiments, using action-conditioned future-feature prediction, inverse dynamics, and masked-present prediction.

We then transfer the learned visual and context encoders to a causal monitor and apply temporal supervised fine-tuning (Temporal SFT), which combines supervision throughout each observation window with consistency objectives within and across overlapping windows. At deployment, RoboMonitor requires only the task instruction and camera observations.

On a four-task monitoring benchmark, RoboMonitor trained with 52 labeled episodes achieves 93.1% mean phase accuracy and 85.9% macro recall over two fine-tuning seeds, exceeding Qwen3-VL and Robometer trained with the same monitoring supervision. Its phase accuracy also exceeds that of both Qwen3-VL and Robometer trained with 100 episodes.

A Qwen3-VL ablation shows that Temporal SFT reduces mean spurious phase switching from 15.23% to 4.95%.In closed-loop deployment, the integrated system completes 39 of 40 simulated Toolbox Sorting trials and 35 of 40 real-world Reel Packing trials, with no false recovery triggers observed.

summary.en: Robot execution monitoring must identify task phase, failure, and completion, but policy datasets rarely include such labels. RoboMonitor pretrains visual and context encoders on 25 hours of multi-camera trajectories across 12 tasks and two embodiments, using future-feature prediction, inverse dynamics, and masked-present prediction. The encoders are transferred to a causal monitor with temporal supervised fine-tuning across overlapping observation windows; deployment needs only task instructions and camera images. With 52 labeled episodes on a four-task benchmark, the authors report 93.1% mean phase accuracy and 85.9% macro recall. Closed-loop trials complete 39/40 simulated sorting and 35/40 real reel-packing tasks, with no observed false recovery triggers.
summary.zh: 机器人执行监测需识别当前阶段、失败和任务完成，但策略数据通常缺少监测标注。RoboMonitor先在25小时、涵盖12项操作任务和两种机器人形态的多摄像头轨迹上，以未来特征预测、逆动力学和当前帧掩码预测预训练，再将编码器迁移至因果监测器并用跨观察窗口的时间监督微调；部署只需指令和相机图像。四任务基准中，使用52条标注轨迹时，作者报告阶段准确率93.1%、宏平均召回率85.9%，高于相同监督量的比较方法；闭环系统完成模拟分拣39/40次及真实绕线任务35/40次，未观察到误触发恢复。

items.title: RoboMonitor: Label-Efficient Runtime Monitoring of Robot Task Execution via Predictive Representation Learning

However, despite research suggesting that a person may have a different prioritization of objectives depending on time-varying factors such as the environment, their mood, or energy levels, existing HILO approaches only consider a single objective or enforce a fixed weighting on a set of objectives. Neither approach is capable

sections.text:
Human-in-the-loop optimization (HILO) is a common approach for optimizing the control of assistive devices to account for the wearer's unique biomechanics and subjective preferences.

However, despite research suggesting that a person may have a different prioritization of objectives depending on time-varying factors such as the environment, their mood, or energy levels, existing HILO approaches only consider a single objective or enforce a fixed weighting on a set of objectives.

Neither approach is capable of representing an individual's preferences over objectives. In this work, we propose Multi-Objective Human-in-the-loop Bayesian Optimization (MO-HILBO), which builds on explicit multi-objective Bayesian optimization to efficiently infer a personalized set of Pareto-optimal controllers.

We compare our approach with an existing multi-objective HILO method and experimentally demonstrate MO-HILBO on a lower-limb exoskeleton across two objectives: metabolic cost (efficiency) and ordinal human feedback (comfort).

We find that MO-HILBO （1） discovers Pareto-optimal controllers, and （2） that the pairwise ordering of points on the Pareto front itself is consistent with validation trials. Lastly, we open-source mohilo, a Python package for running both HILO and MO-HILBO on wearable devices: https://dynamicmobility.github.io/mohilo/.

summary.en: Human-in-the-loop optimization for assistive devices must balance objectives such as efficiency and comfort, whose priorities may vary over time. Existing methods often optimize one objective or impose fixed weights. MO-HILBO uses explicit multi-objective Bayesian optimization to infer a personalized Pareto set of controllers. The authors compare it with an existing multi-objective HILO method and test it on a lower-limb exoskeleton using metabolic cost and ordinal comfort feedback. They report discovering Pareto-optimal controllers, with pairwise ordering along the Pareto front consistent with validation trials. The abstract gives no numerical improvement in metabolic cost or comfort.
summary.zh: 辅助设备的人体在环优化需兼顾穿戴者效率、舒适度等目标，而固定目标或固定权重难以表达个人随环境、情绪或精力变化的偏好。MO-HILBO以多目标贝叶斯优化从交互中推断个性化帕累托控制器集合，并与既有多目标人体在环方法比较。作者在下肢外骨骼上以代谢成本和序数舒适反馈为两个目标进行实验，报告方法能发现帕累托最优控制器，且帕累托前沿点的两两排序与验证试验一致。研究聚焦所测外骨骼和两个目标，摘要未报告具体代谢或舒适度改善幅度。

items.title: Multi-Objective Human-in-the-Loop Bayesian Optimization of a Lower-Limb Exoskeleton

One of the core problems at present is to coordinate multiple robots to complete the unwinding operation in a highly constrained environment. The existing distributed training framework faces some observability challenges in high-density barrier and unstable environments, resulting

sections.text:
In the field of precision manufacturing in complex constrained environments, the role of soft robots is increasingly prominent, and the realization of anti-winding control based on multi-intelligent body reinforcement learning has become a research hotspot.

One of the core problems at present is to coordinate multiple robots to complete the unwinding operation in a highly constrained environment. The existing distributed training framework faces some observability challenges in high-density barrier and unstable environments, resulting in poor learning results.

This paper proposes a topology-driven Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (TD-MARL) framework to coordinate multi-robot systems to avoid entanglement.

Specifically, the critical network adopts centralized learning, so that each intelligent body can perceive the strategies of other intelligent bodies by sharing the topological state, thus alleviating the training instability caused by complex interactions; eliminating the demand for communication resources between robots through distributed execution, Upgrade system reliability; the integrated topological security layer uses topological invariants to accurately assess and mitigate the risk of entanglement to avoid the strategy from falling into local difficulties.

Finally, the full simulation experiments carried out in the real simulation environment show that the method is better than the current advanced deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method in terms of convergence and anti-winding effect.

summary.en: Coordinating multiple robots to avoid entanglement in constrained environments is difficult when dense obstacles and instability limit observability. The paper proposes topology-driven multi-agent reinforcement learning (TD-MARL). Centralized training shares topological state so agents can account for one another's strategies; execution is distributed to reduce inter-robot communication. A topological safety layer assesses and mitigates entanglement risk. Experiments in a simulation environment are reported to show better convergence and anti-entanglement performance than current deep reinforcement learning methods. The abstract provides no numerical metrics and describes no validation on physical soft robots.
summary.zh: 高密度障碍和不稳定环境会增加多机器人协同解缠任务的可观测性与训练难度。论文提出拓扑驱动多智能体强化学习框架TD-MARL，通过集中训练共享拓扑状态，使各策略感知其他智能体行为；执行阶段分布式运行以减少机器人间通信，并加入拓扑安全层评估和缓解缠绕风险。作者在仿真环境中进行实验，报告相较当时先进深度强化学习方法，收敛性和抗缠绕效果更好。摘要中的系统描述和评估均指仿真，未报告真实软体机器人硬件验证或定量指标。

items.title: Topology-Driven Anti-Entanglement Control for Soft Robots

As such, we introduce MR. POP, a GPU-based a.s.a.o. multi-robot planner based on dRRT and the AO-x meta-algorithm. MR. POP uses large-scale GPU-based SIMT-parallelism to simultaneously

sections.text:
Finding globally optimal paths remains a fundamental challenge in multi-robot motion planning. Despite acceleration of almost-surely asymptotically optimal (a.s.a.o.) planners via CPU-based parallelism, achieving both probabilistic convergence guarantees and strong computational performance, these algorithms still struggle to scale to multi-robot settings.

As such, we introduce MR. POP, a GPU-based a.s.a.o. multi-robot planner based on dRRT and the AO-x meta-algorithm. MR. POP uses large-scale GPU-based SIMT-parallelism to simultaneously run hundreds of roadmap construction and tree search iterations with underlying parallel nearest neighbor search and collision checking operations.

We show that this enables MR. POP to become the only planner achieving a 100% solve rate while being faster than state-of-the-art a.s.a.o. planners in multi-robot systems up to 35-DOF. MR. POP also raises the success rate of downstream motion optimizers (e.g., from 4% to 72%), by creating high-quality, diverse seeds that help avoid local minima.

summary.en: Multi-robot motion planning must scale to high-dimensional systems while retaining probabilistic convergence guarantees of asymptotically optimal planners. MR. POP combines dRRT with the AO-x meta-algorithm and uses GPU SIMT parallelism for roadmap construction, tree search, nearest-neighbor queries, and collision checks. The authors report that, for systems up to 35 degrees of freedom, it is the only evaluated planner with a 100% solve rate while also running faster than state-of-the-art asymptotically optimal planners. Diverse, high-quality seeds raise a downstream optimizer's example success rate from 4% to 72%. The abstract does not describe physical robot trials.
summary.zh: 多机器人运动规划既要扩展到高自由度系统，也希望保留渐近最优规划的概率收敛性质。MR. POP将dRRT与AO-x结合，利用GPU大规模SIMT并行同时构建路线图、执行树搜索及近邻查询和碰撞检查。作者报告在最高35自由度的多机器人系统中，它是唯一达到100%求解率且快于所比较渐近最优规划器的方法；生成质量较高且多样的初始解，还使下游运动优化器成功率示例从4%升至72%。这些是论文所测规划任务结果，摘要未描述实体机器人执行。

items.title: MR. POP: Multi-Robot Parallel Optimizing Planner for Almost-Surely Asymptotically Optimal Planning

We propose an interaction-centric framework that leverages the shared structure of two-finger grippers via a parameterized universal gripper abstraction, yielding a canonical gripper-frame representation. sections.text:
Achieving robust cross-embodiment generalization in imitation learning demands overcoming a critical representation flaw that inextricably entangles task semantics with hardware-specific visual geometry.

We propose an interaction-centric framework that leverages the shared structure of two-finger grippers via a parameterized universal gripper abstraction, yielding a canonical gripper-frame representation.

Given language and RGB-D observations, a VLM infers the subtask and grounds an interaction triplet (gripper, held, target), while SAM~2.1 tracks masks to reduce VLM queries.

We design concise hybrid features that combine target/collision artificial potential fields for global guidance with segmented gripper-frame point clouds for local geometry, and use a Flow-Matching Transformer to predict smooth 7-DoF action chunks.

Experiments in simulation and real-world tasks demonstrate that ours is the first imitation learning approach to simultaneously achieve competitive benchmark scores and extreme cross-embodiment/cross-viewpoint zero-shot sim-to-real transfer to completely distinct, heterogeneous robot platforms.

summary.en: Cross-embodiment imitation learning can entangle task semantics with hardware-specific visual geometry. This framework builds a canonical representation around a parameterized universal two-finger gripper. From language and RGB-D observations, a VLM grounds a gripper-held-target interaction, while SAM 2.1 tracks masks to reduce VLM queries. Hybrid features combine target and collision potential fields with segmented gripper-frame point clouds; a flow-matching transformer predicts smooth 7-DoF action chunks. Simulation and real-world experiments are reported to demonstrate zero-shot sim-to-real transfer across distinct robot platforms and viewpoints, though the abstract provides no detailed metrics or platform count.
summary.zh: 模仿学习的跨形态泛化常把任务语义与硬件视觉几何纠缠在一起。论文提出面向双指夹爪的交互中心框架，以参数化通用夹爪建立规范坐标表示；视觉语言模型根据语言和RGB-D观察推断子任务及夹爪、持有物、目标三元关系，SAM 2.1跟踪掩码以减少模型查询。混合特征结合目标与碰撞人工势场及夹爪坐标系点云，再由流匹配Transformer生成平滑七自由度动作块。作者称仿真与真实任务实现了对异构平台和视角的零样本仿真到现实迁移，但摘要未给具体指标或平台数量。

items.title: Enabling a Unified Cross-Domain Representation for Two-Finger Gripper Manipulation via Interaction-Centric Modeling

items.intro: arXiv:2609.30704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human spatial attention is widely conceptualized as being guided by a priority map that integrates perceptual salience, current goals, and past experiences. Here, we extend priority-based computation to movement control in artificial agents. We first introduce a lightweight model of visual search based on an integrated priority map. Trained on human saccades, it reproduced key behavioral patterns, including oculomotor suppression and history-driven selection. Extending the search model, we equipped an artificial agent with

sections.text:
Human spatial attention is widely conceptualized as being guided by a priority map that integrates perceptual salience, current goals, and past experiences. Here, we extend priority-based computation to movement control in artificial agents. We first introduce a lightweight model of visual search based on an integrated priority map.

Trained on human saccades, it reproduced key behavioral patterns, including oculomotor suppression and history-driven selection. Extending the search model, we equipped an artificial agent with a priority field and evaluated its performance in a reach-avoid task that required reaching a goal destination while avoiding moving obstacles.

Compared with alternative architectures, priority-field agents trained more efficiently and performed better in unseen, complex scenarios, even from simple demonstrations. Adding a simple memory mechanism also produced human-like, history-driven effects in anticipating the likely location of the upcoming goal.

These findings suggest that priority-based computation may provide a promising foundation for movement control in artificial agents.

summary.en: The paper extends human priority-map accounts of spatial attention to movement control in artificial agents. A lightweight visual-search model trained on human saccades integrates perceptual salience, goals, and history, reproducing reported patterns such as oculomotor suppression and history-driven selection. The authors then apply a priority field to a reach-avoid task with moving obstacles. Compared with alternative architectures, priority-field agents train more efficiently and perform better in unseen complex scenarios, even from simple demonstrations. Adding a simple memory produces history-dependent anticipation of likely goal locations. The results suggest a possible basis for movement control; no physical robot evaluation is described.
summary.zh: 论文将人类视觉注意中的优先级图思想扩展到人工智能体的运动控制。作者先以人类眼跳数据训练整合显著性、目标和历史信息的视觉搜索模型，报告其复现眼动抑制和历史驱动选择等行为；随后把优先级场用于需到达目标并避开移动障碍的趋近—避障任务。相较其他架构，优先级场智能体训练更高效，在未见复杂场景表现更好，即使示范较简单也如此。加入简易记忆后，还出现由历史影响的目标位置预期。研究提示该计算机制可能有助运动控制，摘要未描述实体机器人验证。

items.title: From Visual Search to Movement Control: A Priority Field for Artificial Agents

We compare the two on the Unitree G1 humanoid in NVIDIA Isaac Lab. In the standing mode of a standardized evaluation, the dual-critic run reaches targets 3.5x faster (6.5 vs. 22

sections.text:
Multi-objective reinforcement learning for humanoid robots must coordinate locomotion and manipulation within one policy. A natural design choice is between a single (unified) critic that estimates the combined value of all objectives and separate (dual) critics with disjoint reward signals. We compare the two on the Unitree G1 humanoid in NVIDIA Isaac Lab.

In the standing mode of a standardized evaluation, the dual-critic run reaches targets 3.5x faster (6.5 vs. 22.6 simulation steps), achieves 2x the throughput (14.3 vs. 7.0 validated reaches per 1,000 steps) and a higher validated reach rate (65.2% vs. 53.8%) than the unified-critic run.

That evaluation pins the fingers open for every policy, whereas the unified run had trained driving its own. When the unified run drives its own fingers, with nothing else changed, the standing-mode gap falls from 3.5x to 1.3x in speed and from 2x to 1.1x in throughput. This is a single re-evaluation of a single checkpoint, and we do not generalize from it.

Adding five anti-gaming reward mechanisms to the dual critic did not raise validated reach rate (60.9% vs. 65.2%).

The two runs differ not only in the critic but also in the PPO update rule (one summed advantage under one likelihood ratio, versus a per-stream advantage and a ratio per actor), and further in curriculum, arm action dimensionality, finger control and reward weights; each is a single run.

The measurement therefore cannot separate the critic from the update rule. We argue that critic architecture deserves explicit treatment as a design variable in multi-objective humanoid RL, and specify the single-variable ablation needed to establish its causal contribution.

Code, checkpoints and a project page: https://mturan33.github.io/critic-architecture-matters/

summary.en: This study compares dual and unified critics for multi-objective humanoid locomotion and manipulation on a Unitree G1 in Isaac Lab. In a standardized standing-mode evaluation, the dual-critic run reaches targets 3.5 times faster, achieves about twice the validated-reach throughput, and has a higher validated reach rate. However, all policies had fingers pinned open, unlike the unified run's training setup. Re-evaluating one unified-critic checkpoint with its own finger control narrows the gaps substantially. The runs also differ in PPO updates, curriculum, action dimensions, and reward weights, and each is a single run; the authors therefore cannot isolate a critic effect or generalize causally.
summary.zh: 论文在Isaac Lab中的Unitree G1人形机器人上比较多目标强化学习的双评论家与统一评论家设计。标准站立模式评估中，双评论家运行触达目标快3.5倍、每千步有效触达数约为两倍，验证触达率也较高；但评估把所有策略手指固定张开，而统一评论家训练时控制自身手指。重新评估单个统一评论家检查点并让其控制手指后，速度和吞吐差距明显缩小。两组还同时存在PPO更新、课程、动作维度和奖励权重等差异，各仅一次运行，故无法将结果归因于评论家本身；作者明确不作普遍化结论。

items.title: Critic Architecture Matters: Dual vs. Unified Critics for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

Existing approaches commonly acquire a loco-manipulation policy through reward engineering or demonstrations followed by task-specific training, making it costly to scale to new tasks. sections.text:
For humanoids to be useful in everyday environments, they must perform a wide range of tasks that couple locomotion and manipulation. Existing approaches commonly acquire a loco-manipulation policy through reward engineering or demonstrations followed by task-specific training, making it costly to scale to new tasks.

In this work, we propose a hierarchical approach to humanoid loco-manipulation that eliminates these per-task requirements. HuGo, Humanoid policy code Generation, uses a Large Language Model (LLM) to generate executable, closed-loop high-level policy code from a task description on top of a frozen low-level whole-body policy.

Given the task, observation, and command specifications, the LLM constructs the task logic in code. HuGo then refines the policy from its rollouts using numerical trajectories and selected video frames to produce feedback and targeted code updates.

Across five simulation tasks, using two different low-level policies, HuGo substantially outperforms a high-level reinforcement learning baseline and approaches the performance of a demonstration-based baseline. We achieve this level of performance without task-specific reward design or demonstration collection.

We further demonstrate zero-shot transfer of simulation-generated policies to hardware and show that applying the same refinement loop to real-world rollouts can further improve transfer performance without expert demonstrations or policy retraining. Project website is https://iconlab.negarmehr.com/HuGo/

summary.en: Humanoid loco-manipulation often requires task-specific reward engineering or demonstrations and retraining. HuGo uses an LLM to generate executable closed-loop high-level policy code from task, observation, and command specifications atop a frozen low-level whole-body policy. It refines code using rollout trajectories and selected video frames. Across five simulation tasks and two low-level policies, the authors report substantial gains over a high-level RL baseline and performance approaching a demonstration-based baseline, without task-specific reward design or demonstration collection. They also report zero-shot transfer of simulation-generated policies to hardware and further improvement from real rollouts without expert demonstrations or policy retraining.
summary.zh: 人形机器人执行移动与操作耦合任务，常需为每项任务设计奖励或收集示范并单独训练。HuGo让大语言模型根据任务、观察和命令规格，在冻结的全身低层策略上生成闭环高层策略代码，再依据轨迹数据和选取的视频帧反馈迭代修订代码。作者在五项仿真任务和两种低层策略上评估，报告其显著优于高层强化学习基线、接近示范学习基线，且未进行任务专属奖励设计或示范收集。还报告仿真策略零样本迁移到硬件，并可用真实运行反馈继续改进，无需专家示范或策略重训；摘要未量化硬件效果。

items.title: HuGo: LLMs as Whole-Body Policy Code Designers for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

sections.text:
Model-based control can directly execute specified objectives, while learning can amortize such behaviors into reactive policies, making their combination a natural solution to multi-stage manipulation.

We introduce Semantically UNified (SUN) Programs, typed executables that compile grounded relations into aligned optimal control objectives, satisfaction predicates, and learning rewards. Our harness, Kuafu, equips a foundation model as a task-level agent to orchestrate scene preparation, verification, residual RL, and data production.

The agent uses program feedback to repair candidate programs and training diagnostics to calibrate relative reward weights, retaining accepted task semantics across tool calls. Across nine multi-stage manipulation tasks, Kuafu achieves 82.03% average success rate, significantly outperforming all learned baselines.

Its learned controllers generate demonstrations at 10.57x the human-teleoperation rate, yielding data that improve visualpolicy success by 23.6 percentage points over the strongest baseline. The policies transfer zero-shot to physical Franka and Kinova robots, demonstrating sim-to-real generalization.

summary.en: SUN Programs combine model-based control objectives with learned reactive policies for multi-stage manipulation. Typed programs compile grounded relations into aligned optimal-control objectives, satisfaction predicates, and learning rewards. The Kuafu harness uses a foundation-model agent to orchestrate scene preparation, verification, residual RL, and data production, repairing programs and calibrating reward weights from feedback. Across nine multi-stage tasks, the authors report 82.03% average success, above all learned baselines. Learned controllers generate demonstrations 10.57 times faster than human teleoperation, and those data improve visual-policy success by 23.6 percentage points over the strongest baseline. Zero-shot transfer to physical Franka and Kinova robots is reported.
summary.zh: 多阶段操作可将模型控制的明确目标与学习所得的反应式策略结合。论文提出语义统一程序SUN Programs，把场景关系编译为一致的最优控制目标、满足谓词和学习奖励；Kuafu则以基础模型代理协调场景准备、验证、残差强化学习和数据生成，并依据程序反馈修复程序、依据训练诊断调整奖励权重。九项多阶段操作任务上，作者报告平均成功率82.03%，高于所有学习基线；学得控制器生成示范的速度为人工遥操作的10.57倍，所得数据使视觉策略成功率比最强基线高23.6个百分点。还报告策略零样本迁移至实体Franka和Kinova机器人。

items.title: SUN: Agentic Robot Policy Learning with Persistent Task Programs

In this work, we propose the Future Representation Action Model (FRAM), a small policy that explicitly links the future end-effector trajectory to the current visual input. FRAM uses the image coordinates of the predicted trajectory as spatial pointers and reads local visual features related to the motion from the current image. This organizes the information for action generation

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action models achieve strong performance in robot manipulation, but often require large numbers of parameters. In this work, we propose the Future Representation Action Model (FRAM), a small policy that explicitly links the future end-effector trajectory to the current visual input.

FRAM uses the image coordinates of the predicted trajectory as spatial pointers and reads local visual features related to the motion from the current image. This organizes the information for action generation into the reference position (Where), the visual state (What), and the future motion (Future).

Trajectory labels are generated automatically from demonstrations and camera geometry, so no manual annotation is needed. With 138.7M parameters, including a frozen language encoder, FRAM reaches an average success rate of 92.2% over the four standard LIBERO suites, close to the 94.2% of $\pi_0$ with 3.3B parameters.

Without extra training, it also reaches an average of 67.3% on LIBERO-Plus. Ablations confirm that both the future trajectory and the local visual features improve performance and robustness. On a real dual-arm UR5e, FRAM stacks cups using only wrist cameras, including choosing and switching between the left and right arms.

These results show that selecting visual information based on future motion is an effective way to obtain both high performance and robustness in a small robot policy.

summary.en: Large VLA policies can be costly, so FRAM links predicted future end-effector motion to current visual feature selection in a compact policy. It uses image coordinates of the predicted trajectory as spatial pointers to read local motion-relevant features. Trajectory labels are generated automatically from demonstrations and camera geometry, without manual annotation. With 138.7 million parameters including a frozen language encoder, FRAM reports 92.2% average success across four LIBERO suites, compared with 94.2% for the 3.3-billion-parameter pi0. It achieves 67.3% on LIBERO-Plus without extra training and stacks cups on a real dual-arm UR5e using wrist cameras.
summary.zh: 视觉语言动作策略通常参数量较大，FRAM尝试以未来轨迹引导当前图像特征选择，构建紧凑操作策略。它把预测的末端轨迹图像坐标作为空间指针，从当前图像读取运动相关局部视觉特征；轨迹标签由示范和相机几何自动生成，无需人工标注。138.7百万参数（含冻结语言编码器）的FRAM在四个LIBERO套件平均成功率为92.2%，接近33亿参数π0的94.2%；无需额外训练，在LIBERO-Plus为67.3%。消融支持轨迹和局部特征均有帮助；真实双臂UR5e仅用腕部相机完成叠杯并切换左右臂。

items.title: FRAM: Trajectory-Guided Visual Feature Selection for Compact Language-Conditioned Robot Manipulation

items.intro: arXiv:2609.31225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Contact-rich manipulation requires robots to balance accurate motion tracking with compliant interaction, yet most visual-action policies leave compliance fixed at the controller level. We present Imp-ACT, a methodologically grounded and practical approach to incorporating direction-dependent Cartesian stiffness modulation directly into demonstration collection, without manual stiffness selection or offline target reconstruction. During teleoperation, a self-tuning impedance controller adapts stiffness along the instantaneous direction of motion while maintaining compliance in orthogonal directions. The adapted stiffness

sections.text:
Contact-rich manipulation requires robots to balance accurate motion tracking with compliant interaction, yet most visual-action policies leave compliance fixed at the controller level.

We present Imp-ACT, a methodologically grounded and practical approach to incorporating direction-dependent Cartesian stiffness modulation directly into demonstration collection, without manual stiffness selection or offline target reconstruction.

During teleoperation, a self-tuning impedance controller adapts stiffness along the instantaneous direction of motion while maintaining compliance in orthogonal directions. The adapted stiffness is applied and recorded alongside visual observations and motion commands, capturing motion and compliance under the same dynamics.

We implement this pipeline using Action Chunking with Transformer (ACT) to predict end-effector pose, gripper action, and motion-direction stiffness from visual, proprioceptive, and wrench observations. The performance of Imp-ACT is evaluated on wiping and plug insertion using both success rate and quantitative measures of contact behavior.

Compared with fixed low- and high-stiffness baselines, Imp-ACT achieves comparable or higher success while maintaining low interaction forces. In wiping, it reduces contact-force vibration by approximately $29\times$ relative to the compliant baseline and $180\times$ relative to the stiff baseline.

In plug insertion, it reduces forces orthogonal to the insertion direction by $43\%$ relative to the better fixed-stiffness baseline.

These results highlight the benefit of maintaining sufficient stiffness along the direction needed for task execution while preserving compliance in other directions to limit contact forces and accommodate environmental constraints.

summary.en: Contact-rich manipulation needs accurate motion tracking and compliant interaction, while many visual-action policies fix compliance at the controller level. Imp-ACT adapts Cartesian stiffness along the instantaneous motion direction during teleoperation while remaining compliant orthogonally, recording stiffness together with images and commands. An Action Chunking with Transformer policy predicts end-effector pose, gripper action, and directional stiffness from visual, proprioceptive, and wrench inputs. In wiping and plug insertion, the authors report comparable or higher success than fixed-stiffness baselines with low interaction forces. Wiping force vibration falls about 29-fold and 180-fold versus compliant and stiff baselines; orthogonal insertion forces fall 43% versus the better fixed baseline.
summary.zh: 接触丰富的操作需要既准确跟踪动作，又顺应环境，但视觉动作策略通常把柔顺性固定在控制器层。Imp-ACT在遥操作示范采集时用自调阻抗控制器，沿即时运动方向调节笛卡尔刚度、在正交方向保持柔顺，并同步记录刚度、图像和运动指令；ACT策略再预测末端位姿、夹爪动作及方向刚度。擦拭和插头插入评估中，相较固定刚度基线，作者报告成功率相当或更高且交互力较低；擦拭接触力振动分别比柔顺与刚性基线降低约29倍和180倍，插入时正交方向力比较优固定基线低43%。

items.title: Imp-ACT: Adaptive Impedance Control and Action Chunking with Transformers to Learn Contact-Rich Manipulation from Demonstrations

items.intro: arXiv:2608.06994v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) aim to construct a unified architecture capable of understanding world state evolution and guiding to generative motion planning. However, existing visual branches focus on predicting static visual observation, rather than reflecting potential transition information that captures the evolution of world states under motion interactions. This leads to representational entanglement between high-level physical condition evolution and low-level action trajectory generation within the Action Model, creating a structural bottleneck while weakening

sections.text:
World Action Models (WAMs) aim to construct a unified architecture capable of understanding world state evolution and guiding to generative motion planning.

However, existing visual branches focus on predicting static visual observation, rather than reflecting potential transition information that captures the evolution of world states under motion interactions.

This leads to representational entanglement between high-level physical condition evolution and low-level action trajectory generation within the Action Model, creating a structural bottleneck while weakening the predictive capability of world evolution modeling for action generation.

We propose PILOT (Physical Inference for Latent Optimized Trajectories), whose core Representational Deduction (RD) bridges this gap by integrating motion thought-of-chain (CoT) guidance as a native model capability.

Specifically, RD aims to encourage the action branch to explicitly model potential state transition tokens, which are retained as CoT in the reasoning space to guide fine-grained motion trajectory.

Experiments demonstrate that RD not only significantly improves the success rate and generalization ability of WAMs in complex robotic manipulation tasks but also enhances the model's physical interpretability by decoupling high-level motion semantics from low-level trajectory details.

Furthermore, the abundant state transition supervision signals introduced by RD effectively alleviate the sparse supervision in action generation, enabling it to serve as an efficient few-shot real-robot fine-tuning strategy and demonstrating superior scalability for migration to mainstream WAM architectures.

summary.en: World Action Models may entangle high-level physical state evolution with low-level trajectory generation when visual branches predict only static observations. PILOT introduces Representational Deduction (RD), which encourages the action branch to model potential state-transition tokens as an internal motion chain of thought guiding fine-grained trajectories. The authors report improved success and generalization on complex manipulation, alongside greater physical interpretability through separation of motion semantics from trajectory details. Additional transition supervision is said to alleviate sparse action supervision and support few-shot real-robot fine-tuning. The abstract provides no numerical results or details of physical deployment.
summary.zh: 世界动作模型的视觉分支若只预测静态观察，可能无法表达动作引起的状态变化，进而把高层物理演化与低层轨迹生成纠缠。论文提出PILOT及其表征推演模块RD，将潜在状态转移词元作为模型内的运动思维链，引导细粒度轨迹生成。作者报告该方法提升复杂操作任务成功率和泛化能力，并通过区分运动语义与轨迹细节增强物理可解释性；额外状态转移监督还缓解动作监督稀疏，并支持少样本真实机器人微调。摘要没有列出具体实验数值，也未描述实体部署范围。

items.title: Decoupling Intention from Trajectory: A Representational Deduction Framework for World Action Models

items.intro: arXiv:2609.30036v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Planners built on visual world models commonly score each predicted outcome by its distance to the encoded goal image. We show that this target can limit control even with exact dynamics and globally optimal short-horizon search: reaching a goal may require actions that initially move away from it. With frozen LeWM models, intermediate targets substantially improve action synthesis and recorded-action ranking on Cube, PushT, Reacher, and TwoRoom. Learned targets and targets drawn from

sections.text:
Planners built on visual world models commonly score each predicted outcome by its distance to the encoded goal image. We show that this target can limit control even with exact dynamics and globally optimal short-horizon search: reaching a goal may require actions that initially move away from it.

With frozen LeWM models, intermediate targets substantially improve action synthesis and recorded-action ranking on Cube, PushT, Reacher, and TwoRoom. Learned targets and targets drawn from observed experience both produce these gains.

We introduce Anchored Planning, which retrieves a recorded segment whose start and end resemble the current and goal observations, then aims at an observation shortly after its start. The frozen model scores actions toward this target from the current state.

Without additional training, planning toward observed targets outperforms the LeWM planner on every task in our long-range evaluation. Additional final-goal search falls short of the same gains. Lower successor-prediction error need not translate into better control.

Success also depends on how far ahead the target is placed and on shrinking the retrieval span as execution advances. Changing only the target lets the same frozen model and planner reach goals that final-goal scoring misses.

summary.en: Visual world-model planners often score predicted outcomes by distance to a final goal image, but successful routes may initially move away from the goal. With frozen LeWM models, the authors study intermediate targets and introduce Anchored Planning: retrieve a recorded segment resembling the current and goal observations, then aim at an observation shortly after its start. On Cube, PushT, Reacher, and TwoRoom, intermediate targets improve action synthesis and recorded-action ranking. Without additional training, planning toward observed targets beats final-goal scoring on every task in the long-range evaluation. Performance also depends on target distance and shrinking the retrieval span during execution; lower prediction error alone does not ensure better control.
summary.zh: 视觉世界模型规划器常按预测结果与最终目标图像的距离评分，但到达目标可能需要先朝远离目标的方向运动。论文在冻结LeWM模型上研究中间目标，并提出Anchored Planning：检索起点接近当前观察、终点接近目标的经验片段，再把片段起点之后的短暂观察作为当前规划目标。作者在Cube、PushT、Reacher和TwoRoom任务中报告，中间目标改善动作生成和记录动作排序；无需训练，基于观测经验的目标在所有长程评估任务上优于最终目标评分基线。效果还依赖目标前视距离及随执行缩小检索范围，预测误差更低不必然意味着控制更好。

items.title: Aim Short to Reach Far: Your Frozen World Model Can Plan Better Than You Think

items.intro: arXiv:2609.31323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we study if a robotic hand using proprioception alone can grasp diverse objects with no visual observation. We present a modular dexterous grasping architecture that separates global arm motion from local contact control. An independently controlled arm guides the hand toward the object, while a reinforcement learning policy grasps and stabilizes it using only hand proprioceptive feedback. We call this \textit{a blind grasp reflex}: grasping without images, object poses

sections.text:
In this work we study if a robotic hand using proprioception alone can grasp diverse objects with no visual observation. We present a modular dexterous grasping architecture that separates global arm motion from local contact control.

An independently controlled arm guides the hand toward the object, while a reinforcement learning policy grasps and stabilizes it using only hand proprioceptive feedback. We call this \textit{a blind grasp reflex}: grasping without images, object poses, or geometric observations.

A learned stable-grasp score determines when the object is securely held, allowing the arm to begin post-grasp manipulation. This separation makes grasping a reusable hand-level skill that can be combined with independently designed arm controllers for various manipulation tasks.

Experiments in simulation and on hardware demonstrate robust blind grasping across diverse objects and seamless composition with a range of arm controllers. Moreover, despite never observing contact geometry, the learned grasp score closely aligns with an independent physics-based measure of grasp stability.

The resulting approach follows a simple principle: see to reach, feel to grasp. Project page: https://blindgraspreflex.github.io.

summary.en: This work studies whether a robotic hand can grasp diverse objects using proprioception alone, without visual observations. Its modular architecture separates global arm motion from local contact control: an independently controlled arm approaches the object, while an RL policy uses only hand proprioception to grasp and stabilize it. A learned stable-grasp score determines when the object is secure, allowing the hand-level skill to pair with different arm controllers. Simulation and hardware experiments are reported to show blind grasping across diverse objects and composition with multiple arm controllers. The learned score aligns closely with an independent physics-based grasp-stability measure; no numerical success rate is given.
summary.zh: 论文研究机器人灵巧手能否完全不看视觉，仅凭本体感觉抓取不同物体。所提模块化架构将手臂的大范围接近运动与手部局部接触控制分开：独立手臂控制器把手送近物体，强化学习策略只用手部本体感觉完成抓取与稳定，并以学得的稳定抓握分数判断何时可开始后续操作。由此抓握技能可与不同手臂控制器组合。仿真和硬件实验报告对多种物体均可盲抓，并能与多种手臂控制器组合；稳定分数与独立物理抓握稳定性指标吻合。摘要未提供定量成功率。

items.title: See to Reach, Feel to Grasp: Learning A Blind Grasp Reflex for Anthropomorphic Robotic Hands

To address this limitation, this paper presents a lightweight support-enhanced granular-jamming gripper tailored to a continuum manipulator. The gripper maintains compliance before jamming while establishing a direct load path to the continuum manipulator tip after jamming. To improve its grasping performance, we systematically designed

sections.text:
Continuum manipulators provide dexterous motion in confined spaces, but structural compliance, hysteresis, and load-dependent deformation leave residual position and orientation errors that can undermine reliable contact with rigid grippers.

To address this limitation, this paper presents a lightweight support-enhanced granular-jamming gripper tailored to a continuum manipulator. The gripper maintains compliance before jamming while establishing a direct load path to the continuum manipulator tip after jamming.

To improve its grasping performance, we systematically designed membrane materials, particles, filling ratios, and the internal support structure, and further identify geometry-dependent grasp boundaries with respect to contact offset and object shape.

Building on these results, we construct a physical manipulation system integrating the continuum manipulator, granular-jamming gripper, visual feedback, tendon actuation, and pneumatic control.

We then train a reinforcement-learning-based reaching controller in a randomized simulation and deploy it on the physical system, demonstrating how positioning control and contact level mechanical adaptation can complement each other in a modular grasp-and-release task.

By introducing an adaptive structure that relaxes the need for highly accurate modeling and positioning control, this work explores a design paradigm that integrates physical and embodied intelligence.

summary.en: Continuum arms deform under load and exhibit hysteresis, making reliable contact with rigid grippers difficult. The paper presents a lightweight granular-jamming gripper whose support structure preserves compliance before jamming and creates a direct load path afterward. The authors optimize membrane, particles, filling ratio, and internal support, and examine grasp boundaries across contact offsets and object shapes. A physical system combines the arm, gripper, vision, tendon actuation, and pneumatic control. A reaching controller trained in randomized simulation is deployed on the robot for a modular grasp-and-release task; no quantitative success rate is stated in the abstract.
summary.zh: 针对连续体机械臂存在柔顺、迟滞和负载变形，导致夹持器难以稳定接触的问题，论文设计轻量支撑增强颗粒阻塞夹爪：未阻塞时保持柔顺，阻塞后形成通向机械臂末端的直接载荷路径。作者还优化膜材、颗粒、填充比例和支撑结构，并分析接触偏移及物体形状对应的抓取边界。系统结合视觉、腱驱动和气动控制，在随机化仿真中训练到达控制器，再部署到实体系统，展示了模块化抓取与释放任务；摘要未给出成功率等量化指标。

items.title: A Support-Enhanced Granular-Jamming Gripper for RL-based Grasping with Continuum Manipulators

items.intro: arXiv:2609.30735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mobile humanoid manipulation requires both reaching a usable workspace and preserving precise hand-object interactions as object poses and contact conditions change. Learning these behaviors from limited task-specific data remains challenging. To bridge this gap, we introduce Praxis, a whole-body manipulation framework that combines physical interaction priors from one-shot egocentric video demonstrations with closed-loop posture calibration and online perception. The framework coordinates three stages: vision-language-guided navigation toward target objects, closed-loop posture calibration to align

sections.text:
Mobile humanoid manipulation requires both reaching a usable workspace and preserving precise hand-object interactions as object poses and contact conditions change. Learning these behaviors from limited task-specific data remains challenging.

To bridge this gap, we introduce Praxis, a whole-body manipulation framework that combines physical interaction priors from one-shot egocentric video demonstrations with closed-loop posture calibration and online perception.

The framework coordinates three stages: vision-language-guided navigation toward target objects, closed-loop posture calibration to align the arm-hand workspace, and dexterous manipulation with synchronized upper- and lower-body control.

Online visual feedback re-grounds demonstrated interaction geometry under new object poses and scene configurations, while tactile feedback adapts hand motions to actual contact conditions. Each manipulation skill is specified by one human demonstration, without task-specific manipulation-policy retraining.

Experiments across five long-horizon manipulation tasks demonstrate spatial, visual, and cross-object generalization, as well as recovery from external physical disturbances across all three stages.

summary.en: Mobile humanoids must reach usable workspaces while preserving precise hand-object interaction despite changing poses and contacts. Praxis combines physical interaction priors from a one-shot egocentric demonstration with closed-loop posture calibration and online perception. Its stages cover vision-language-guided navigation, arm-hand workspace alignment, and synchronized whole-body dexterous manipulation. Visual feedback re-grounds demonstrated geometry, while tactile feedback adapts motion to contact, without task-specific policy retraining. Experiments on five long-horizon tasks report spatial, visual, and cross-object generalization, along with recovery from physical disturbances across all three stages.
summary.zh: 移动人形机器人既要到达可操作位置，也要在物体姿态和接触条件变化时保持手物交互精度，而少量任务数据使学习更困难。Praxis从一次第一视角示范提取交互先验，依次进行视觉语言导航、闭环姿态校准和上下身协同的灵巧操作；在线视觉重新定位示范中的几何关系，触觉则按实际接触调整手部动作，无需针对任务重新训练操作策略。作者在五项长时程任务中报告了空间、视觉和跨物体泛化，以及三个阶段面对外部物理扰动时的恢复能力。

items.title: Praxis: Distilling Physical Interaction Priors from Egocentric Videos for Generalizable Whole-Body Manipulation

sections.text:
Open-vocabulary 3D maps enable robots to reason about previously unknown environments using natural language. However, existing systems typically segment every incoming image, associate detections with persistent 3D segments, and frequently perform costly Vision-Language (VL) inference.

We present TRACKGRAPH, an online open-vocabulary system that maintains short-term 2D mask identity directly in the image stream before fusing segments into 3D. FastSAM masks and CLIP features are computed at sparse keyframes, while dense DINOv3 features are used to propagate masks at a high rate in between.

The resulting tracked masks are fused into a class-agnostic 3D segment layer within a hierarchical scene graph, with 3D association handling tracking interruptions and long-term revisits. Compact multi-view CLIP embeddings enable open-vocabulary retrieval.

Across Replica, ScanNet++, and HM3D, TRACKGRAPH achieves competitive open-vocabulary segmentation and retrieval against state-of-the-art mapping methods, including the highest synonym frequency on Replica (0.50).On the same NVIDIA A100, it is 1.7x faster and uses 3.3x less GPU memory than ViT-H OVI-MAP.

Real-world quadruped deployments demonstrate onboard scene graph construction and object search at 7.5Hz, while recorded drone data is used to test the method under aerial viewpoints.

summary.en: Open-vocabulary mapping can require costly per-frame segmentation and repeated vision-language inference. TRACKGRAPH tracks 2D mask identities: FastSAM masks and CLIP features are computed at sparse keyframes, while dense DINOv3 features propagate masks between frames. The tracks form a class-agnostic 3D layer in a hierarchical scene graph for retrieval and revisits. On Replica, ScanNet++, and HM3D, results are competitive. On one A100, it is 1.7 times faster and uses 3.3 times less GPU memory than ViT-H OVI-MAP. Quadruped deployments construct graphs and search at 7.5 Hz; recorded drone data tests aerial views.
summary.zh: 现有开放词汇三维建图常需逐帧分割并频繁运行视觉语言推理，计算开销较大。TRACKGRAPH在图像流中跟踪二维掩码：稀疏关键帧计算FastSAM掩码和CLIP特征，帧间用稠密DINOv3特征传播，再融合为层级场景图中的类别无关三维分割，并用多视角CLIP嵌入检索。在Replica、ScanNet++和HM3D上，作者报告分割与检索表现有竞争力；同一A100上较ViT-H OVI-MAP快1.7倍、显存少3.3倍。四足机器人实地部署以7.5Hz建图和搜物，另用记录的无人机数据测试空中视角。

items.title: TRACKGRAPH: Online Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graphs via Image-Space Tracking

items.intro: arXiv:2609.31374v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Closed-loop driving simulation requires rendered observations to remain reliable as the ego vehicle and surrounding actors move beyond their recorded trajectories, exposing views absent from the source log. Existing data-driven simulators reconstruct dynamic actors from sparse observations, which can result in rendering artifacts under these viewpoint changes. sections.text:
Closed-loop driving simulation requires rendered observations to remain reliable as the ego vehicle and surrounding actors move beyond their recorded trajectories, exposing views absent from the source log.

Existing data-driven simulators reconstruct dynamic actors from sparse observations, which can result in rendering artifacts under these viewpoint changes.

We introduce RECAST (REconstructing Controllable Actors for Simulation and Testing), a 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that generates a view-complete actor from a single segmented vehicle observation in a driving log and registers the generated actor in the reconstructed scene.

RECAST supports planner-in-the-loop rendering under controlled ego-actor interactions. To adapt an image-to-3D prior to real vehicles, we further introduce RECAR, a dataset of approximately 20K real vehicles with 600K background-free RGBA images spanning diverse vehicle colors and types.

We use two-stage adaptation to improve vehicle generation from real driving-log observations. At the actor level, RECAST reduces $\mathrm{FD}_{\mathrm{incep}}$ from 9.788 to 7.992 relative to unadapted TRELLIS.

At the scene level, under actor motion beyond logged trajectories, RECAST reduces $\mathrm{FD}_{\mathrm{incep}}$ from 129.35 to 112.10 and increases $\mathrm{CLIP}_{\mathrm{margin}}$ ($\times1000$) from 0.14 to 3.47 relative to Street Gaussians. We demonstrate planner-in-the-loop simulation with the image-conditioned planner GTRS-Dense.

Compared with native Street Gaussians actors, RECAST increases the no-collision (NC) rate from 22.2% (12/54) to 63.0% (34/54) and the mean minimum predicted time-to-collision (TTC) from 0.798 s to 2.150 s. These experiments show that RECAST supports closed-loop planner evaluation under controlled ego-actor interactions beyond log replay.

Visit our project page at https://zijunkr.github.io/RECAST/

summary.en: Driving simulators can produce artifacts when vehicles move beyond logged viewpoints. RECAST uses 3D Gaussian Splatting to generate a view-complete actor from one segmented vehicle observation for planner-in-the-loop simulation. The authors introduce RECAR, with about 20,000 vehicles and 600,000 background-free images, and adapt an image-to-3D prior. Actor- and scene-level metrics improve over unadapted TRELLIS and Street Gaussians. In planner evaluation, no-collision rate rises from 22.2% to 63.0%, and mean minimum predicted time-to-collision from 0.798 to 2.150 seconds. These results are from simulation.
summary.zh: 驾驶仿真中的车辆偏离日志轨迹时，稀疏观测重建的演员可能出现视角缺失和渲染伪影。RECAST以单张分割车辆观测生成视角完整的三维高斯演员，放入重建场景支持规划器闭环渲染；作者还构建含约两万辆真实车辆、六十万张无背景图像的RECAR数据集，并用两阶段适配提升生成。在演员与场景层面，指标优于未适配TRELLIS和Street Gaussians。相较原生Street Gaussians演员，规划器测试无碰撞率从22.2%升至63.0%，平均最小预测碰撞时间从0.798秒升至2.150秒；这是仿真评估。

items.title: RECAST: From Log Replay to Closed-Loop Driving Simulation with View-Complete Actors

items.intro: arXiv:2608.11521v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: World action models (WAMs) condition robot actions on predicted futures, but iterative video rollout increases deployment latency. We ask whether action generation requires the evolving rollout trajectory or only its future representation. Across four WAMs on 40 simulated robotic manipulation tasks, paired closed-loop interventions show that blocking access to the future cache or reassigning its values changes execution and reduces success. Yet in the evaluated co-denoising settings, reusing one fixed final-clean key/value

sections.text:
World action models (WAMs) condition robot actions on predicted futures, but iterative video rollout increases deployment latency. We ask whether action generation requires the evolving rollout trajectory or only its future representation.

Across four WAMs on 40 simulated robotic manipulation tasks, paired closed-loop interventions show that blocking access to the future cache or reassigning its values changes execution and reduces success.

Yet in the evaluated co-denoising settings, reusing one fixed final-clean key/value (K/V) cache throughout action denoising nearly preserves unmodified execution, with $1.7$--$1.9$ cm end-effector average displacement error. Obtaining this cache still requires iterative video generation.

We therefore propose RIFT (Rollout-free Imagination via Future Tokens), which uses learned anticipation tokens to construct a complete future K/V cache in one backbone pass. On LIBERO, RIFT achieves $98.8\%$ overall success, outperforming all evaluated rollout-based methods while yielding a $3.1$--$9.2\times$ inference speedup.

Without further training, it achieves $81.1\%$ overall success on the out-of-distribution LIBERO-Plus benchmark, a $+9.7$ percentage-point improvement over the strongest evaluated baseline. On RoboTwin, it achieves $92.9\%$ and $92.6\%$ success on clean and randomized scenes, respectively, the highest among the evaluated methods.

On real-world manipulation tasks, RIFT achieves $45.3\%$ average success, a $+6.0$ percentage-point improvement over Fast-WAM-Joint. These results support rollout-free future conditioning without iterative video generation at deployment.

summary.en: World action models use predicted futures, but iterative video rollout adds latency. Interventions across four models and 40 simulated tasks show that blocking or altering the future cache changes execution and lowers success. Reusing a fixed final-clean cache nearly preserves execution in tested co-denoising settings, though obtaining it still requires video generation. RIFT uses learned anticipation tokens to build the future key-value cache in one backbone pass. Authors report 98.8% LIBERO success with 3.1–9.2 times faster inference; results are 81.1% on LIBERO-Plus, 92.9%/92.6% on clean/randomized RoboTwin, and 45.3% average success on real tasks.
summary.zh: 世界动作模型依赖预测未来条件化动作，但部署时反复生成视频会增加延迟。在四种模型、40项仿真任务中，干预显示屏蔽或改写未来缓存会改变执行并降低成功率；所测共同去噪设置中，重复使用固定干净缓存几乎保留表现，但取得缓存仍需迭代生成。RIFT用学习得到的预期token在一次骨干网络前向中构造未来键值缓存，免去部署时的视频迭代。作者报告LIBERO成功率98.8%、推理快3.1至9.2倍；LIBERO-Plus为81.1%，RoboTwin干净/随机场景为92.9%/92.6%，真实操作平均45.3%。

items.title: Keep the Future, Drop the Rollout: RIFT for World Action Models

items.intro: arXiv:2609.30393v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Selecting informative camera views is critical for efficient training and adaptive refinement in 3D Gaussian Splatting, where each observation significantly influences model parameters. However, information-driven view-selection strategies can require repeated evaluations of expensive information-gain oracles as the number of candidate views increases. We propose LiTe-GS, an oracle-efficient method for next best view selection in 3D Gaussian Splatting. LiTe-GS reduces the number of information-oracle evaluations by performing randomized subset evaluation of candidate views rather

sections.text:
Selecting informative camera views is critical for efficient training and adaptive refinement in 3D Gaussian Splatting, where each observation significantly influences model parameters. However, information-driven view-selection strategies can require repeated evaluations of expensive information-gain oracles as the number of candidate views increases.

We propose LiTe-GS, an oracle-efficient method for next best view selection in 3D Gaussian Splatting. LiTe-GS reduces the number of information-oracle evaluations by performing randomized subset evaluation of candidate views rather than exhaustively scoring the full candidate pool.

The resulting approach achieves expected $O(M\log(1/\epsilon))$ oracle complexity with respect to the number of candidate views $M$, independent of the selection cardinality $K$, while providing an explicit trade-off between oracle efficiency and approximation quality through $\epsilon$.

We provide theoretical guarantees on oracle complexity and approximation performance under the proposed selection scheme.

Experiments on Blender and Mip-NeRF 360 demonstrate that LiTe-GS maintains reconstruction quality comparable to Fisher-information-based baselines while substantially reducing the number of Fisher-oracle evaluations across different acquisition settings.

summary.en: Next-best-view selection for 3D Gaussian Splatting can require costly information-gain evaluations. LiTe-GS randomly scores candidate subsets rather than the full pool. Its expected oracle complexity is O(M log(1/ε)), independent of selection cardinality K, with ε controlling the efficiency-approximation trade-off. The paper provides theoretical guarantees. Experiments on Blender and Mip-NeRF 360 report reconstruction quality comparable to Fisher-information baselines while substantially reducing oracle calls; no reduction percentage is given.
summary.zh: 三维高斯泼溅的下一最佳视角选择需评估候选视角信息增益，候选增多时预言机调用成本高。LiTe-GS随机抽取候选子集评估，减少调用；期望复杂度为O(M log(1/ε))，与选择数量K无关，并由ε权衡效率和近似质量。论文给出复杂度与近似性能的理论保证。Blender和Mip-NeRF 360实验中，作者报告重建质量与Fisher信息基线相近，同时显著减少不同采集设置下的预言机调用；摘要未提供减少比例。

items.title: LiTe-GS: Oracle-Efficient Next Best View Selection for 3D Gaussian Splatting

items.intro: arXiv:2609.30828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Precision manipulation with contact-critical interactions is often history-dependent: visually similar observations can correspond to different latent interaction states and therefore require different actions, while small execution errors can alter task outcomes. Policies relying on the current visual observation alone cannot resolve such ambiguity; force-aware and memory-augmented methods enrich physical or temporal context, while reactive high-rate policies improve local contact response, yet long-horizon temporal reasoning and precision execution remain largely decoupled in existing methods

sections.text:
Precision manipulation with contact-critical interactions is often history-dependent: visually similar observations can correspond to different latent interaction states and therefore require different actions, while small execution errors can alter task outcomes.

Policies relying on the current visual observation alone cannot resolve such ambiguity; force-aware and memory-augmented methods enrich physical or temporal context, while reactive high-rate policies improve local contact response, yet long-horizon temporal reasoning and precision execution remain largely decoupled in existing methods, limiting reliable progression in visually aliased precision manipulation.

To bridge this gap, we introduce History-Conditioned Interaction Reasoning and Execution (HIRE), a cross-rate framework comprising a history-conditioned Interaction-State Reasoner (ISR) and a high-rate Interaction-Manifold Executor (IME).

ISR encodes ordered wrench history with a temporal wrench encoder and Force Perceiver as persistent physical evidence for state-consistent action generation, while IME structures contact-critical motion into intrinsic progress and transverse correction for precise execution; their cross-rate loop allows the resulting physical traces to inform subsequent reasoning.

In real-robot experiments across surface, insertion, and rotational interactions, HIRE achieves at least 90% completion across all evaluated task stages while improving interaction-state disambiguation, execution precision, and generalization.

More broadly, HIRE provides a unified reasoning--execution perspective on precision manipulation under history-dependent partial observability, where physical interaction both realizes task intent and reveals latent-state evidence for future decisions. Code will be released upon publication.

summary.en: Contact-critical manipulation depends on interaction history: similar images can reflect different latent states, and small execution errors can change outcomes. HIRE combines a history-conditioned Interaction-State Reasoner (ISR) with a high-rate Interaction-Manifold Executor (IME) in a cross-rate loop. ISR encodes ordered wrench history as persistent physical evidence; IME structures contact-critical motion into intrinsic progress and transverse correction, then returns physical traces to inform later reasoning. Real-robot experiments on surface, insertion, and rotational interactions report at least 90% completion across all evaluated task stages, with improvements in state disambiguation, precision, and generalization. The abstract does not specify task counts or detailed comparisons.
summary.zh: 精细接触操作具有历史依赖性：视觉相似的画面可能对应不同隐状态，需要不同动作，而小误差也会改变结果。HIRE将历史条件交互状态推理器ISR与高速交互流形执行器IME组成跨频率闭环；ISR编码有序力/力矩历史，作为持续物理证据，IME则把接触关键运动拆成内在进度和横向修正，执行轨迹再反馈供后续推理。作者在真实机器人表面交互、插入和旋转实验中报告，所有评估任务阶段完成率至少90%，并改善状态辨析、执行精度及泛化。该结果限于摘要提及的真实机器人实验任务，未给出任务数量或具体对照数据。

items.title: HIRE: History-Conditioned Interaction Reasoning and High-Rate Execution for Visually Aliased Precision Manipulation

Existing learned estimators are also commonly trained independently for each vehicle; this preserves vehicle-specific behavior but prevents vehicles from sharing common terrain representations. DGT-MAP addresses both limitations through a self-supervised framework that learns global, directional, and vehicle-conditioned traversability costmaps from RGB-D observations and locomotion signals. A shared multi-task backbone learns common terrain features across

sections.text:
Off-road traversability is direction-dependent and vehicle specific, yet most global maps assign a single isotropic cost to each location. Existing learned estimators are also commonly trained independently for each vehicle; this preserves vehicle-specific behavior but prevents vehicles from sharing common terrain representations.

DGT-MAP addresses both limitations through a self-supervised framework that learns global, directional, and vehicle-conditioned traversability costmaps from RGB-D observations and locomotion signals.

A shared multi-task backbone learns common terrain features across training vehicles while vehicle-specific prediction heads preserve platform-dependent responses. At inference, DGT-MAP produces a heading-indexed costmap that can be used by a direction-aware planner.

We evaluate DGT-MAP in simulation by integrating it into a Hybrid A* navigation stack and measuring downstream task success on challenging terrains, including slopes that are traversable downhill but not uphill and a ridge obstacle that is traversable by some vehicles, but not by others.

Across evaluated tasks, DGT-MAP achieves the highest or tied-highest navigation success rate when compared against geometric, binary, and learned direction-agnostic baselines.

summary.en: Off-road traversability depends on direction and vehicle type, but common maps use isotropic costs. DGT-MAP learns shared terrain features and vehicle-specific directional costmaps from RGB-D and locomotion signals. It supplies heading-indexed costs to a direction-aware planner. Integrated with Hybrid A*, it is evaluated in simulation on slopes and vehicle-dependent ridge obstacles. Across tasks, it achieves the highest or tied-highest navigation success against geometric, binary, and direction-agnostic learned baselines. The abstract reports no physical-robot trials.
summary.zh: 越野可通行性既受行驶方向影响，也因车辆而异，但常见地图为每个位置赋予单一各向同性代价，独立训练的车辆模型又难共享地形表征。DGT-MAP从RGB-D观测和运动信号自监督学习全局、方向及车辆条件化代价图，以共享多任务骨干提取地形特征，再由车辆专属预测头保留平台差异，输出按航向索引的地图供方向感知规划器使用。作者将其接入Hybrid A*，在模拟中测试上下坡差异及车辆特异的山脊障碍等地形。相较几何、二值和方向无关学习基线，所测任务的导航成功率最高或并列最高；摘要未报告实机结果。

items.title: DGT-Map: Directional Global Traversability Mapping Utilizing Multi-Task Learning for Heterogeneous Vehicles

However, scaling existing benchmarks remains difficult because of their reliance on costly reconstructed 3D assets, limiting geographic diversity and episode scale. To address this, we introduce SatNav, a scalable, long-horizon UAV VLN benchmark built from high-resolution satellite imagery. SatNav targets city-level navigation missions and uses satellite crops as approximations

sections.text:
Urban uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) vision-language navigation (VLN) requires agents to follow instructions across extended urban spaces, inherently demanding long-term memory and geospatial grounding.

However, scaling existing benchmarks remains difficult because of their reliance on costly reconstructed 3D assets, limiting geographic diversity and episode scale. To address this, we introduce SatNav, a scalable, long-horizon UAV VLN benchmark built from high-resolution satellite imagery.

SatNav targets city-level navigation missions and uses satellite crops as approximations of UAV nadir views for visual observations. Through an automated cue-to-episode pipeline, SatNav constructs 118K episodes from 59 scenes across 18 cities, with an average trajectory length of 379 m.

To stress-test long-horizon memory and geospatial reasoning, SatNav defines three task families: Boundary, Landmark, and Route, targeting loop progress tracking, landmark-based spatial grounding, and route following with counting cues.

Benchmarking classical VLN agents and recent agents based on large vision-language models (LVLMs) on SatNav shows that city-scale navigation remains challenging. We further introduce SwiftVLN, a modular framework with switchable memory components, and conduct systematic memory-design ablations.

Finally, satellite-to-UAV transfer experiments show that satellite-trained navigation models can operate on real-flight UAV observations, showing the practical relevance of SatNav. Our project page: https://eku127.github.io/SatNav/

summary.en: City-scale UAV vision-language navigation requires long-term memory and geospatial grounding, while benchmarks based on reconstructed 3D assets are costly to scale. SatNav uses high-resolution satellite imagery, with crops approximating nadir UAV views, to create 118,000 episodes across 59 scenes in 18 cities; average trajectories are 379 meters. It defines Boundary, Landmark, and Route task families. Evaluations of classical and large vision-language-model agents show that city-scale navigation remains challenging. The authors also introduce SwiftVLN with switchable memory components and conduct ablations. Satellite-to-UAV transfer experiments show that satellite-trained models can operate on real-flight observations, though no quantitative transfer result is stated.
summary.zh: 城市级无人机视觉语言导航需要长时记忆和地理定位，但依赖重建三维资产的基准难以扩展地域与任务规模。SatNav以高分辨率卫星影像裁片近似无人机俯视视角，通过自动线索生成流程构建118,000个任务，覆盖18座城市的59个场景，平均轨迹379米，并设置边界、地标和路线三类长程任务。对经典导航代理和近期大视觉语言模型代理的测试显示城市尺度导航仍具挑战。作者另提出可切换记忆组件的SwiftVLN并开展消融；卫星训练到无人机实飞观测的迁移实验表明模型可处理真实飞行影像，但摘要未报告定量迁移成绩。

items.title: SatNav: A Scalable Benchmark for Long-Horizon UAV Vision-Language Navigation from Satellite Imagery

A spatial quadtree schedules sensing goals across regions to reduce repeated visits while retaining all orientation configurations for routing. Under exact sensing and geometric computation and star-shaped robot and envelope

sections.text:
We present the dynamic rotation-stacked visibility graph (dRVG), an online motion planner that guides polygonal robots to specified goals in initially unknown, static environ- ments. It merges local roadmaps from successive observations to plan collision-free translations and rotations without a uniform position grid.

A spatial quadtree schedules sensing goals across regions to reduce repeated visits while retaining all orientation configurations for routing. Under exact sensing and geometric computation and star-shaped robot and envelope assumptions, dRVG with center scans is resolution-complete relative to full- map RVG at the same angular resolution.

In experiments using footprint scans, dRVG solves all 140 cases across 20 difficult maps and seven angular resolutions within a 20 s planning budget, with a median planning time of 1.18 s at 360 orientation layers. Six microMVP demonstrations illustrate the complete online planning loop on a physical robot.

summary.en: The online dRVG plans collision-free translation and rotation for polygonal robots in unknown static environments, merging local roadmaps without a uniform position grid. A spatial quadtree schedules sensing while preserving orientation configurations. Under exact sensing and geometry plus star-shaped robot and envelope assumptions, center scans are resolution-complete relative to full-map RVG. In footprint-scan tests, it solves all 140 cases across 20 maps and seven angular resolutions within 20 seconds; median planning time is 1.18 seconds at 360 orientation layers. Six demonstrations show the online loop on a physical robot.
summary.zh: 在未知静态环境中规划多边形机器人的平移和旋转，既要避免碰撞，也要减少反复探索。dRVG在线合并连续观测得到的局部可见图，不使用均匀位置网格；空间四叉树安排各区域的感知目标，同时保留朝向配置用于路径规划。在精确感知与几何计算、机器人及包络为星形等假设下，中心扫描版本相对同角分辨率的完整地图RVG具有分辨率完备性。采用足迹扫描的实验中，作者报告在20张困难地图、七种角分辨率共140个案例中均于20秒规划预算内求解，360层朝向时中位规划时间1.18秒；另展示了实体机器人上的六次完整在线规划流程。

items.title: dRVG: Quadtree-Guided, Resolution-Complete Online Motion Planning for Polygonal Robots in Unknown Environments
