sections.text:
Tactile information is essential for contact-rich manipulation tasks in robotics. Vision-based tactile sensors make it particularly easy to design end-to-end manipulation policies with tactile sensing, as they enable the use of existing encoders from computer vision.

However, this has led to a huge variety of architectures, training datasets, and evaluation protocols, making it difficult to determine which design choices best encode touch. In this work, we address this gap and present a comprehensive study of tactile encoders and fusion strategies across various contact-rich manipulation tasks in real-world experiments.

To enable a controlled comparison, we train and evaluate all models under the same pipeline and experimental setup, comprising more than 2000 real-world rollouts.

Our results go beyond other studies that only compare simulation performance, which does not necessarily translate to real-world settings, where large-scale evaluations are needed to obtain reliable statistics. Our key finding is that there is no universally optimal representation or fusion strategy for encoding visual-tactile.

Instead, the best encoder backbone and fusion scheme depend strongly on the task.

summary.en: Tactile manipulation studies vary widely in encoders, training data, and evaluation protocols, making design comparisons difficult and simulated performance an uncertain guide to real-world results. TACTIC conducts a controlled study of tactile encoders and visual-tactile fusion strategies across contact-rich tasks, using a shared training pipeline and more than 2,000 real-world rollouts. Its central finding is that there is no universally best representation or fusion strategy: the best encoder backbone and fusion scheme depend strongly on the task. The abstract does not name individual tasks or provide performance figures, so it does not support a single overall winning architecture.
summary.zh: 触觉策略的编码器、训练数据和评测流程差异很大，难以判断何种表示和融合方式适合接触丰富的操作，也难以从仿真推断实机表现。TACTIC在统一训练流程和实验设置下，对多种触觉编码器及融合策略进行系统比较，覆盖真实世界多项接触操作任务，并收集超过2000次实机运行。作者的主要发现不是存在通用最优方案，而是最佳编码骨干和视觉—触觉融合方式强烈依赖具体任务。摘要未列举各任务名称或性能数值，因此不能据此判断某种架构在总体上胜出。

items.title: TACTIC: Understanding Tactile Encoders and Conditioning for Contact-rich Robot Manipulation Policies

items.intro: arXiv:2603.07096v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Robots that share space with people need human motion predictions with reliable uncertainty, not just accurate means. This paper presents a structured multitask variational Gaussian process (GP) for probabilistic full-body human motion prediction. The model integrates one-shot prediction of the full horizon, multitask outputs that couple future time steps, a factorization into one sparse variational GP per joint-dimension pair of the rotation representation, and a continuous 6D rotation representation with forward kinematics that

sections.text:
Robots that share space with people need human motion predictions with reliable uncertainty, not just accurate means. This paper presents a structured multitask variational Gaussian process (GP) for probabilistic full-body human motion prediction.

The model integrates one-shot prediction of the full horizon, multitask outputs that couple future time steps, a factorization into one sparse variational GP per joint-dimension pair of the rotation representation, and a continuous 6D rotation representation with forward kinematics that preserves bone lengths.

Its predictive distribution is available in closed form: a Gaussian with full temporal covariance for each rotation coordinate, which downstream planners operating in rotation coordinates can use without sampling, density estimation, or forward kinematics.

On Human3.6M, the model achieves lower kernel-density-estimated negative log-likelihood (KDE NLL) than Motron and DLow at every prediction step, 22-52 nats below Motron. Empirical coverage is conservative at the 50% and 80% levels and close to nominal at 95% over a 2 s horizon.

The probabilistic model uses 0.24 M parameters, about seven times fewer than Motron, and a separately trained 0.35 M-parameter deterministic variant has a mean angle error 3-22% higher than Motron's.

Ablations confirm the benefit of the 6D representation and show that, at a fixed training budget, factorized joint outputs outperform coupled right-arm alternatives in NLL and CRPS while using less memory.

These results show that compact, structured GPs provide analytic, temporally structured uncertainty with conservative empirical coverage for robotic systems.

summary.en: Robots sharing space with people need uncertainty estimates for full-body motion. This structured multitask variational Gaussian process predicts the full horizon, factorizes sparse processes by joint and rotation dimension, and uses continuous 6D rotations with forward kinematics. It provides an analytic Gaussian distribution with temporal covariance. On Human3.6M, KDE negative log-likelihood is below Motron and DLow at every step; coverage is conservative at 50% and 80%, near nominal at 95%. The probabilistic model has 0.24 million parameters. A separately trained deterministic variant has 3–22% higher mean angle error than Motron.
summary.zh: 与人共处的机器人需要人体运动预测及可信的不确定性，而不仅是均值准确。论文提出结构化多任务变分高斯过程，一次预测完整时间范围，以关节—维度因子化稀疏过程和连续6D旋转表示人体姿态，并用正向运动学保持骨长；输出具有时间协方差的解析高斯分布。Human3.6M测试中，其KDE负对数似然各步均低于Motron和DLow，经验覆盖率在50%与80%水平偏保守、95%水平接近标称。概率模型含0.24百万参数；另行训练的确定性版本角度误差比Motron高3%至22%。

items.title: Structured Multitask Gaussian Processes for Probabilistic Full-Body Human Motion Prediction

items.intro: arXiv:2609.30404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present POIL, a point-based one-shot imitation learning framework with stable dynamical systems. While one-shot imitation avoids collecting extensive demonstrations, successful one-shot manipulation requires not only transferring a demonstrated trajectory to a novel object but also executing it robustly under changing scene conditions, grasp configurations, and external disturbances. POIL addresses both problems through a shared representation: a set of 3D points on the object's functional part, used jointly for trajectory transfer and closed-loop

sections.text:
We present POIL, a point-based one-shot imitation learning framework with stable dynamical systems.

While one-shot imitation avoids collecting extensive demonstrations, successful one-shot manipulation requires not only transferring a demonstrated trajectory to a novel object but also executing it robustly under changing scene conditions, grasp configurations, and external disturbances.

POIL addresses both problems through a shared representation: a set of 3D points on the object's functional part, used jointly for trajectory transfer and closed-loop execution. The one-shot transfer from the demonstrated trajectory is enabled with point correspondences.

POIL grounds the shared functional part with a multi-modal large language model, and transfers the trajectory across viewpoint, pose, and object category changes.

During execution, multi-view tracking observes the same points online, and Point-set BCSDM drives them in closed loop by projecting per-point velocities onto a single rigid-body twist computed from the tracked points alone. This extends stable dynamical models from an SE（3） pose to a point set without requiring a known 3D model or pose estimator.

We show that at the goal the controller becomes a gradient flow on the classical SO（3） potential, so its terminal phase inherits the almost-global convergence of that potential under a rigid-object assumption.

Across simulation and real-robot experiments, POIL transfers a single demonstration across object category, grasp pose, and goal geometry, while recovering from external disturbances during execution. Project page: https://sangminkim-99.github.io/poil

summary.en: POIL uses 3D points on an object's functional part to transfer a one-shot demonstration and guide closed-loop execution. A multimodal language model grounds the part, point correspondences transfer the trajectory, and multi-view tracking feeds Point-set BCSDM. It estimates rigid-body motion from tracked points without a known 3D model or pose estimator. Under a rigid-object assumption, its terminal controller inherits almost-global convergence from a classical rotation potential. Simulation and real-robot experiments report transfer across object categories, grasp poses, and goal geometry, plus recovery from disturbances.
summary.zh: 一次示范迁移操作轨迹时，还需应对新物体、抓取姿态、场景变化和外部扰动。POIL以物体功能部位的一组三维点作为共享表示，通过点对应迁移演示轨迹，并由多模态大语言模型定位该功能部位；执行时，多视角跟踪这些点，Point-set BCSDM仅依据跟踪点估计刚体运动，实现闭环控制，无需已知三维模型或位姿估计器。作者证明在刚体假设下终端阶段继承经典旋转势的几乎全局收敛性质。仿真和实机实验表明，单次示范可跨物体类别、抓取姿态及目标几何迁移，并在执行时从外界扰动中恢复。

items.title: POIL: Point-based One-Shot Imitation Learning with Stable Dynamical Systems

sections.text:
Moving Horizon Estimation (MHE) is a state estimation method based on finite-horizon optimization that can offer higher accuracy at the cost of increased computation compared to Kalman filter-based approaches.

We present a linear smoothing MHE formulation as a dense Quadratic Program (QP), and a solver consisting of a continuous-time Newton's method augmented with the $\mathcal{L}_1$ Adaptive Optimizer ($\mathcal{L}_1$-AO).

While MHE is inherently time-varying, conventional approaches treat it as a sequence of independent, time-invariant problems and employ iterative solvers at each time step, which can be both inaccurate and computationally burdensome.

In contrast, time-varying solvers track the optimal solution with fewer iterations by exploiting the temporal evolution of the problem, thereby reducing the computational load.

In this research, we enhance both the performance and efficiency of MHE through a time-varying solver with an $\mathcal{L}_1$-AO augmentation that compensates for the prediction inaccuracy, which is common in practice due to noisy sensors and the lack of prior knowledge of the system.

Simulation results on a quadrotor platform show that the $\mathcal{L}_1$-AO-augmented approach solves the MHE optimization problem more efficiently than the baseline time-invariant solver and achieves higher estimation accuracy under challenging conditions, compared with both the Extended Kalman Filter and the standard MHE.

summary.en: The paper formulates linear smoothing moving-horizon estimation as a dense quadratic program and proposes a time-varying Newton solver augmented with an L1 Adaptive Optimizer to compensate for prediction error. This exploits temporal evolution instead of solving each time step independently. Quadrotor simulations report greater efficiency than a time-invariant solver and higher estimation accuracy under challenging conditions than the Extended Kalman Filter and standard MHE. The abstract reports simulation only and gives no error values.
summary.zh: 移动时域估计可提高状态估计精度，但比卡尔曼滤波计算更重；逐时刻把问题当作独立静态优化又会增加迭代和误差。作者将线性平滑MHE写为稠密二次规划，并提出追踪时变最优解的连续时间牛顿求解器，以L1自适应优化器补偿传感噪声及系统先验不足造成的预测误差。四旋翼仿真中，增强求解器相比基准时不变求解器更高效，并在困难条件下较扩展卡尔曼滤波和标准MHE获得更高估计精度。结果仅来自摘要所述仿真平台，未报告真实飞行验证或具体误差数字。

items.title: Moving Horizon Estimation for Quadrotors: An $\mathcal{L}_1$ Adaptive Optimizer Approach

sections.text:
Event cameras offer a high temporal resolution over traditional frame-based cameras, which makes them suitable for motion and structure estimation. However, it has been unclear how event-based 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) approaches could leverage fine-grained temporal information of sparse events.

This work proposes GPERT, a framework to address the trade-off between accuracy and temporal resolution in event-based 3DGS. Our key idea is to decouple the rendering into two branches: event-by-event geometry (depth) rendering and snapshot-based radiance (intensity) rendering, by using ray-tracing and the image of warped events.

The extensive evaluation shows that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on the real-world datasets and competitive performance on the synthetic dataset.

Also, the proposed method works without prior information (e.g., pretrained image reconstruction models) or COLMAP-based initialization, is more flexible in the event selection number, and achieves sharp reconstruction on scene edges with fast training time.

We hope that this work deepens our understanding of the sparse nature of events for 3D reconstruction. https://github.com/e3ai/gpert

summary.en: GPERT addresses how event-based 3D Gaussian Splatting can use the fine timing of sparse events. It separates event-by-event depth rendering with ray tracing from snapshot radiance rendering using warped-event images. The authors report state-of-the-art results on real-world datasets and competitive performance on synthetic data. The method requires neither pretrained image-reconstruction models nor COLMAP initialization, supports flexible event counts, and produces sharp scene edges with fast training. The abstract supplies no metric values, so comparisons are limited to the evaluated datasets.
summary.zh: 事件相机具有高时间分辨率，但如何利用稀疏事件中的细粒度时序信息进行三维高斯泼溅重建仍不明确。GPERT将渲染拆成两路：通过光线追踪逐事件估计几何深度，并利用扭曲事件图像进行快照式辐射强度渲染，以协调精度和时间分辨率。作者在真实数据集上报告达到当时领先表现，在合成数据集上表现有竞争力；方法不依赖预训练图像重建模型或COLMAP初始化，可灵活改变事件选取数量，并报告场景边缘重建清晰、训练较快。摘要没有提供指标数值，结论限于所测数据集。

items.title: Geometric-Photometric Event-based 3D Gaussian Ray Tracing

Existing methods mainly focus on improving trajectory multi-modality, enhancing trajectory representations, or reshaping the candidate distribution. Nevertheless, we identify a pronounced generation-evaluation asymmetry in multi-modal planning: despite strong oracle performance, existing planners often fail to reliably select the best available candidate, leaving substantial planning potential unrealized. To address this challenge, we propose iDriveVLA, a multi-modal planning

sections.text:
Multi-modal planning is promising for autonomous driving by representing multiple plausible behaviors in ambiguous and long-tail scenarios. Existing methods mainly focus on improving trajectory multi-modality, enhancing trajectory representations, or reshaping the candidate distribution.

Nevertheless, we identify a pronounced generation-evaluation asymmetry in multi-modal planning: despite strong oracle performance, existing planners often fail to reliably select the best available candidate, leaving substantial planning potential unrealized.

To address this challenge, we propose iDriveVLA, a multi-modal planning framework that improves the candidate trajectory space while enabling more reliable and context-aware trajectory evaluation.

Specifically, iDriveVLA introduces a unified trajectory evaluator comprising a Safety-aware Scorer for quality and risk estimation, together with a VLM-guided Modulator for scene-adaptive criterion weighting.

We further develop an oracle-aligned progressive training strategy consisting of candidate imitation pretraining, candidate space refinement, and semantic ranking alignment. On the public NAVSIM v1 leaderboard, iDriveVLA achieves a new state-of-the-art performance of 94.95 PDMS, surpassing the human-expert reference.

summary.en: Multimodal driving planners can represent alternative behaviors in ambiguous or long-tail scenes, but often fail to select their strongest candidate despite good oracle performance. iDriveVLA combines candidate-space improvement with context-aware evaluation. Its unified evaluator includes a safety-aware scorer for quality and risk and a vision-language modulator that adjusts criterion weights by scene. Progressive training covers candidate imitation, candidate-space refinement, and semantic ranking alignment. On the public NAVSIM v1 leaderboard, the authors report 94.95 PDMS, surpassing the human-expert reference. This is a benchmark score; the abstract does not establish general road safety or real-world deployment.
summary.zh: 多模态自动驾驶规划可保留歧义和长尾场景中的多种候选行为，但已有方法虽能生成较好的候选轨迹，却常不能可靠选出最佳方案。iDriveVLA将候选轨迹空间改进与上下文感知评估结合：安全评分器估计质量和风险，视觉语言调制器按场景调整评价准则权重；渐进训练包含候选模仿预训练、候选空间精炼和语义排序对齐。在公开NAVSIM v1排行榜上，作者报告取得94.95 PDMS并超过人类专家参考成绩。该数字是特定公开基准排行榜指标，并非普遍道路安全或实车部署结论。

items.title: Evaluation Is All You Need for Multi-Modal Autonomous Driving

Visual-inertial sensing supplies local motion constraints, but false visual associations can corrupt the estimator. sections.text:
Reliable absolute pose estimation in urban environments is undermined by outlier measurements and incorrect temporal associations that can persist in tightly coupled estimators. Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) observations provide globally referenced measurements but are prone to multipath effects.

Visual-inertial sensing supplies local motion constraints, but false visual associations can corrupt the estimator. We present SeA-RVINS, a fixed-lag factor-graph Real-Time Kinematic (RTK) visual-inertial system for robust urban pose estimation. A semantic-aware learned stereo frontend rejects unreliable tracks before persistent landmarks enter the graph.

For double-differenced GNSS measurements, SeA-RVINS applies Dynamic Covariance Scaling through configurable batch, scalar, and latent-pivot robust formulations while retaining the shared-pivot correlation structure.

We propose a hybrid ambiguity-continuation strategy that shares one ambiguity state over short arcs with verified continuity and softly links successive arcs through random-walk factors.

On an approximately 20-km route from the public TEX-CUP dataset, including about 50\% deep-urban driving, the latent-pivot configuration achieves 100\% availability and a 1.6-m maximum horizontal error, with 96.16\% and 99.90\% of epochs below 1.0 and 1.5 m, respectively. The implementation is released as open-source software

summary.en: SeA-RVINS is a fixed-lag RTK visual-inertial factor graph for urban pose estimation. Its semantic-aware stereo frontend rejects unreliable tracks, while robust GNSS estimation preserves shared-pivot correlations and a hybrid strategy continues ambiguity states across short arcs. On an approximately 20-kilometer TEX-CUP route, about half deep urban, the latent-pivot configuration reports 100% availability, 1.6-meter maximum horizontal error, and 96.16%/99.90% of epochs below 1.0/1.5 meters. This result is from one public-data route.
summary.zh: 城市环境中的GNSS多路径和错误视觉关联会破坏绝对位姿估计。SeA-RVINS构建固定滞后的RTK视觉惯性因子图，以语义感知立体视觉前端剔除不可靠轨迹；对双差GNSS观测采用保留共享基准相关性的鲁棒估计，并以混合模糊度延续策略连接连续短弧段。在TEX-CUP约20公里路线（约一半为深城市路段）上，潜在基准配置可用率100%、最大水平误差1.6米，96.16%和99.90%的历元误差分别低于1.0米和1.5米。结果来自单条公开数据路线。

items.title: SeA-RVINS: Semantic-Aware Tightly Coupled RTK-Visual-Inertial System with Correlation-Preserving Robust Estimation for Urban Navigation

sections.text:
As populations in developed countries age and labor shortages intensify, Cybernetic Avatars (CAs) are proposed to extend human capabilities through robotic embodiments, requiring effective Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) frameworks.

Extended Reality (XR), an umbrella term for Augmented Reality (AR), Augmented Virtuality (AV), and Virtual Reality (VR), offers such interfaces, but prior research typically fixes the XR modality without evaluating its effect on task outcomes.

This study examines whether the XR modality impacts HRI performance and whether an adaptive interface adjusting the level of virtuality along the Reality-Virtuality Continuum (RVC) at runtime improves it. A custom XR application interfaced with a mobile manipulator supports immersive control and runtime modality switching.

In a within-participant multi-room pick-and-place experiment comparing fixed AR, AV, and VR with dynamic RVC through task metrics, the NASA-TLX, and the System Usability Scale (SUS), this study demonstrates that 1) the fixed reality modality affects HRI results, and 2) dynamically changing the modality along the RVC improves them.

AR yielded significantly lower mental demand, effort, and frustration than AV and VR, while the dynamic RVC condition achieved the highest throughput and lowest workload, highlighting the value of adaptive XR interfaces for human-robot symbiosis. The implementation is available at https://github.com/CarlTornberg/XR-HRI.

summary.en: Extended reality can support human-robot interaction, but prior work often fixes one modality without testing its effects on task outcomes. This study builds an XR application connected to a mobile manipulator and compares fixed AR, AV, and VR with runtime switching along the Reality-Virtuality Continuum. A within-participant, multi-room pick-and-place experiment uses task metrics, NASA-TLX, and the System Usability Scale. The authors report that fixed modality affects outcomes: AR has significantly lower mental demand, effort, and frustration than AV and VR, while dynamic switching yields the highest throughput and lowest workload. The abstract does not state participant count or effect sizes.
summary.zh: 扩展现实可用于网络化机器人交互，但既有研究常固定增强现实、增强虚拟或虚拟现实模式，未比较模式对任务表现的影响。该研究开发连接移动操作机器人的XR应用，在多房间取放任务中进行参与者内比较，评估固定AR、AV、VR及运行时沿现实—虚拟连续体动态切换的界面，并使用任务指标、NASA-TLX和SUS量表。作者报告固定模式会影响交互结果；AR相较AV和VR显著降低心理需求、努力程度和挫折感，而动态模式取得最高吞吐量和最低工作负荷。结论来自摘要所述实验条件，未给出样本数及效应大小。

items.title: Evaluating the Impact of Adaptive Extended Reality on Human-Robot Interaction Across the Reality-Virtuality Continuum

Efficiency in these systems allows for smaller, cooler, and lighter devices. sections.text:
Perception in robotics and XR fundamentally relies on good state estimation. Visual-inertial odometry (VIO) and Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (VI-SLAM) are proven ways of achieving this goal in a cost-effective and accurate manner. Efficiency in these systems allows for smaller, cooler, and lighter devices.

GPU acceleration is a natural approach for reducing latency, thanks to their wide availability in platforms like embedded computers, mobile phones, and XR headsets. However, previous works in the literature have limited themselves to the use of CUDA for this task, significantly reducing deployment options to a single vendor.

We instead leverage the vendor-agnostic Vulkan API, originally designed for the strict performance requirements of 3D graphics applications. In this work, we present VkVIO, the first, to the best of our knowledge, cross-platform GPU-accelerated VIO method. We provide state-of-the-art accuracy with causal estimates required for real-time operation.

We deploy VkVIO on a diverse range of devices spanning a workstation, a laptop, and an extremely inexpensive single-board computer, while outperforming CUDA-based systems on the same hardware. VkVIO enables possibilities for low-latency, low-power, and low-cost VIO in robotics and XR.

summary.en: GPU acceleration can reduce visual-inertial odometry latency, but prior approaches have largely relied on CUDA, limiting deployment to one vendor. VkVIO uses the vendor-agnostic Vulkan API and is presented by its authors as the first cross-platform GPU-accelerated VIO method, producing causal estimates for real-time use. They deploy it on a workstation, laptop, and inexpensive single-board computer. The abstract reports state-of-the-art accuracy and better performance than CUDA-based systems on the same hardware. It argues that this enables low-latency, low-power, low-cost VIO for robotics and XR, but provides no device-specific speed, power, or accuracy figures.
summary.zh: VIO的GPU加速既有方案主要依赖CUDA，限制了设备厂商和部署选择。VkVIO改用面向跨厂商的Vulkan API，提出作者所称首个跨平台GPU加速视觉惯性里程计，并提供适用于实时运行的因果估计。系统部署于工作站、笔记本和低成本单板计算机等不同设备；作者报告在相同硬件上优于CUDA方案，同时达到先进精度。摘要强调低延迟、低功耗和低成本部署潜力，但未给出各设备的速度、功耗或精度数据，也未说明所有设备上的具体对照方法。

items.title: VkVIO: Cross-platform GPU Acceleration for Visual-Inertial Odometry with Vulkan

SANDO addresses this trade-off through three contributions. First, a heat map-based A* global planner steers the path away from high-risk regions, and a spatiotemporal safe flight corridor (STSFC) generator produces time-layered polytopes that inflate obstacles only by

sections.text:
This paper presents SANDO, a safe trajectory planner for 3D dynamic unknown environments. Existing soft-constraint planners are fast but do not guarantee collision-free paths, while hard-constraint methods typically ensure safety at the cost of longer computation. SANDO addresses this trade-off through three contributions.

First, a heat map-based A* global planner steers the path away from high-risk regions, and a spatiotemporal safe flight corridor (STSFC) generator produces time-layered polytopes that inflate obstacles only by their worst-case reachable set at each time layer, rather than over the entire horizon.

Second, trajectory optimization is formulated as a mixed-integer quadratic program with hard collision-avoidance constraints, and variable elimination reduces the number of decision variables. Third, a formal safety analysis establishes collision-free guarantees under explicit velocity-bound, size-bound, and estimation-error assumptions.

Ablation studies confirm that variable elimination yields up to 7.4 times faster optimization and that STSFCs are critical for feasibility in dense dynamic environments.

In simulations against state-of-the-art methods, SANDO achieves a 100% success rate across all forest and dynamic benchmark difficulty levels with no constraint violations, and perception-only experiments demonstrate the full perception-to-planning pipeline.

Hardware experiments with fully onboard planning, perception, and localization demonstrate six safe flights in static environments and twelve among dynamic obstacles.

summary.en: SANDO combines heat-map-guided A*, time-layered safe flight corridors, and mixed-integer quadratic trajectory optimization with hard collision constraints. Variable elimination reduces decision variables; formal guarantees rely on bounds for velocity, size, and estimation error. Ablations report up to 7.4 times faster optimization and show corridors aid feasibility in dense dynamic scenes. Simulations achieve 100% success across tested forest and dynamic benchmark difficulties with no constraint violations. Fully onboard hardware trials demonstrate six safe static flights and twelve flights among dynamic obstacles.
summary.zh: 动态未知环境中的软约束规划虽快却不能保证无碰撞，硬约束方法通常较慢。SANDO结合热图引导A*、按时间分层并按各层最坏可达范围膨胀障碍物的安全走廊，以及带硬碰撞约束的混合整数二次规划；变量消元减少决策变量。形式化保证依赖明确的速度、尺寸及估计误差界。消融显示变量消元最多使优化快7.4倍，时空走廊对密集场景可行性关键。模拟基准各难度森林和动态场景成功率均为100%且无约束违反；全机载实验另展示静态环境六次、动态障碍间十二次安全飞行。

items.title: SANDO: Safe Autonomous Trajectory Planning for Dynamic Unknown Environments

sections.text:
We present Cloak, a training recipe that endows a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model with zero-shot cross-embodiment transfer by cloaking the end-effector from its own wrist camera. The end-effector occupies a large and consistent region of the wrist view and masking it allows for embodiment-agnostic visual reasoning.

Cloak renders a mask in simulation from the robot's known geometry, accurately and in real time, with no segmentation or generative models. During training, we augment the mask so the model generalizes to embodiments unseen at training time. We demonstrate the recipe with Cloak-VLA, a VLA trained with Cloak on a single parallel-jaw gripper dataset.

No data of new embodiments is ever collected. Cloak-VLA transfers zero-shot to various unseen embodiments, including another gripper, another arm, and a five-fingered hand, while preserving the source embodiment's performance. By decoupling the wrist view from its own embodiment, Cloak allows data to outlive the hardware it was collected on.

summary.en: A VLA may over-rely on the end-effector visible in its wrist camera, making transfer to different robot embodiments difficult. Cloak masks the end-effector during training, rendering masks in simulation from known robot geometry without segmentation or generative models. Mask augmentation encourages embodiment-agnostic visual reasoning. The authors train Cloak-VLA on data from one parallel-jaw gripper and collect no data from new embodiments. They report zero-shot transfer to another gripper, another arm, and a five-fingered hand while preserving performance on the source embodiment. The abstract provides no task scores or quantitative transfer measurements.
summary.zh: 视觉语言动作模型可能把腕部相机中占据显著区域的末端执行器当作身体特征，因而难以迁移到未见过的机器人形态。Cloak在训练时用仿真根据已知几何实时生成末端掩码，并增强掩码变化，使模型学习与具体形态无关的视觉推理；不需要分割或生成模型。作者以单一平行夹爪数据训练Cloak-VLA，且不采集新形态数据。论文报告其零样本迁移到另一夹爪、另一机械臂及五指手，同时保留源形态表现。摘要未给出具体任务成绩或迁移性能数值。

items.title: Cloak: Zero-Shot Cross-Embodiment Manipulation by Masking the End-Effector from the VLA

sections.text:
Advanced Air Mobility operations are expected to significantly increase aerial traffic in urban airspace, requiring autonomous traffic management systems to ensure collision-free operations in highly congested environments.

In this paper, we propose a multi-agent coordination framework that uses minimum time-to-reach (TTR) as a unifying metric for priority assignment, temporal separation, and safety filtering. We focus on the problem of coordinating multiple aerial vehicles merging into an air corridor while maintaining safe separation between vehicles.

Vehicles are assigned arrival-consistent priority based on TTR, and target TTR values are used to enforce temporal spacing, which induces spatial separation. A priority-consistent safety filtering layer based on Hamilton-Jacobi reachability value functions promotes collision avoidance while minimally modifying the reference guidance.

Simulation results in a highly congested corridor merging scenario show that the proposed method improves safety, fairness, and efficiency compared to time-optimal guidance and priority-agnostic safety filtering.

summary.en: Congested urban airspace requires coordinating aircraft priorities, arrival timing, and collision avoidance when multiple vehicles merge into a corridor. The proposed framework uses minimum time-to-reach (TTR) for priority assignment, temporal separation, and safety filtering. Arrival-consistent priorities and target TTR values enforce time gaps that induce spatial separation; a Hamilton-Jacobi reachability filter promotes collision avoidance while minimally changing reference guidance. Simulation of a highly congested corridor merge reports improved safety, fairness, and efficiency compared with time-optimal guidance and priority-agnostic safety filtering. The abstract gives no metric values and reports simulation rather than flight experiments.
summary.zh: 城市空域拥挤时，多架飞行器合流需要协调优先级、时间间隔和避碰。论文以最短到达时间TTR为统一度量：按到达一致性分配优先级，用目标TTR安排时间间隔以形成空间分离，再以基于Hamilton-Jacobi可达性的安全过滤器，在尽量少改动参考引导的情况下促进避碰。方法针对多航空器汇入空中走廊的情境。高拥挤合流场景模拟显示，相较时间最优引导和不考虑优先级的安全过滤，所提方法改善安全性、公平性和效率；摘要未提供具体指标数值或实飞验证。

items.title: Time-To-Reach Separation and Safety Filtering for Safe, Fair, and Efficient Multi-Agent Coordination

Existing methods mitigate this covariate shift by collecting additional data where the policy fails or is likely to fail. sections.text:
Policies trained with imitation learning can accumulate errors over time, causing the robot to drift outside the training distribution. Existing methods mitigate this covariate shift by collecting additional data where the policy fails or is likely to fail.

The first places the robot in unsafe conditions and the second requires choosing an appropriate noise distribution to collect new expert demonstrations under that noise.

We propose Policy-Calibrated DAgger, a method that makes use of the properties of recent generative policies to estimate the policy's noise offline by using its own predicted action distribution.

We measure a diffusion policy's spread of predicted actions at observations along the expert trajectory and measure its closed-loop error relative to a recorded trajectory.

To address issues with measuring error in a multimodal action space, we guide the policy towards the trajectory during closed-loop control through partial denoising, and use properties of a diffusion model to unnormalize the measured error as if we did not guide it.

We experiment in a scenario where a robot is tasked to reach an engine lever in a cluttered and narrow environment and show results in a 3D photorealistic simulator and a 2D planar reacher environment.

We show that our method surpasses policies trained with dataset aggregation without noising and matches the performance of the best noise level in hindsight, without requiring a sweep over noise levels.

summary.en: Imitation policies can drift outside their training distribution, while common DAgger remedies require collecting failure-state data or selecting a noise distribution in advance. Policy-Calibrated DAgger estimates policy noise offline from a diffusion policy's predicted action spread along expert observations. Partial denoising guides closed-loop execution, with a correction for measuring error in multimodal action spaces. Tests use an engine-lever reaching task in a photorealistic 3D simulator and a 2D planar environment. The authors report better results than dataset aggregation without noise and performance matching the best noise level in hindsight, without sweeping noise settings. The abstract reports no physical-robot evaluation.
summary.zh: 模仿学习策略会随闭环误差逐渐偏离专家数据分布，常见DAgger缓解方式需在失败状态采集数据或预先选择噪声强度，前者可能不安全，后者要调参。Policy-Calibrated DAgger利用扩散策略在专家轨迹观测处预测动作分布的离散程度，离线估计噪声；再通过部分去噪引导闭环执行，并校正多模态动作空间中的误差度量。作者在发动机拉杆狭窄杂乱场景的逼真三维模拟器和二维平面环境中测试，报告其优于不加噪声的数据聚合策略，并达到事后挑选最佳噪声水平的表现，无需扫描噪声参数。摘要未报告实机实验。

items.title: Policy-Calibrated DAgger: Offline Calibrated Noise Injection for Imitation Learning

items.intro: arXiv:2609.31137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Driving in dense urban traffic is interactive: whether a merge or an unprotected turn succeeds depends on how surrounding agents respond to the ego vehicle. Conventional planners predict first and plan second and, therefore, cannot account for this dependency. Methods that integrate prediction and planning either train both jointly, which introduces task interference, or keep them separate and are restricted to a predefined set of proposals. We present INTERACT: Interactive Planning for Autonomous

sections.text:
Driving in dense urban traffic is interactive: whether a merge or an unprotected turn succeeds depends on how surrounding agents respond to the ego vehicle. Conventional planners predict first and plan second and, therefore, cannot account for this dependency.

Methods that integrate prediction and planning either train both jointly, which introduces task interference, or keep them separate and are restricted to a predefined set of proposals. We present INTERACT: Interactive Planning for Autonomous Driving via Anchor-Conditioned Prediction and Trust-Region Refinement.

Our key insight is that surrounding agents react to the intent a trajectory expresses rather than to its exact realization, so a single reactive prediction stays valid across an entire family of plans. INTERACT therefore decomposes interactive planning into prediction across driving intents and optimization within each intent.

We derive a small set of diverse intents, which we call anchors, from map geometry, query a dedicated ego-conditioned prediction model once per anchor, and refine every anchor with the Cross-Entropy Method under a trust-region penalty that keeps the refined plan close enough to its anchor for the conditioned reaction to still apply.

Prediction thus remains a separate model, avoiding task interference, while conditioning on anchors preserves the dependency. Because each anchor is refined continuously, the final plan is not restricted to the anchor set, yet INTERACT requires only one predictor query per anchor rather than one per candidate plan, with all anchors processed in parallel.

On the nuPlan and interPlan closed-loop benchmarks, INTERACT sets a new state of the art, with the largest gains precisely in the interactive scenarios that motivate the method. The code will be released upon acceptance.

summary.en: In dense traffic, merges and unprotected turns depend on how other agents respond to the ego vehicle, which predict-then-plan systems do not capture. INTERACT derives diverse intent anchors from map geometry, queries an ego-conditioned predictor once per anchor, and continuously refines each plan with the Cross-Entropy Method under a trust-region penalty. This preserves the intent-conditioned reaction while allowing final plans beyond the anchor set; prediction remains separate from planning. On nuPlan and interPlan closed-loop benchmarks, the authors report state-of-the-art results, with the largest gains in interactive scenarios. The abstract gives no scores and describes no real-road vehicle testing.
summary.zh: 密集交通中的并线和无保护转弯取决于周围车辆如何响应自车意图，先预测再规划的流程难以建模这种依赖。INTERACT从地图几何提取少量多样驾驶意图锚点，每个锚点查询一次自车条件化预测模型，再用带信赖域惩罚的交叉熵方法连续优化轨迹，确保周车反应仍适用于该意图。预测与规划保持分离以避免联合训练干扰，最终计划也不局限于离散锚点。作者在nuPlan和interPlan闭环基准报告达到新的最佳表现，提升最大处正是交互性场景；摘要未给出分数，也未报告实车道路测试。

items.title: INTERACT: Interactive Planning for Autonomous Driving via Anchor-Conditioned Prediction and Trust-Region Refinement

Modular reconfigurable robots (MRRs) can achieve such functionalities by docking and rearranging individual units, but most rely on rigid modules that lack structural compliance, resulting in limited capabilities. Continuum robots offer compliance through flexible backbones, yet they cannot self-reconfigure into task-adaptive multi-robot configurations. Here, we introduce an MRR that unifies the advantages of

sections.text:
Robots that can change their morphologies and behaviors for different tasks and environments hold great promise for adaptable, multifunctional systems.

Modular reconfigurable robots (MRRs) can achieve such functionalities by docking and rearranging individual units, but most rely on rigid modules that lack structural compliance, resulting in limited capabilities. Continuum robots offer compliance through flexible backbones, yet they cannot self-reconfigure into task-adaptive multi-robot configurations.

Here, we introduce an MRR that unifies the advantages of both architectures by combining a tensegrity-based compliant body with claw-based connection mechanisms. Each robot can manipulate and locomote independently, and multiple robots can self-reconfigure into different morphologies (e.g., chains, loops, branches) for cooperative manipulation and locomotion.

We demonstrate the robots' capability across diverse tasks and environments, including coordinated object manipulation and transport, multimodal locomotion, and loco-manipulation in real-world scenarios.

These results lay a foundation for adaptable and multifunctional robotic collectives, with broad potential applications in manufacturing, space exploration, and search-and-rescue operations.

summary.en: Modular robots can reconfigure by docking units but are often rigid, while continuum robots are compliant but cannot self-reconfigure into cooperative multi-robot forms. The paper introduces a modular reconfigurable robot combining a compliant tensegrity body with claw-based connectors. Individual robots locomote and manipulate independently; multiple units self-reconfigure into chains, loops, or branches for cooperative tasks. Demonstrations include coordinated object manipulation and transport, multimodal locomotion, and real-world loco-manipulation. The abstract reports prototype demonstrations but no quantitative measures or deployment scale. Manufacturing, space exploration, and search and rescue are described as potential applications, not established deployments.
summary.zh: 可重构模块机器人通常依靠刚性单元，柔顺性不足；连续体机器人虽柔软，却不能自主组合成任务适配的多机器人形态。论文提出以张拉整体柔顺机身和爪式连接机构结合两者优势的模块机器人：单体可独立移动和操作，多台可自重构为链、环、分支等形态，协同搬运或移动。作者在多种任务和环境中展示协调物体操作与运输、多模态运动，以及真实场景中的移动操作。摘要展示了机器人原型与实地行为，但未提供量化指标或制造部署规模；制造、太空及搜救仅被提出为潜在应用方向。

items.title: Tensegrity Continuum Robots Enable Task-Adaptive Morphologies for Cooperative Behaviors

items.intro: arXiv:2609.30523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-powered multi-robot systems are vulnerable to semantic manipulation: an accepted false world-state claim can trigger a fleet-wide behavioral cascade, causing unnecessary replanning, increased path costs, congestion, or apparent mission infeasibility. Conditioning on a successful manipulation, we propose an active verification framework that contains its downstream effects before they propagate across the fleet. A dedicated verification module generates a structured Verify-Adapt-Hold plan: selected robots inspect consequential regions, a limited subset

sections.text:
Large language model (LLM)-powered multi-robot systems are vulnerable to semantic manipulation: an accepted false world-state claim can trigger a fleet-wide behavioral cascade, causing unnecessary replanning, increased path costs, congestion, or apparent mission infeasibility.

Conditioning on a successful manipulation, we propose an active verification framework that contains its downstream effects before they propagate across the fleet.

A dedicated verification module generates a structured Verify-Adapt-Hold plan: selected robots inspect consequential regions, a limited subset provisionally adapts when necessary, and the remaining robots retain their trusted plans.

We evaluate the framework in a multi-robot transportation environment using injected false obstacle claims across different impacts and team sizes. Evaluation measures cascade containment, Sum-of-Costs, makespan, and coverage ratio.

Results show that treating post-compromise verification as a team-level planning problem, rather than a binary trust decision, effectively limits the cascading physical consequences of semantic manipulation.

summary.en: False world-state claims can trigger cascading replanning in LLM-powered robot fleets. Assuming a manipulation has succeeded, the paper proposes active verification through a Verify-Adapt-Hold plan: selected robots inspect key regions, a limited subset adapts if needed, and others retain trusted plans. Tests inject false obstacle claims of varying impact and team size in a multi-robot transport environment, measuring containment, cost, makespan, and coverage. Results indicate team-level verification limits physical cascades; numerical effect sizes are not given.
summary.zh: 由大语言模型驱动的多机器人系统若接受虚假的世界状态声明，可能引发全队级级联行为，导致重规划、路径代价上升、拥堵或任务看似不可行。针对操纵已成功发生的情况，作者提出主动验证框架，生成“验证—适应—保持”团队计划：选定机器人检查关键区域，必要时只让有限子集暂时调整，其余机器人保留可信计划。研究在多机器人运输环境中注入不同影响程度的虚假障碍声明，并以级联遏制、总代价、完工时间和覆盖率评估。结果表明将事后验证视为团队规划问题可限制级联物理后果；摘要未给量化改善幅度。

items.title: Containing Behavioral Cascades from Manipulated Claims in LLM-Powered Multi-Robot Systems

Many conventional navigation policies learn a single normative behavior, either through reinforcement learning against a fixed reward function or imitation of human demonstrations, exposing no interface for adjusting that conduct at runtime. We present a diffusion-based navigation framework whose social behavior can be tuned at deployment: a desired style is specified, such

sections.text:
Beyond collision avoidance, socially competent robot navigation requires adherence to implicit social conventions that vary across contexts, cultures, and deployment requirements.

Many conventional navigation policies learn a single normative behavior, either through reinforcement learning against a fixed reward function or imitation of human demonstrations, exposing no interface for adjusting that conduct at runtime.

We present a diffusion-based navigation framework whose social behavior can be tuned at deployment: a desired style is specified, such as how closely the robot passes, which side it yields to, or how much it defers to groups, and the planner adapts accordingly.

Continuous style axes can be followed independently or composed, spanning a behavioral space rather than discrete, primitive-based specifications. A feasibility projection layer separates learned social behavior from kinematic feasibility and collision avoidance.

A single-axis sweep illustrates a tradeoff curve that strictly dominates the evaluated fixed-behavior baseline configurations, and stylistic differences are replicated in real-world demonstrations.

summary.en: SoGuDiff makes socially guided navigation adjustable at runtime, addressing policies that encode only one fixed norm. Users specify continuous styles such as passing distance, yielding side, or deference to groups, and can compose axes. A feasibility projection separates learned behavior from kinematic and collision constraints. A single-axis sweep yields a trade-off curve that strictly dominates evaluated fixed-behavior baselines, while real-world demonstrations reproduce stylistic differences. The abstract gives no user-study details or quantitative safety metrics.
summary.zh: 常见导航策略把社会规范固定在训练奖励或人类示范中，部署时无法按场景调整机器人让行和通行风格。SoGuDiff提出扩散式导航框架，可在运行阶段指定连续风格轴，例如通过他人时的距离、让行方向或对群体的退让程度，也可组合不同轴形成行为空间。可行性投影层将学习到的社会行为与运动学可行性及避碰分开处理。单轴扫描得到的权衡曲线严格支配所测固定行为基线配置，真实世界演示也复现了风格差异。结果支持可调行为展示，但摘要未说明参与者研究、具体场景覆盖或量化安全指标。

items.title: SoGuDiff: Socially Guided Diffusion for Steerable, Norm-Grounded Robot Navigation

items.intro: arXiv:2609.31439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Policy learning and compliant control offer a promising route to reliable autonomous assembly under pose errors and contact uncertainty. However, combining them does not ensure coordination: the policy may continue pushing against contact while the controller yields, producing sustained loading with limited progress. To address this problem, we propose LeCo (Leverage Compliance), a policy-admittance learning framework that guides a visual policy through execution-time interaction under fixed admittance. A multirate feedback mechanism aggregates high-rate

sections.text:
Policy learning and compliant control offer a promising route to reliable autonomous assembly under pose errors and contact uncertainty. However, combining them does not ensure coordination: the policy may continue pushing against contact while the controller yields, producing sustained loading with limited progress.

To address this problem, we propose LeCo (Leverage Compliance), a policy-admittance learning framework that guides a visual policy through execution-time interaction under fixed admittance. A multirate feedback mechanism aggregates high-rate contact-interaction records into policy-transition rewards.

An integrated conflict cost then characterizes sustained policy-loading/controller-unloading opposition, while a directional high-force tail cost captures continued-loading events within a transition. Together with task completion, these costs encourage the policy to leverage compliance with less unproductive loading.

We evaluate LeCo on four real connector-assembly tasks, obtaining an aggregate success rate of 94%.Across tasks, mean successful-trial resultant-force and torque peaks decrease by approximately 30% and 64% relative to the comparison baseline.

Reward ablation further shows that adding conflict shaping reduces median successful-trial contact-conditioned conflict density by approximately 53%.These results support learning to leverage fixed compliance by turning multirate policy-admittance interaction into complementary reward signals for effective, lower-load insertion.

summary.en: LeCo addresses insertion policies that keep pushing while an admittance controller yields. It converts high-rate contact records into rewards, including a conflict cost for opposing policy and controller actions and a high-force tail cost for continued loading. Across four real connector-assembly tasks, aggregate success is 94%. Successful-trial peak resultant force and torque fall about 30% and 64% versus the baseline. An ablation reports roughly 53% lower median contact-conditioned conflict density when conflict shaping is added.
summary.zh: 在插接装配中，视觉策略可能持续对抗接触，而顺应控制器不断退让，形成持续受力却进展有限的冲突。LeCo通过固定导纳下的执行期交互引导视觉策略，把高速接触记录汇总成策略转移奖励；冲突代价衡量策略加载与控制器卸载的持续对抗，定向高力尾部代价惩罚持续加载事件，并结合任务完成信号训练。四项真实连接器装配任务的总体成功率为94%；相较基线，成功试验的合力峰值和力矩峰值分别约降30%和64%。奖励消融显示加入冲突塑形后，成功试验的接触条件冲突密度中位数约降53%。

items.title: Learning to Leverage Compliance: A Policy-Admittance Learning Framework for Robotic Insertion

items.intro: arXiv:2603.06480v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) enables robots to follow natural-language instructions in visually grounded environments, serving as a key capability for embodied robotic systems. Recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong navigation performance, but their high computational cost introduces latency that limits real-time deployment. We propose a training-free spatio-temporal vision token pruning framework tailored to VLA-based VLN. We apply spatial token selection to the current view, alongside spatio-temporal compression for historical memories, enabling efficient long-horizon

sections.text:
Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) enables robots to follow natural-language instructions in visually grounded environments, serving as a key capability for embodied robotic systems. Recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong navigation performance, but their high computational cost introduces latency that limits real-time deployment.

We propose a training-free spatio-temporal vision token pruning framework tailored to VLA-based VLN. We apply spatial token selection to the current view, alongside spatio-temporal compression for historical memories, enabling efficient long-horizon inference while reducing redundant computation.

Leveraging attention-based token importance and query-guided spatio-temporal filtering, the proposed approach preserves navigation-relevant information without retraining or modifying pretrained models, allowing plug-and-play integration into existing VLA systems.

Through experiments on standard VLN benchmarks, we confirm that our method significantly outperforms existing pruning strategies. It successfully preserves superior navigation accuracy under extreme pruning scenarios, all while maintaining the highly competitive inference efficiency.

Real-world deployment on a Unitree Go2 quadruped robot further validates reliable and low-latency instruction-following navigation under practical robotic constraints. We hope this work helps bridge the gap between large-scale multimodal modeling and efficient, real-time embodied deployment in robotic navigation systems.

Project Page: https://wqtwjt1996.github.io/publications/2026-vln.html

summary.en: This training-free method prunes current-view spatial tokens and compresses historical visual memory for VLA-based navigation, using attention importance and query-guided filtering without changing pretrained models. On standard VLN benchmarks, it outperforms existing pruning strategies and retains navigation accuracy under extreme pruning with competitive inference efficiency. Deployment on a Unitree Go2 demonstrates low-latency instruction following on a physical robot. The abstract gives no pruning ratios or accuracy values.
summary.zh: 视觉语言导航模型计算成本高、历史视觉记忆冗余，限制了实时部署。论文提出无需训练的时空视觉token剪枝框架：筛选当前视图空间token，并压缩历史记忆中的时空信息，结合注意力重要性和查询引导过滤减少重复计算，同时不改动预训练模型。标准导航基准实验中，作者报告其显著优于既有剪枝策略，在极端剪枝下仍保持较高导航准确率和有竞争力的推理效率；Unitree Go2四足机器人的真实部署展示低延迟指令跟随。摘要未给出具体剪枝比例或准确率数字。

items.title: History-Conditioned Spatio-Temporal Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language Navigation

items.intro: arXiv:2609.31606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning robot policies for tasks with sparse success signals is challenging when completion depends on coordinated actions, precise contact outcomes, or satisfying several conditions together. Intricate physical interactions with the world further complicate these requirements. Prior work using conventional reward shaping mechanisms provides dense feedback but local progress might not translate into eventual task completion. We present Signal Temporal Logic-guided Stein Variational Policy Gradient (STL-SVPG), a population-based method that uses smooth STL robustness

sections.text:
Learning robot policies for tasks with sparse success signals is challenging when completion depends on coordinated actions, precise contact outcomes, or satisfying several conditions together. Intricate physical interactions with the world further complicate these requirements.

Prior work using conventional reward shaping mechanisms provides dense feedback but local progress might not translate into eventual task completion. We present Signal Temporal Logic-guided Stein Variational Policy Gradient (STL-SVPG), a population-based method that uses smooth STL robustness as a trajectory-level training objective.

Differentiating this objective through the dynamics assigns credit to policy actions according to their effect on the complete task specification, rather than local progress alone.

We evaluate the approach on six quadcopter and manipulator tasks that involves event-triggered responses, strictly ordered behavior, responses within specified deadlines, and physical interaction with the world. STL-SVPG achieves the highest mean success rate among the compared methods on five of six benchmarks.

Simulation-trained policies trained in simulation transfer temporal and contact task behavior to the real world.

summary.en: STL-SVPG addresses sparse-success robot tasks with smooth Signal Temporal Logic robustness as a trajectory-level objective, assigning action credit according to the complete task specification. Across six quadcopter and manipulator tasks involving event triggers, ordering, deadlines, and physical interaction, it achieves the highest mean success on five benchmarks. Simulation-trained policies transfer temporal and contact behaviors to the real world. The abstract provides no task-specific figures.
summary.zh: 当任务成功信号稀疏且依赖有序动作、限时响应或精确接触时，局部奖励进展未必带来整体完成。STL-SVPG以信号时序逻辑的平滑鲁棒度作为轨迹级训练目标，并通过动力学反向传播，将信用分配给影响完整任务规格的策略动作；方法采用群体式Stein变分策略梯度。作者在六项四旋翼和机械臂任务中比较，任务包含事件触发、严格顺序、截止时间和物理交互，报告STL-SVPG在六项中的五项取得最高平均成功率。仿真训练策略还将时序和接触任务行为迁移到真实世界；摘要没有报告各任务数值。

items.title: Learning Robot Policies from Sparse Success Signals via STL-Guided Stein Variational Policy Gradient

In this context, Augmented Reality (AR) presents itself as a fundamental enabling technology, capable of both displaying information to the operator and gathering spatial data about the surrounding environment. This thesis presents the development of a sensor streaming framework that connects the Magic Leap

sections.text:
In recent years, Human-Robot Collaboration (HRC) has taken on a central role in Industry 4.0 and collaborative robotics, demanding communication channels that are increasingly bidirectional, intuitive, and efficient.

In this context, Augmented Reality (AR) presents itself as a fundamental enabling technology, capable of both displaying information to the operator and gathering spatial data about the surrounding environment.

This thesis presents the development of a sensor streaming framework that connects the Magic Leap 2 AR headset with the ROS 2 (Robot Operating System) ecosystem.

Using the Unity development environment and the ROSTCP-Connector package, an on-board application for the headset was developed, capable of acquiring real-time data from the integrated sensors (pose tracking, cameras, and environmental sensors) and publishing it to dedicated ROS 2 topics.

In order to test the accuracy, latency, and robustness of the generated data stream, the framework was validated using SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) algorithms known in the literature.

The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed architecture ensures stable data transmission, laying the groundwork for safe real-time interaction and shared spatial awareness, and opening up new perspectives for the control and supervision of robotic systems in complex HRC scenarios.

summary.en: Human-robot collaboration needs interfaces that both present information to operators and stream spatial sensor data to robot software. This thesis develops a framework connecting a Magic Leap 2 headset with ROS 2. A Unity application using ROSTCP-Connector acquires pose tracking, camera, and environmental sensor data and publishes it to dedicated ROS 2 topics. The authors validate accuracy, latency, and robustness of the stream using established SLAM algorithms. Experimental results report stable data transmission and describe the framework as groundwork for real-time interaction and shared spatial awareness. The abstract provides no numerical accuracy or latency results and no specific collaboration-task evaluation.
summary.zh: 人机协作需要增强现实既向操作者呈现信息，也将设备空间传感数据接入机器人系统。该论文开发Magic Leap 2与ROS 2之间的传感流框架，使用Unity和ROSTCP-Connector构建头显应用，采集位姿跟踪、相机及环境传感器数据并发布到ROS 2话题。作者以文献中的SLAM算法验证数据流的准确性、延迟和稳定性，实验结果报告传输稳定，为实时交互和共享空间感知奠定基础。摘要未给出精度、延迟、鲁棒性数值或具体协作任务，因此结论主要是框架实现及其SLAM验证。

items.title: Augmented Reality Interfaces for Human-Robot Collaboration: Development of a ROS 2-Based Sensor Streaming Framework and Validation via SLAM Algorithms

items.intro: arXiv:2609.31185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Effective wind gust rejection and stable hovering are critical for the outdoor operation of autonomous drones. However, existing gust rejection methods are primarily reactive, inferring the disturbance from the resulting motion or measuring it at the airframe. Either way, the wind has already begun to act before it can be compensated. In this work, we anticipate the gust instead by measuring the wind ahead of the drone with a low-cost, low-weight pitot-static sensor

sections.text:
Effective wind gust rejection and stable hovering are critical for the outdoor operation of autonomous drones. However, existing gust rejection methods are primarily reactive, inferring the disturbance from the resulting motion or measuring it at the airframe. Either way, the wind has already begun to act before it can be compensated.

In this work, we anticipate the gust instead by measuring the wind ahead of the drone with a low-cost, low-weight pitot-static sensor mounted on a boom. The resulting wind preview is incorporated into a nonlinear model predictive controller (MPC), which optimizes the drone motion while anticipating wind disturbances.

A longer boom offers more preview time but adds inertia and degrades flight performance. We characterize this trade-off in simulation and show that the optimal preview distance is not a fixed property of the platform, but shifts with the wind speed and with how quickly the drone can respond.

Indoor hardware experiments confirm the trend and show that the proposed controller substantially improves hover performance against a PX4 baseline and an otherwise identical wind-unaware MPC.

Outdoor experiments show that the error along the wind direction is reduced by 54 percent with respect to the baseline, demonstrating that a single wind-aligned sensor can significantly improve hovering performance.

summary.en: A forward-boom pitot-static sensor previews wind for a nonlinear model-predictive controller, instead of reacting after gusts affect the drone. Longer booms add preview time but also inertia. Simulations show the best distance depends on wind speed and vehicle response. Indoor hardware confirms this trend and reports better hovering than PX4 and wind-unaware MPC baselines. Outdoors, along-wind error falls 54% relative to the baseline.
summary.zh: 无人机常用的阵风抑制方法要么从机体运动反推风扰，要么在机身测风，扰动已开始作用后才响应。该方法将低成本轻量皮托静压传感器置于机体前方支杆上，预先测风并输入非线性模型预测控制器。较长支杆可增加预览时间，却会增加惯量、影响飞行；模拟分析显示最佳预览距离随风速和无人机响应速度变化，而非固定平台参数。室内硬件实验确认该趋势并报告悬停优于PX4基线和不使用风预览的MPC；户外实验中，沿风方向误差较基线降低54%。

items.title: Onboard Wind-Preview Model Predictive Control Using Pitot-Static Sensing for Multirotor UAVs

Reactive synthesis can generate such supervisors with formal guarantees, but deployment requires more than proving a Generalized Reactivity (1) (GR(1)) specification realizable. Designers must encode failure-prone capabilities, choose liveness assumptions that match retry intent, audit strategies, and translate them into robot software. We present an open-source pipeline for Robot Operating System (ROS) 2 Flexible Behavior Engine (FlexBE) supervisors that

sections.text:
High-level robotic supervisors coordinate capabilities whose reported outcomes determine the robot's next action. Reactive synthesis can generate such supervisors with formal guarantees, but deployment requires more than proving a Generalized Reactivity （1） (GR（1）) specification realizable.

Designers must encode failure-prone capabilities, choose liveness assumptions that match retry intent, audit strategies, and translate them into robot software.

We present an open-source pipeline for Robot Operating System (ROS) 2 Flexible Behavior Engine (FlexBE) supervisors that generates capability-based GR（1） specifications, analyzes assumptions before synthesis, audits strategies, reduces states with a behavior-preservation proof, and emits executable state machines.

Across four case studies (six comparisons), including hardware on two quadcopter platforms, we compare enumerated and one-hot encodings and two liveness formulations. Under the tested backend, enumerated encoding usually synthesizes faster, although fewer propositions do not reliably predict smaller controllers or lower symbolic cost.

System-Goal without pending memory is the only liveness treatment confirmed to yield executable controllers under both encodings across the reported grid; Fair-Outcome can permit realizable cycles without designer-intended completion.

For this backend and model, we recommend enumerated encoding with System-Goal and auditing every realized strategy, since proposition count and realizability do not measure deployability.

The auditor is sound and complete for four structural defect classes (protocol violations, deadlocks, bounded-failure violations, goal-unreachable traps) but is not a general liveness verifier, and the reduction preserves capability-level behavior.

Together, these stages narrow the gap between formal realizability and controllers that pass protocol and structural-progress checks.

summary.en: The paper presents a ROS 2 FlexBE pipeline that generates GR(1) specifications, analyzes assumptions, audits strategies, reduces states with a behavior-preservation proof, and emits state machines. Four case studies with six comparisons, including two quadcopter platforms, find enumerated encoding usually synthesizes faster under the tested backend. Only System-Goal without pending memory is confirmed to yield executable controllers under both encodings. The auditor covers four structural defect classes but is not a general liveness verifier; recommendations are specific to this backend and model.
summary.zh: 形式化规范可实现不保证监督器可部署：能力失败、活性假设和策略结构都可能造成协议缺陷或无法完成目标。论文提出ROS 2 FlexBE流水线，从能力生成GR(1)规格、分析假设、审计策略、在行为保持证明下压缩状态并输出状态机。四个案例、六组比较（含两种四旋翼硬件）显示，所测后端中枚举编码通常综合更快；仅System-Goal无待处理记忆的活性处理在两种编码下均确认可生成可执行控制器。审计器针对四类结构缺陷可靠且完备，但不是通用活性验证器；建议限于该后端和模型。

items.title: Realizability Is Not Enough: Encoding, Liveness, and Auditing of Synthesized Robot Supervisors

items.intro: arXiv:2609.31232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bringing an aerial robotics method from simulation to flight should not require rebuilding a mature autopilot or adding a companion computer. Cybflight is an open-source embedded Rust research autopilot whose typed, replaceable interfaces connect hardware access, perception, state estimation, trajectory planning, and control. This modular development and compile-time optimization workflow is demonstrated with replaceable Rust implementations of model predictive contour-tracking control (MPCTC) and incremental nonlinear dynamic inversion (INDI) running on one STM32H743 without

sections.text:
Bringing an aerial robotics method from simulation to flight should not require rebuilding a mature autopilot or adding a companion computer. Cybflight is an open-source embedded Rust research autopilot whose typed, replaceable interfaces connect hardware access, perception, state estimation, trajectory planning, and control.

This modular development and compile-time optimization workflow is demonstrated with replaceable Rust implementations of model predictive contour-tracking control (MPCTC) and incremental nonlinear dynamic inversion (INDI) running on one STM32H743 without a companion computer.

Using this configuration, the vehicle reaches 12.38 m/s during indoor flight, while an outdoor flight using global navigation satellite system (GNSS) position updates reaches 31.4 m/s.

These flights show that running demanding estimation and nonlinear control entirely on a flight-controller microcontroller need not come at the expense of a modular autopilot structure.

summary.en: Taking aerial-robotics methods from simulation to flight can require rebuilding a mature autopilot or adding a companion computer. Cybflight is an open-source embedded Rust research autopilot with typed, replaceable interfaces for hardware, perception, state estimation, planning, and control. The paper demonstrates model-predictive contour tracking and incremental nonlinear dynamic inversion on one STM32H743, without a companion computer. With this configuration, the vehicle reaches 12.38 m/s in indoor flight and 31.4 m/s in an outdoor flight using GNSS position updates. These demonstrations show onboard execution on a flight-controller microcontroller; the abstract gives no comparative performance baseline.
summary.zh: 将空中机器人研究方法从仿真带到飞行，通常要改造成熟自动驾驶仪或增加伴随计算机。Cybflight是开源嵌入式Rust研究自动驾驶仪，以可替换、带类型接口连接硬件、感知、状态估计、轨迹规划和控制。论文展示在单块STM32H743上运行可替换的模型预测轮廓跟踪控制与增量非线性动态逆控制，无需伴随计算机。该配置在室内飞行达到12.38米/秒；使用GNSS位置更新的户外飞行达到31.4米/秒。作者据此说明复杂估计和非线性控制可在飞控微控制器运行并保持模块化结构，摘要未提供对照性能。

items.title: Cybflight: An Embedded Rust Autopilot for Aerial Robotics Research

items.intro: arXiv:2607.02222v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Vision-Language Navigation has increasingly emphasized high-level instruction reasoning, memory, global map construction, and instruction decomposition, while the low-level action representation remains comparatively underexplored. We propose CoFL-S, a low-level vision-language-action framework that predicts a language-conditioned flow field over the robot's local visible sector and generates continuous trajectories by rolling out the predicted field. To train this low-level representation, we convert each VLN-CE episode, originally a whole-episode instruction paired with an action sequence, into frame-level

sections.text:
Vision-Language Navigation has increasingly emphasized high-level instruction reasoning, memory, global map construction, and instruction decomposition, while the low-level action representation remains comparatively underexplored.

We propose CoFL-S, a low-level vision-language-action framework that predicts a language-conditioned flow field over the robot's local visible sector and generates continuous trajectories by rolling out the predicted field.

To train this low-level representation, we convert each VLN-CE episode, originally a whole-episode instruction paired with an action sequence, into frame-level local supervision with aligned sub-instructions and matched action, trajectory, and dense flow-field targets.

For evaluation, we introduce a continuous-time Habitat benchmark that isolates low-level action interfaces from instruction decomposition and executes all methods through a shared velocity-command controller, enabling decomposition-independent closed-loop comparison across different planner frequencies rather than fixed discrete forward-and-turn transitions in VLN-CE.

Under matched encoders and training settings, CoFL-S consistently outperforms baselines across planner frequencies in the continuous-time Habitat benchmark, and zero-shot real-world closed-loop deployment further shows its advantage over the evaluated baselines beyond simulation. See the project website at https://github.com/ut-dragon-lab/CoFL

summary.en: CoFL-S predicts a language-conditioned flow field over the robot's visible sector and rolls it out into continuous trajectories. Training creates frame-level local supervision from full-episode instructions and actions. A continuous-time Habitat benchmark compares low-level interfaces across planner frequencies using a shared velocity controller. With matched encoders and training, CoFL-S outperforms baselines across frequencies. Zero-shot real-world closed-loop deployment also reports an advantage beyond simulation, though no numerical scores are given.
summary.zh: 视觉语言导航研究多聚焦高层指令推理，低层动作表示相对不足。CoFL-S预测机器人局部可见扇区上的语言条件流场，并沿流场展开为连续轨迹；训练时把完整导航任务转成逐帧局部监督，配对局部指令、动作、轨迹和稠密流场目标。作者另构建连续时间Habitat基准，通过统一速度控制器比较不同规划频率下的闭环低层接口，避免指令分解差异。相同编码器和训练设置下，CoFL-S在该基准多个频率均优于基线；零样本真实机器人闭环部署也报告优于所比较方法，体现超出仿真的结果，但摘要未提供量化成绩。

items.title: CoFL-S: Spatially Queryable Sector Flow Fields for Local Language-Conditioned Navigation

Deploying such systems in construction, however, requires a precise inventory of worker activities and the capabilities needed to execute them. We present TARCAT, an occupation-grounded taxonomy derived from 91 O*NET task statements across seven high-employment construction occupations and 30 instructional videos. TARCAT defines 41 primitives spanning intellectual, social, and physical categories and provides a mechanism for composing

sections.text:
Recent vision-language-action models offer a path toward robots with broader capabilities than conventional task-specific systems. Deploying such systems in construction, however, requires a precise inventory of worker activities and the capabilities needed to execute them.

We present TARCAT, an occupation-grounded taxonomy derived from 91 O*NET task statements across seven high-employment construction occupations and 30 instructional videos. TARCAT defines 41 primitives spanning intellectual, social, and physical categories and provides a mechanism for composing parameterized primitive sequences into reusable skills.

This human-interpretable vocabulary supports the specification of robot requirements and enables coding agents to retrieve and extend skill libraries for task execution. We also demonstrate selected primitives on a DOBOT CR3 arm with a CRAFT hand.

TARCAT thus provides a common vocabulary for analyzing construction work and developing general-purpose construction robots. Annotations are available at https://github.com/AICPS/TARCAT-Taxonomy.

summary.en: Deploying vision-language-action models in construction requires an inventory of worker activities and the capabilities robots need. TARCAT derives an occupation-grounded taxonomy from 91 O*NET task statements across seven high-employment construction occupations and 30 instructional videos. It defines 41 intellectual, social, and physical primitives and supports composing parameterized sequences into reusable skills. The human-interpretable vocabulary is intended to specify robot requirements and help coding agents retrieve or extend skill libraries. Selected primitives are demonstrated on a DOBOT CR3 arm with a CRAFT hand. The abstract reports taxonomy construction and demonstrations, not task coverage rates, success statistics, or full construction-site validation.
summary.zh: 将视觉语言动作模型用于施工机器人，需要先系统描述工人活动及执行能力。TARCAT依据七类高就业施工职业的91条O*NET任务陈述和30段教学视频，构建面向职业活动的分类体系，定义41项认知、社交和身体操作原语，并支持组合带参数的原语序列形成可复用技能。该人类可读词汇旨在帮助明确机器人需求，也可供编码代理检索和扩展技能库。作者在DOBOT CR3机械臂和CRAFT手上演示了部分原语。摘要提供分类体系和选定原语展示，但没有报告任务覆盖率、机器人成功率或完整施工现场验证。

items.title: A Taxonomy of Construction Task Activities for Robot Workers

items.intro: arXiv:2609.31386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Load-adaptive gravity balancing mechanisms (LA-GBMs) can accommodate various loading conditions by passively changing their characteristics in response to payload variations. However, their design is difficult because both the desired mechanism motion and static equilibrium under variable payloads must be satisfied simultaneously. This study proposes a general design methodology for LA-GBMs that does not depend on specific mechanism architectures or mechanical elements. The necessary conditions for the potential fields of LA-GBMs are formulated, and

sections.text:
Load-adaptive gravity balancing mechanisms (LA-GBMs) can accommodate various loading conditions by passively changing their characteristics in response to payload variations. However, their design is difficult because both the desired mechanism motion and static equilibrium under variable payloads must be satisfied simultaneously.

This study proposes a general design methodology for LA-GBMs that does not depend on specific mechanism architectures or mechanical elements.

The necessary conditions for the potential fields of LA-GBMs are formulated, and two general forms are derived: an affine form representing the effect of payload mass and a factorized form representing state transitions associated with load adaptation and gravity balancing.

These forms are then provided to generative AI as design requirements to generate candidate potential functions. The generated functions are analytically verified in terms of their conformity to the two general forms and the conditions required for valid LA-GBMs.

Furthermore, the obtained potential functions are decomposed into individual terms, and an example of a method for constructing an LA-GBM by combining springs, counterweights, and function-generating linkage mechanisms is presented.

By using potential functions as an intermediate representation, the proposed framework enables the generation of LA-GBM design candidates without prescribing a mechanism architecture in advance. Mechanical realizability and manufacturability of the generated potential fields remain important issues for future work.

summary.en: Load-adaptive gravity-balancing mechanisms must accommodate changing payloads while satisfying desired motion and static equilibrium, complicating design. The study proposes an architecture-independent methodology, derives necessary potential-field conditions, and formulates affine and factorized forms for payload effects and load-adaptation transitions. These forms become requirements for generative AI to produce candidate potential functions, which are then analytically checked against the conditions. The authors show how to decompose a candidate into terms implemented with springs, counterweights, and function-generating linkages. They explicitly identify mechanical realizability and manufacturability as future issues; the abstract reports no physical mechanism validation.
summary.zh: 负载自适应重力平衡机构需在负载变化时被动改变特性，同时满足期望运动和静力平衡，设计难以兼顾。研究提出不绑定特定机构或机械元件的通用方法，推导此类机构势场的必要条件，并得到表示负载质量影响的仿射形式和表示载荷适应、重力平衡状态转换的因子形式。作者将这些形式作为约束交给生成式人工智能产生候选势函数，再解析检验其形式与有效性条件，并展示如何分解后用弹簧、配重和连杆机构构造实例。论文明确指出生成势场的机械可实现性和可制造性仍待解决，未报告实体机构验证。

items.title: Modeling and Generative-AI-Based Design of Load-Adaptive Gravity Balancing Mechanisms

Yet, the current VLA landscape remains fragmented and exploratory. Although many groups have proposed their own VLA models, inconsistencies in training protocols and evaluation settings make it difficult to identify which design choices truly matter. To bring structure to this evolving space, we reexamine the VLA design space under

sections.text:
Following the rise of large foundation models, Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) emerged, leveraging strong visual and language understanding from Vision-Language Models for general-purpose policy learning. Yet, the current VLA landscape remains fragmented and exploratory.

Although many groups have proposed their own VLA models, inconsistencies in training protocols and evaluation settings make it difficult to identify which design choices truly matter. To bring structure to this evolving space, we reexamine the VLA design space under a unified framework and evaluation setup.

Starting from a simple VLA baseline similar to RT-2, which is the origin of VLA, we systematically dissect design choices along three dimensions: foundational components, perception essentials, and action modeling perspectives. From this study, we distill 12 key findings that together form a practical recipe for building strong VLA models.

The outcome of this exploration is a simple yet effective model, VLANeXt. It outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on the LIBERO and LIBERO-plus benchmarks and demonstrates strong performance in real-world experiments. Beyond identifying the core recipe, we further ask how far these design principles extend to the emerging paradigms in VLAs.

We thus expand VLANeXt along several emerging directions, including model scaling, latent-action pretraining, latent predictive representation learning, and world action modeling. These studies give rise to the VLANeXt family, spanning compact and scaled VLA variants, latent-action models, JEPA-style predictive models, and World Action Models.

Our results show that the core recipe provides a strong foundation across different model scales and emerging paradigms.

summary.en: The paper studies VLA design under a unified training and evaluation setup, covering foundational components, perception, and action modeling. It distills 12 findings into a recipe and the VLANeXt model, which reportedly outperforms prior methods on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus and performs strongly in real-world experiments; scores are not given. The recipe is extended to scaling, latent-action pretraining, predictive representations, and world-action modeling, producing several model variants. The authors report it provides a strong foundation across the paradigms studied.
summary.zh: 视觉语言动作模型研究的训练和评测设置不一，设计选择难以比较。论文在统一框架下从基础组件、感知和动作建模拆解VLA设计，总结12项经验并形成VLANeXt。作者报告其在LIBERO和LIBERO-Plus超过已有方法，且真实实验表现良好，但摘要未给分数。研究再将配方扩展到模型规模、潜在动作预训练、潜在预测表示和世界动作建模，形成多类VLA、潜在动作、JEPA式预测及世界动作模型。作者报告该配方在所研究范式中均提供了良好基础。

items.title: VLANeXt Family: A Systematic Study of VLA Models from Core Recipes to Emerging Paradigms
